Arabists differed about the nominative of the male and the accusative of the slave. Some grammarians of Basra said about the meaning of that it is as if he said: What you have missed is the mention of your Lord's mercy on His slave, and the slave is made accusative by mercy as you say: He mentioned Zaid's beating of Amr. Some grammarians of Kufa said: The male is raised by Ka Ha Ya Ain Sad, and if you wish you can imply this is the mention of your Lord's mercy. He said: The meaning is that your Lord mentioned His slave with His mercy, advancing and delaying.

The correct statement in my opinion is to say: The male is raised by an omitted pronoun, which is this, as He did in other surahs, such as the statement of God, A declaration of immunity from God and His Messenger, and His statement, A surah We have sent down, and the like. The servant is in the accusative case because of mercy, and Zachariah is in the accusative case because it is a statement about the servant, so the interpretation of the statement is: This is a mention of the mercy of your Lord to His servant Zachariah.

They said: It is only appropriate for something like this to be a connection, if it is not disconnected from what it is connected to, like His statement, A support that will support me.
The more correct of the two readings in my opinion is the reading of the one who reads it with the two letters raised as a connection to the Surat Maryam: 6

, my Lord, pleasing. guardian, because the guardian is indefinite, and that Zachariah only asked his Lord to grant him a guardian who would have this description, as was narrated from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, not that he asked Him for a guardian, then he informed that if He granted him that, this would be his description, because if that were the case, that would be from Zachariah entering into the knowledge of the unseen which God has concealed from His creation. , O Lord, pleasing, means: And make, O Lord, the guardian whom You grant me pleasing, pleasing to You and to Your servants with his pleasure in religion, character, and morals.
And pleasing is a verbal noun inflected from the object of the verb.

x: God Almighty says: So his Lord responded to him and said to him: O Zachariah, indeed We give you good tidings of Our grant to you of a boy whose name will be John. Qatada used to say: God named him John because He brought him back to life through faith.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his saying, O Zachariah, indeed We give you good tidings of a boy whose name will be John, a servant whom God brought to life for faith. And his saying,
h
We have not made for him before any namesake
, the people of interpretation differed in their interpretation of that.

x: Some of them said: Its meaning is that no barren woman has ever given birth to anyone like him.
Who said that?

c: Ali told me, he said: Abdullah told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his saying to Yahya,
h
We have not made for him a namesake before
, means: barren women have never given birth to a child like him.

x: Others said: Rather, its meaning is: We did not make for him an example before him.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Al-Muthanna told us: Abu Al-Rabi’ told us: Salim bin Qutaybah told us: Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Al-Hakam, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement,
h
We have not made for Him any namesake before
, he said: any similar.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement,
h
We have not made for him before any namesake
, he said: An example.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same.

x: Others said: This means that no one was named after him before him.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement,
h
We have not made for him a namesake before
, no one had been named with that name before him.

c: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement,
h
We have not made for him a namesake before
, he said: No one was named Yahya before him.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj,
m: the same.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam told us
m: regarding the statement of God, We have not made for him any namesake before, he said: No one before him was named with this name.
b.via: Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam

c: Musa told us, he said: Amr told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: “Indeed, We give you good tidings of a boy whose name will be Yahya. We have not given anyone before him a namesake.” No one before him was named Yahya.

x: This statement, I mean the statement of the one who said: There was no one before Yahya named after him for Yahya, is more similar to the interpretation of that, and the meaning of the statement is: We did not make for the boy whom we gave as a spoil to you, whose name was Yahya before him, anyone named after him, and the word named is a noun derived from muf’il ilayhi.

God the Almighty says: Zachariah said when God gave him the good report of John: My Lord, how will I have a boy? And how can that be for me, while my wife is barren and cannot conceive, and I have become too weak from old age to have intercourse with women? Will You strengthen me to do what I have become too weak for, and make my wife fertile, for You are able to do that and to do what You will, or should I marry a wife other than my barren wife? He seeks confirmation from his Lord of the report, about the way in which the child that God gave him the good report would be for him, not out of denial from him, may God bless him and grant him peace, of the reality of what God promised him of a child, and how could that be a denial from him that He would grant him the child that He gave him the good report of, when he was the one who initiated the question to his Lord with His saying: Then grant me from Yourself an heir * Who will inherit me and inherit from the family of Jacob after His saying: Indeed, my bones have weakened and my head is shining with white hair.
Al-Saddī said about this:

c: Musa bin Harun told me, he said: Amr told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, he said:
m: Gabriel called to Zachariah, "Indeed, We give you good tidings of a boy whose name will be John. We have not given anyone before a namesake." When he heard the call, Satan came to him and said: O Zachariah, the voice that you heard is not from God, it is rather from Satan mocking you. If it were from God, He would have revealed it to you as He reveals to you other matters. So he doubted and said: How can I have a boy? He said: Where can he be from? And I have reached old age and my wife is barren. His saying,
h
And I have reached extreme old age

, means: I have become extremely old and have become like dry bones. It is said of a dry stick: an extremely old and stubborn stick. It has become extremely old, ya’tiyan and ‘atwan, and ‘asa ya’su ‘asan and ‘aswan. Everyone who has reached his limit in arrogance, corruption, or disbelief is extremely old and stubborn. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said.

x: Who said that?

c: Yaqub told me, he said: Hisham told us, he said: Husayn told us, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: I have learned the entire Sunnah, except that I do not know whether the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to recite in the noon and afternoon prayers or not, and I do not know how he used to recite this letter
h
and I have reached extreme old age
or deep old age.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement,
h
And I have reached extreme old age
, he said: By extreme old age he means old age.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: all on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, his statement atiya he said: thinness of bone.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us: Abd al-Razzaq told us: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement, from old age, insolence, he said: in age, and he was seventy-something years old.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement,
h
And I have reached extreme old age
, he said: The one who has become too old to have children is someone who thinks he will never have children.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn bin Al-Faraj,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd bin Sulayman narrated to us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement,
h
And I have reached extreme old age
, that it is old age.

evidence.text: Yaqub told me, he said: Hisham told us, he said: Husayn told us, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: I have learned the entire Sunnah, except that I do not know whether the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to recite in the noon and afternoon prayers or not, and I do not know how he used to recite this letter and I have reached extreme old age or deep old age.

x: God Almighty says: God said to Zachariah, answering him, He said, ‘Likewise.’ He says: This is the matter, as you say that your wife is barren, and that you have reached extreme old age. But your Lord says: The creation of what you gave me good report of, the boy whose name I told you was John, is easy for Me. So, from His saying,
h
Your Lord said
, ‘It is easy for Me.’ He is a metaphor for creation. And His statement,
h
And I created you before

, and you were nothing, the Most High says, “The creation of what I promised you that I would give you of the boy whose matter I mentioned to you since your old age and the barrenness of your wife is not more wondrous than your creation, for I created you and brought you into being a sound human being before My creation, and I did not give you the good report that I would give you of a child, and you were nothing, so likewise will I create for you the child that I gave you the good report of from your barren wife, with your old age and the weakness of your bones and the white hair of your head.”

And His saying, He said, ‘My Lord, make for me a sign.’ God Almighty says: Zachariah said: O Lord, make for me a sign and proof of what Your angels gave me of this boy about Your command and Your message, so that my heart may be reassured by that.

c: As Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, He said, ‘My Lord, make for me a sign,’ he said: He said, My Lord, make for me a sign that this is from You.

c: Musa told us, he said: Amr told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of al-Suddi:
m: He said: O Lord, if this voice is from you, then make for me a sign. God said: Your sign for that is that you will not speak to people for three nights while you are sound and healthy. There is no illness or disease preventing you from speaking. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said.

x: Who said that?

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Hakam told us, on the authority of Amr, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Saeed, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: Three nights together. He said: His tongue was tied without illness.

c: Ali told me, he said: Abdullah told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his saying three nights together means: without being mute.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, three nights together, he said: Do not let illness prevent you from speaking.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: That you do not speak to people for three nights in a row. He said: Healthy, and illness does not prevent you from speaking.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: “He said: Your sign is that you will not speak to people for three nights, without harm or muteness. He was only punished with that because he asked for a sign after the angels had spoken to him face to face, and he took hold of his tongue until he could not speak without nodding.

c: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Ikrimah,
m: regarding his statement, “three nights together,” he said: together, without being mute.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, He said, ‘Your sign is that you will not speak to people for three nights,’ and you are healthy. He said: So his tongue was tied, and he was unable to speak to anyone, and in that time he would glorify God, read the Torah, and read the Gospel. But if he wanted to speak to people, he was unable to speak to them.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, on the authority of someone
m: who is not accused, on the authority of Wahb ibn Munabbih al-Yamani, who said: God took hold of his tongue without harm, so he could no longer speak, and he only spoke to his people by gesture, until the three days had passed which God made a sign to fulfill what He promised him of His gift to him.

c: Musa told us, he said: Amr told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi,
m: “He said: Your sign is that you will not speak to people for three nights, without being mute except by gestures.” So his tongue was tied for three days and three nights.

x: Others said: Al-Sawi is an attribute of days. They said: The meaning of the speech is: He said, Your sign is that you will not speak to people for three consecutive nights.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his statement, He said, Your sign is that you will not speak to the people for three consecutive nights. He said: Three consecutive nights.

x: God Almighty says: Then Zachariah came out to his people from his place of prayer when he had restrained his tongue from speaking to the people, as a sign from God to him of the truth of His promise to him.
Ibn Jurayj used to say about the meaning of his exit from his prayer niche:

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj,
m: So he came out to his people from the prayer niche. He said: He looked out over his people from the prayer niche.

x: We have explained the meaning of the mihrab before, so there is no need to repeat it in this place.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding his statement,
h
So he came out to his people from the sanctuary
, he said: The sanctuary is his place of prayer, and he read, Then the angels called to him while he was standing praying in the sanctuary. And his saying,
h
Then He revealed to them

, means: He pointed to them. And that signal may be with the hand, with a book, or something else, by which one understands what he wants. And the Arabs have two dialects for that: waha revelation and awha inspiration. So whoever says waha revelation, says in yaf’al he does yahy he gives life, and whoever says awha revelation, says yuhy he inspires, and likewise awma gesture and yawma gesture. So whoever says wama gesture, says in yaf’al he does yamy he gives life, and whoever says awma gesture, says yawmi my day.

x: The interpreters differed about the meaning by which he revealed to his people.
Some of them said: He revealed to them by a gesture with his hand.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, So He revealed: So Zakariya pointed.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, on the authority of someone
m: who is not accused, on the authority of Wahb ibn Munabbih:
h
Then He revealed to them
. He said: Revelation is a sign.

c: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: So he revealed to them, he said: He gestured to them.

x: Others said: The meaning of inspired is wrote.
Who said that?

c: Mahmoud bin Khidash told us: Ibad bin Al-Awam told us, on the authority of Sufyan bin Hussein, on the authority of Al-Hakam, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding the statement of God Almighty:
h
Then He inspired them to glorify Him morning and evening
, he said: It was written for them on the earth.

c: Al-Hasan told us: Abd al-Razzaq told us, on the authority of al-Thawri, on the authority of Ibn Abi Laila, on the authority of al-Hakam:
m: h
Then He revealed to them
. He said: He wrote to them.

c: Musa told us, he said: Amr told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi,
m: h
So he came out to his people from the sanctuary
, and he wrote for them in a book, that they should glorify God morning and evening, and that is his saying, So he inspired them.

x: Others said: The meaning of this is: their command.
Who said that?

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement,
h
Then He inspired them to glorify Him morning and evening

, he said: I do not know whether it was a book that He wrote for them, or a sign that He indicated, and God knows best. He said: He commanded them to glorify Him morning and evening, and He did not speak to them. His saying, That they glorify Him in the morning and the evening, has been explained previously in the ways in which glorification is directed. It may be possible in this place that he meant by it glorification, which is the remembrance of God, so their command to devote themselves to the remembrance of God at the two ends of the day by glorifying Him. It may also be possible that he meant by it prayer, so their command to pray at these two times. Qatada used to say about this:

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us: Abd al-Razzaq told us: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement, Then He inspired them to glorify Him in the morning and the evening. He said: He signaled to them to pray in the morning and the evening. Surat Maryam: 11 Then he came out to his people from the sanctuary and signaled to them to glorify God morning and evening.

x: God Almighty says: Then John was born to Zachariah. When he was born, God said to him: O John, take this book with strength, meaning the book of God that He revealed to Moses, which is the Torah. With strength, he says: with seriousness.

c: As Al-Hasan told us, he said: Abd Al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement,
h
Take the Book with strength
, he said: Seriously.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
h
Take the Book with strength
, he said: seriously.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same. Ibn Zayd said about this:

c: Yunus told me that Ibn Wahb told us that
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding his statement, O Yahya,
h
take the Book with strength
, he said: Strength is to do what God has commanded him to do and to avoid what God has forbidden him to do.

x: I have explained the meaning of that with its evidence in what has passed in this book of ours, in Surat Al Imran, so that makes it unnecessary to repeat it in this place. And His statement,
h
And We gave him judgment while he was a boy
, means that God Almighty says: And We gave him understanding of the Book of God while he was a boy, before he reached the age of manhood.

c: Ahmad bin Mani’ told us: Abdullah bin Al-Mubarak told us: Muammar told me,
m: and he did not mention it from anyone else regarding this verse:
h
And We gave him judgment while he was a boy
. He said: It reached me that the boys said to Yahya: Let us go play. He said: I was not created for play. So God revealed:
h
And We gave him judgment while he was a boy

x: And His saying,
h
And mercy from Us
, God Almighty says:
h
And mercy from Us
and love for him, We gave him wisdom while he was a boy.
The interpreters differed about the meaning of compassion.
Some of them said: It means mercy, and they directed the speech to something similar to the meaning we directed it to.
Who said that?

c: Ali told us, he said: Abdullah told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his statement,
h
And compassion from Us
, meaning:
h
And mercy from Us

c: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told us: Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar told us: Shuʿbah told us, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of ʿIkrimah,
m: regarding this verse,
h
And compassion from Us
, he said: Mercy.

c: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement,
h
And compassion from Us
, he said: Mercy from Us.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hisham told us, he said: Juwaybir told us, on the authority of Al-Dahhak,
m: his statement:
h
And compassion from Us
he said: Mercy from Us, and no one possesses the power to bestow it except Us.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn bin Al-Faraj,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh, who said: Ubayd bin Sulayman told us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement,
h
And compassion from Us
, meaning: Mercy from Us, which no one other than Us is able to give.

x: Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is: And a mercy from Us to Zachariah. We gave him wisdom while he was a boy, and We did to him what We did.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement,
h
And compassion from Us
, meaning: mercy from Us.

x: Others said: The meaning of this is: Out of compassion for him, we did that.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us
And Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, his statement,
h
And compassion from Us
, he said: compassion from his Lord towards him.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same.

x: Others said: Rather, the meaning of compassion is love. They directed the meaning of the words to: And out of love from Us, We did that.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Hakam told us, on the authority of Anbasa, on the authority of Yahya bin Saeed, on the authority of Ikrimah:
m: h
And compassion from Us
. He said: Love for him.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding his statement, and compassion, he said: As for compassion, it is love.

x: Others said that it means that we respect him.
Who said that?

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Abu Tamila told us, on the authority of Abu Hamza, on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of Ata’ bin Abi Rabah,
m: h
And compassion from Us
. He said: Exaltation from Us. It was mentioned on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, that he said: I do not know what compassion is.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said: Amr ibn Dinar told me that
m: he heard Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: By God, I do not know what Hanan is. And the Arabs have two dialects for Hananak: Hananak, O our Lord, and Hananaik? As Tarafa ibn al-Abd said about Hananaik: Abu Munther, you have perished, so let some of us outlast your kindness. Some evil is less serious than others. Imru Al-Qais said in another language: And the Banu Shamji bin Jarim give it to their goat, your compassion, the compassionate one. The Arab scholars differed about Hananik.

x: Some of them said: It is the dual of Hanan.
Others said: Rather, it is a language that is not a dual. They said: That is like their saying: Hawalik?

Hitting, stabbing and shaking Those who said that Hananik is a dual have equated all of that, in that all of it is a dual. The origin of that, I mean Hanan, is from the saying of the speaker: So-and-so yearned for such-and-such, meaning he felt comfortable with him and longed for him. Then it is said: So-and-so yearned for so-and-so, if he described himself as being affectionate towards him, tender towards him, and merciful towards him, as the poet said: Have mercy on that king, for every situation has its own words.
Meaning: Be kind to me. Tenderness: is a noun derived from the saying: Welcome so-and-so to so-and-so. It is said from this: I was kind to him, so I am kind to him with tenderness and affection.

i: From this, it is said of a man’s wife: He was kind to him, because he was kind to her and showed her affection, as the rajaz poet said:
x: And one dark night I walked, and Hannah and Beit did not harm me.

And His saying, and zakat, God Almighty says: And We gave Yahya wisdom while he was a boy, and zakat: which is purification from sins, and using his body in the obedience of his Lord, so zakat is in apposition to wisdom from His saying, And We gave him wisdom. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement and zakat he said: Zakat is righteous work.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj,
m: his statement, and zakat, he said: righteous, pure work.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid bin Sulayman told us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement, and zakat, meaning righteous, pure deeds. And His saying, And he was pious, God Almighty says: And he was fearful of God, performing His obligations, avoiding His prohibitions, and hastening to obey Him.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: And he paid zakat and was pious. He said: He was pure and did not commit a sin.

c: Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding his statement, and zakat, and he was righteous, he said: As for zakat and piety, people have known them.

x: God Almighty says: He was dutiful to his parents, quick to obey them and love them, not disobedient to them. And he was not a disobedient tyrant. God Almighty says: He was not arrogant about obeying his Lord and obeying his parents, but he was humble and submissive to God and his parents, obeying what He commanded and refraining from what He forbade, not disobeying his Lord or his parents. His saying disobedient is a noun meaning that he is disobedient, from the saying of the speaker: So-and-so disobeyed his Lord, so he disobeys Him disobediently.
And his saying, "
h
Peace be upon him the day he was born

, the day he dies, and the day he is raised alive," means: And security from God the day he was born, from Satan afflicting him with evil, as he afflicts the children of Adam, and that is because it was narrated from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: Every child of Adam will come on the Day of Resurrection with a sin except for what was from John, son of Zechariah.

c: Ibn Hamid told us that: Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Yahya ibn Saeed, on the authority of Saeed ibn al-Musayyab, who said: Ibn al-Aas told me that
m: he heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say that.

c: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement, a disobedient tyrant, he said: Ibn al-Musayyab used to mention that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: No one will meet God on the Day of Resurrection except one who has sinned, except Yahya ibn Zakariya. He said: Qatada said: He did not sin, nor did he intend to have intercourse with a woman. And his saying,
h
And on the Day he dies

, he says: And security from God Almighty for him from the trials of the grave, and from the terror of the Day of Resurrection. And on the Day he is raised alive, he says: And security for him from the punishment of God on the Day of Resurrection, the Day of the Greatest Terror, from anything terrifying him, or from what terrifies creation. It was mentioned about Ibn Uyaynah in this regard:

c: Ahmad bin Mansour Al-Fayrozi told me: Sadaqah bin Al-Fadl told me:
m: I heard Ibn Atiyah say: The most frightening thing for a person is in three situations: the day he is born and sees himself emerging from what he was in; the day he dies and sees a people he has never seen; and the day he is resurrected and sees himself in a great gathering place. He said: So God honored Yahya bin Zakariya in it, and singled him out with peace, saying: “And
h
peace be upon him the day he was born
and the day he dies and the day he is resurrected alive.”

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, that Al-Hasan said:
m: Jesus and John met, and Jesus said to him: Ask forgiveness for me, you are better than me. The other said to him: Ask forgiveness for me, you are better than me. Jesus said to him: You are better than me. Have you greeted myself? And may God greet you. So God recognized its virtue.

x: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: And remember, O Muhammad, in the Book of God which He revealed to you in truth, Mary, the daughter of Imran, when she withdrew from her family and separated herself from them. It is derived from the verb nabdh, and nabdh means throwing away, and we have explained that with its evidence previously. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement,
h
And mention in the Book
, Mary, when she withdrew, meaning she was isolated from her family.

c: Sulayman ibn Abd al-Jabbar told me: Muhammad ibn al-Salt told us: Abu Kudayna told us, on the authority of Qabus, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: When she withdrew from her people to a place in the east. He said: She went out to a place in the east.

c: Musa told us, he said: Amr told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, he said:
m: Mary went out to the side of the prayer niche because of her menses, and this is His statement:
h
Then she withdrew from her family to a place to the east
: to the east of the prayer niche. And his saying, an eastern place, means: So she moved away and isolated herself from her people in a place before the rising of the sun, not its setting.

c: As Al-Hasan told us, he said: Abd Al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement, an eastern place, he said: from the east.

c: Ishaq bin Shaheen told me: Khalid bin Abdullah told us, on the authority of Dawud, on the authority of Amer, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said:
m: I know God’s creation, why did the Christians take the east as their qiblah? Because God said: Then she withdrew from her people to a place in the east, so they took the birth of Jesus as their qiblah.

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, he said: Abd Al-A’la told us, he said: Dawud told us, on the authority of Amer, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: the same.

c: Sulayman ibn Abd al-Jabbar told me: Muhammad ibn al-Salt told us: Abu Kudayna told us, on the authority of Qabus, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said:
m: The People of the Book were prescribed to pray towards the House and to perform the Hajj for God, and nothing turned them away from them except that your Lord said: You have withdrawn from your people to a place in the East, so they prayed before sunrise.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: When she withdrew from her people to a place to the east. He said: Vast and secluded. It was said: It only became a place near the rising of the sun, because what was near the east was better for them than what was near the west, and that is also what was mentioned among the Arabs.

x: And his saying, So she took a veil from them means: So she took a veil from her family to conceal her from them and from the people. And it was mentioned on the authority of Ibn Abbas that she was in a place facing the east, because God shaded her with the sun and made a veil from it for her.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his statement, She withdrew from her people to a place to the east, he said: A place where the sun shaded her so that none of them could see her.

x: Another said about this:

c: Musa told us, he said: Amr told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: So I took a veil from them of walls. And His saying,
h
So We sent to her Our Spirit

, means that God Almighty says: So We sent to her when she withdrew from her people to a place in the east, and took a veil from them: Gabriel. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said.

x: Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement,
h
Then We sent to her Our spirit
, he said: Gabriel was sent to her, as he told us.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, on the authority of someone
m: who is not accused, on the authority of Wahb ibn Munabbih, who said: I found Gabriel with her, whom God had represented as a perfect human being.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj,
m: his statement,
h
Then We sent to her Our spirit
, he said: Gabriel.

c: Muhammad bin Sahl told me: Ismail bin Abdul Karim told us:
m: Abdul Samad bin Maqal, the nephew of Wahb, told me: I heard Wahb bin Munabbih say: God sent Gabriel to Mary, and he appeared to her as a perfect human being.

c: Musa told us, he said: Amr told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of al-Suddi, he said:
m: When she had purified herself, meaning Mary from her menstruation, there was a man with her, and this is His statement:
h
Then We sent to her Our Spirit

, and he appeared to her as a well-proportioned man. God Almighty says: So he appeared to her in the form of a human being of sound creation among them, meaning in the form of a man from the children of Adam, of moderate creation.

x: God Almighty says: Mary feared Our Messenger, when he appeared to her as a well-mannered man, and she thought he was a man who wanted to have intercourse with her.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj,
m: regarding his statement, Indeed, I seek refuge in the Most Gracious from you, if you should be fearing God. He said: I feared that he only wanted it for herself.

c: Musa told us, he said: Amr told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi,
m: Then he appeared to her as a well-proportioned man. When she saw him, she was terrified by him and said: I seek refuge in the Most Gracious from you, if you should fear God. So she said: I seek refuge, O man, in the Most Gracious from you. She said: I seek refuge in the Most Gracious from you lest you do to me what He has forbidden you, if you have piety towards Him, fear His prohibitions, and avoid His disobedience, because whoever fears God, then he avoids that. If this was interpreted to mean: I seek refuge in the Most Gracious from you, if you fear God in my seeking refuge and protection in Him from you, then that would be correct.

c: Ibn Hamid also told us, saying: Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, on the authority of someone
m: who is not accused, on the authority of Wahb ibn Munabbih, She said, ‘I seek refuge in the Most Merciful from you, if you should be righteous.’ And you do not see anything but that he is a man from the children of Adam.

c: Abu Kurayb told us, he said: Abu Bakr told us, on the authority of Asim, he said: Ibn Zayd said:
m: And he mentioned the stories of Mary and said: You know that the pious one has a mind when she said: Indeed, I seek refuge in the Most Merciful from you, if you should be fearing God. He said: I am only a messenger from your Lord. God Almighty says: Then Our Spirit said to her: "I am only a messenger from your Lord, O Mary. He sent me to you "to give you a pure boy." The reciters differed in reading this. The reciters of Hijaz and Iraq, other than Abu Amr, read it as laahbi lak meaning: I am only a messenger from your Lord. He said: He sent me to you to give you a pure boy in the narrative. Abu Amr bin Al-Ala read it as liahbi lak ghulam zakiyyan meaning: I am only a messenger from your Lord. He sent me to you so that God may give you a pure boy.

x: The correct reading in this regard is what the reciters of the regions have said, which is la-ahba laka with an alif without a ya’, because this is how it is in the copies of the Qur’an of the Muslims, and this is the reading of their ancients and moderns, except for Abu ʿAmr, and it is not permissible to differ from them in what they have agreed upon, and it is not permissible for anyone to differ from their copies of the Qur’an. The pure boy is the one who is pure from sins, and the Arabs also say: a pure and virtuous boy, and a high and high boy.

evidence.text: The reciters differed in reading this.
The reciters of Hijaz and Iraq, other than Abu Amr, read it as laahbi lak meaning: I am only a messenger from your Lord.
Abu Amr bin Al-Ala read it as liahbi lak ghulam zakiyyan meaning: I am only a messenger from your Lord.

Abu Jaʿfar said: The correct reading in this regard is what the reciters of the regions have said, which is la-ahba laka with an alif without a ya’, because this is how it is in the copies of the Qur’an of the Muslims, and this is the reading of their ancients and moderns, except for Abu ʿAmr, and it is not permissible to differ from them in what they have agreed upon, and it is not permissible for anyone to differ from their copies of the Qur’an.

x: God Almighty says: Mary said to Gabriel, How can I have a boy? How can I have a boy? Is it before a husband that I marry, so that I may provide for him from him, or does God begin his creation from the beginning? And no man has touched me from the children of Adam through lawful marriage nor have I since none of them touched me in a lawful way out of lust I desired and did that in an unlawful way, so I conceived him from fornication.

c: As Musa told us, he said: Amr told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi,
m: And I was not a prostitute, meaning: a fornicator.

x: He said, 'Thus said your Lord, it is easy for Me.' God Almighty says: Gabriel said to her: "This is the matter as you describe, that no man has touched you and you are not unchaste, but your Lord said: It is easy for Me." That is, creating the boy whom you said I would give you is easy for Me, and it is not difficult for Me to create him. I gave him to you without a male to conquer you. And We will make him a sign to the people. He says: And so that We may make the boy whom We give to you a sign and proof of My creation, I give him to you. And a mercy from Us. He says: And a mercy from Us to you, and to whoever believes in him and acknowledges him, I create him from you. And it was a matter already decreed. He says: And his creation from you was a matter that God had decreed, and His judgment had gone ahead, and His foreknowledge preceded that he would be from you.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, who said: Someone I do not accuse told me, on the authority of Wahb ibn Munabbih:
m: And it was a matter decreed, meaning that God had decided on it, so there was no escape from it.

x: In this speech there is something that was omitted, its mention was omitted, as the indication of what was mentioned of it was sufficient for it. So We breathed into him of Our spirit into a boy. And she carried him and withdrew with him to a remote place. And thus came the interpretation of the people of interpretation.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Sahl told me, he said: Ismail bin Abdul Karim told us, he said:
m: Abdul Samad bin Maqal, the nephew of Wahb bin Munabbih, said: I heard Wahb say: When God sent Gabriel to Mary, he appeared to her as a perfect human being, and she said to him, I seek refuge in the Most Merciful from you, if you should be righteous. Then he blew into the pocket of her garment until the breath reached the womb and it was covered.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, on the authority of someone
m: who is not accused, on the authority of Wahb ibn Munabbih al-Yamani, who said: When he said that, meaning when Gabriel said, “Thus says your Lord: it is easy for Me,” the verse, she submitted to God’s command, so He blew into her bosom and then left her.

c: Musa told us, he said: Amr told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of al-Suddi, he said:
m: She threw her jilbab over her when Gabriel said that to her, so Gabriel took hold of her sleeves and blew into the pocket of her robe, which was torn in the front, and the breath entered her chest, and she became pregnant. Then her sister, the wife of Zachariah, came to visit her one night, and when she opened the door for her, she embraced her, and the wife of Zachariah said: O Mary, do you perceive that I am pregnant? Mary said: I also perceive that I am pregnant. The wife of Zachariah said: I have found that which is in my womb prostrating to that which is in your womb. So that is his saying, Confirming a word from God.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, he said: Ibn Jurayj said:
m: They say: He only blew into the pocket of her armor and her sleeve. And his saying,
h
So I withdrew with him to a remote place

, means: So I isolated myself with the one I carried, who was Jesus, and I withdrew with him to a remote place from the people. He says: A place far away from the people. It is said: He is in a remote place and Qasaf has the same meaning, as the rajaz poet said: You will sit in the seat far away from me, you dirty, fried one It is said: The place became distant, and I distanced the thing: if I removed it and delayed it. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said.

x: Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his statement,
h
So she withdrew with him to a remote place
, he said: A remote place.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: all of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, his statement, a remote place, he said: remote.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same.

c: Musa told us, he said: Amr told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, he said:
m: When it was time for Mary to give birth, she went out to the eastern side of the prayer niche and reached its farthest point.

x: And His saying,
h
So the birth pangs brought her to the trunk of the palm tree
, the Most High says:
h
So the birth pangs brought her to the trunk of the palm tree

, then it was said: When the ba' was dropped from it, it brought her, just as it is said: I brought you Zayd, so if the ba' is deleted, it is said: I brought you Zayd, just as the Most High said: Bring me iron sheets, and the meaning is: Bring me iron sheets, but the alif was extended when the ba' was deleted, and just as they said: I went out with it and I brought it out, and I went with it and I made it go, and it is more effective than coming, just as it is said: He came, and I brought him, meaning I brought him, and an example of the Arabs: The worst that came to me is the brain of Achilles tendon, and I willed, and it is said: The worst that comes to you and wills you to that, and from it is the saying of Zuhair: A neighbor who came to you relying on you, fear and hope came to him Meaning: He brought it, and he brought it to us, and he made you happy: from the language of Tamim, and he brought you from the language of the people of Aliyah, and the one who interpreted that interpreted it to mean: he forced her, because when the labor pains came to her at the trunk of the palm tree, he had forced her to it.
And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: all of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, his statement,
h
Then the birth pangs came upon her
, he said: The birth pangs forced her to labor.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, he said:
m: The birth pangs forced her to go to the trunk of the palm tree. Ibn Jurayj said: Ibn Abbas said: The birth pangs forced her to go to the trunk of the palm tree.

c: Musa told us, he said: Amr told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: Then the birth pangs drove her to the trunk of the palm tree. He said: The birth pangs forced her to the trunk of the palm tree.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement,
h
Then the pangs of childbirth drove her to the trunk of the palm tree
, he said: He forced her to the trunk of the palm tree. They differed as to the place where Mary took Jesus to give birth and where the labor pains came to her.

x: Some of them said: It was in the lowest part of Egypt and the last part of Syria. This is because she fled from her people when she became pregnant, so she headed towards Egypt, fleeing from them.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Sahl told us: Ismail bin Abdul Karim told us: Abdul Samad bin Maqal told us that
m: he heard Wahb bin Munabbih say: When Mary became pregnant, there was with her a relative of hers called Yusuf the carpenter. They were going to the mosque near Mount Zion, and that mosque at that time was one of their greatest mosques. Mary and Yusuf were serving in that mosque at that time, and there was great merit in serving it, so they desired that, so they were in charge of treating it themselves, cleaning it, sweeping it, purifying it, and every work that was done in it. No one among the people of their time worked more diligently and worshipped than them. The first to deny Mary’s pregnancy was her companion Yusuf. When he saw what was wrong with her, he was horrified by it, and it was great and terrible for him, so he did not know what to base his case on. When Yusuf wanted to accuse her, he mentioned her righteousness and innocence, and that she had never been away from him for a single hour. When he wanted to acquit her, he saw what had appeared on her. When that became too much for him, he spoke to her, and the first thing he said to her was: He said to her: Something has occurred to me about you that I feared, and I was keen to conceal it and keep it to myself, but that overcame me, and I found that speaking about it would be more healing for my chest. She said: Then say something nice. He said: “I would not say anything to you except that, so tell me. Can a plant grow without a seed?” She said: Yes. He said: Can a tree grow without rain falling on it? She said: Yes. He said: Can there be a boy without a boy? She said: Yes. He said: “Do you not know that God, the Blessed and Exalted, caused the plant to grow on the day He created it without a seed, and that the seed on that day only came from the plant that God caused to grow without a seed? Or do you not know that God, by His power, caused the tree to grow without rain, and that by that power He made the rain life for the tree after He created each one of them alone?” Or do you say: God will not be able to cause the tree to grow until He seeks help from water, and were it not for that He would not have been able to cause it to grow? Joseph said to her: I do not say this, but I know that God Almighty has power over whatever He wills. He says to it, Be, and it is. Mary said: Did you not know that God Almighty created Adam and his wife without a female Surat Maryam: 23 Then the birth pangs drove her to the trunk of a palm tree. She said, "Oh,
h
I wish I had died before this
and was in oblivion, forgotten." or a male? He said: Yes.

c: So when she told him that,
m: it occurred to him that what was in her was something from God Almighty, and that he could not ask her about it, because he saw that she was concealing it. Then Joseph took over the service of the mosque, and he spared her all the work she used to do there, because he saw the delicacy of her body, the yellowness of her color, the ageing of her face, the protrusion of her belly, the weakness of her strength, and the narrowness of her sight. Mary had not been like that before, so when her period of confinement approached, God revealed to her, Leave the land of your people, for if they get hold of you, they will insult you and kill your son. So she confided that to her sister, and her sister was pregnant at that time, and she had been given the good report of Yahya. When they met, Yahya’s mother found what was in her womb falling on its face, prostrating herself, confessing to Jesus. So Joseph carried her to the land of Egypt on his donkey, with nothing between it and the saddlebags when she rode. So Joseph set out with her until he was adjacent to the land of Egypt, at the farthest reaches of her people’s land. Mary was in confinement, and he forced her to the donkey’s manger, meaning the donkey’s trough, and the base of a palm tree. That was at a time when I think it was cold or hot, Abu Ja’far was skeptical, so Mary was distressed. The labor pains were severe, so she took refuge in a palm tree and embraced it, and the angels surrounded her, standing in rows surrounding her. Another statement other than this was narrated on the authority of Wahb bin Munabbih, which is:

c: Ibn Humayd narrated to us: Salamah narrated to us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, on the authority of someone
m: who is not accused, on the authority of Wahb ibn Munabbih, who said: When the time for her Mary’s delivery was approaching, and she experienced what a woman experiences in labor pains, she left the city, heading west from Ilia, until the birth overtook her at a village six miles from Ilia called Bethlehem. Then the labor pains brought her to the base of a palm tree, where there was a cow’s manger and beneath it a spring of water, so she gave birth to him near it.

x: Others said: Rather, when the time came for her to give birth, she went out to the eastern side of the prayer niche, and she came to its farthest point, and the labor pains forced her to the trunk of the palm tree. This is what al-Suddi said, and the narration of it was mentioned before.

c: Zakariya bin Yahya bin Abi Zaida told me: Hajjaj told us: Ibn Jurayj said: Al-Mughira bin Othman told me:
m: I heard Ibn Abbas say: It was not long before she became pregnant and gave birth.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said: And Al-Mughira bin Othman bin Abdullah informed me that
m: he heard Ibn Abbas say: It is not until she became pregnant and gave birth. And his saying,
h
I wish I had died before this
, he mentioned that she said that during labor out of shyness in front of people.

c: As Musa told us, he said: Amr told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, he said:
m: She said while she was being released from the rope out of shyness from the al-Nas 114:Oh,
h
I wish I had died before this
distress that I am in, and the grief of giving birth to a child without a husband, and I had been forgotten. She says: Oh,
h
I wish I had died before this

distress that I am in, and the grief of giving birth to a child without a husband, and I had been forgotten: something that was forgotten and then not sought after, like menstrual rags that when they are thrown away and discarded are not sought after or mentioned. Likewise, everything that is forgotten and left and not sought after is forgotten. And forgotten with the opening of the letter noon and its breaking are two well-known dialects of the Arabic languages with the same meaning, like the string and the string, and the bridge and the bridge, and whichever of them the reader recites is correct in our view, and with the breaking the majority of the readers of Hijaz, Madinah, and Basra and some of the people of Kufa recited it, and with the opening it is recited by the people of Kufa, and from it the saying of the poet: As if she has forgotten about the earth, she tells it when she comes out, and if she talks to you, she is noble. What he means by his saying: she sought it is: she sought it, because she had forgotten it until it was lost, then she remembered it and sought it. What he means by his saying: she sought it is: she did good and was truthful. If the word forget had been directed to the source of forgetfulness, it would have been correct. This is because the Arabs, as mentioned about them, say: I forgot it by forgetfulness and forgetfulness, as some of them said from the obedience of the Lord and the disobedience of Satan, meaning and disobedience, and as you say I came to it by coming and coming, as the poet said: They are known for their immoral acts and consider doing good deeds as forbidden. His saying forgotten is an action verb from I forgot something, as if she said: I wish I were the thing that was thrown away, then left and forgotten. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said.

x: Who said that?

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said: Ata’ Al-Khurasani told me, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his saying, Oh,
h
I wish I had died before this
and was forgotten and forgotten, I was not created, and I was nothing.

c: Musa told us, he said: Amr told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi,
m: h
And I was forgotten
, forgotten. He says: forgotten: my memory was forgotten, and forgotten: you say: my trace was forgotten, so no trace or eye can see me.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
And I was forgotten
and forgotten: meaning something that is not known or remembered.

c: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement,
h
And I was forgotten
, forgotten, he said: I do not know and it is not known who I am.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Abu Jaʿfar, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ bin Anas, Forgotten he said:
m: It is the miscarriage.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding his statement, Oh,
h
I wish I had died before this
and was forgotten and forgotten, I was never anything on earth.

Do you not see in the context of his statement, So she carried him and withdrew with him to a remote place, meaning: So she carried Jesus and withdrew with him. If this is the correct interpretation that we have explained, then it is clear that both readings, I mean from beneath her with a kasra, and from beneath her with a fatha, are correct. h

The Arabs do this because actions are referred to by the preposition ba, so it is said when you refer to I struck Amr: I did it to him, and so on with every action. Therefore, the preposition ba is inserted in actions and is removed, so its entry and exit are one meaning, so the meaning of the statement is:

, and if the commentators had interpreted it in this way: And shake toward you fresh, ripe dates with the trunk of the palm tree, meaning: on the trunk of the palm tree, in a correct manner, but I do not remember anyone interpreting it in this way. x: The correct thing to say about this, in my opinion, is that these three readings, I mean tasaqtāt with a ta’ and a shaddah on the seen, with a ta’ and a light seen, and with a ya’ and a shaddah on the seen, are readings with similar meanings. Each of them has been read by readers who are knowledgeable about the Qur’an, so whichever one the reader reads, he is correct in it. That is because if the trunk falls with its dates, and it is fixed and not cut off, then the palm tree has fallen with its dates. And if the palm tree falls with its dates, then the entire palm tree has fallen, its trunk and other than its trunk. That is because as long as the palm tree is standing on its foundation, it is only a trunk, a frond, and a palm branch. But if it is cut off, it becomes a trunk. So the trunk that Mary was ordered to shake, no one we know of has mentioned that it was a cut trunk other than al-Suddi.

And it has been claimed that by shaking it it became a palm tree, so its meaning and the meaning of the one who said: The dates that fell on it were one palm tree, so the correctness of what we have said is clear. His saying harvested means harvested. Its original form was maf’ul, so it was changed to fa’il. The harvested is that which is taken fresh. Everything that is taken from a fruit, or transferred from its place with its freshness, has been harvested. Therefore it was said: So-and-so harvests truffles. From this comes the saying of Ibn Akht Jadhima: This is my crime and his choice in it, as every criminal has his hand in his mouth.

x: God the Most High says: So eat of the fresh dates that fall upon you, and drink of the gushing water which your Lord has placed beneath you, fear neither hunger nor thirst. And be refreshed means: And be content and rejoice at the birth of me and do not grieve. The ‘ayn is in the accusative case because it is the one described as settled. The meaning of the statement is: And let your eye be content with your child. Then the action was transferred from the ‘ayn to the woman who has the ‘ayn. So the ‘ayn was in the accusative case since the action was originally for her according to the interpretation, similar to what was done in His statement: But if they give up willingly to you anything thereof
r
(An-Nisa’: 4)
, but it is: If they give up willingly to you anything thereof.” And His statement: And they are straitened with them (Hud 11:77- Al-‘Ankabut: 33). And from this is His statement:

meaning:
h
Fried fresh dates fall upon you
, so the action was transferred to the ‘ayn, according to the reading of those who read it with the letter ya’.

In the reading of those who read it as tasaqat with a ta’, its meaning is: the dates of the palm tree fall on you, then the verb was changed to the palm tree. The reciters differed in their recitation of his statement wa-qari. As for the people of Medina, they recited it wa-qari with a fat-ha on the qaf, according to the language of those who say: I reqararat bi-makan, I reqara bi-hu, and I reqararat ‘ayn, I reqara bi-hu qurur. This is the language of Quraysh, as was mentioned to me, and the recitation is based on it. As for the people of Najd, they say: I reqararat bi-hu ‘ayn, I reqara bi-hu qarran, and I reqararat bi-hu, I reqara bi-hu, so the recitation is based on their language and wa-qari ‘ayn with a kasra on the qaf, and the recitation with us is based on the language of Quraysh with a fat-ha on the qaf. ,’ meaning: So say: I have made it obligatory upon myself to God to be silent and not to speak to anyone from among the children of Adam today, so I will not speak to any human being today.

, that there were those among the Children of Israel who, when they exerted themselves, would fast from speech as they fasted from food, except for the remembrance of God. So he said that to her, and she said: I fast from speech as I fast from food, except for the remembrance of God. So when they spoke to her, she pointed to him, and they said, How can we speak to one who is in the cradle, a child? So he answered them and said, “Indeed, I am the servant of God. He has given me the Scripture,” until he reached, That is Jesus, the son of Mary, the word of truth about which they are in doubt. They differed about the reason for which he ordered her to fast from human speech.

x: Some of them said: He ordered her to do that because she did not have an apparent argument before the people, and that was because she came while she was widowed and had a child, to refrain from speaking so that it would suffice Surat Maryam 19:26 So eat and drink and be refreshed. And if you see from among mankind anyone, say, "Indeed,
h
I have vowed to the Most Merciful a fast
, so I will not speak to any human being today." her, so she ordered her child to speak.
Who said that?

c: Harun bin Ishaq Al-Hamadani narrated to us, saying: Musʿab bin Al-Muqaddam narrated to us, saying: Israel narrated to us, saying: Abu Ishaq narrated to us, on the authority of Haritha, who said:
m: I was with Ibn Masʿud when two men came, one of them greeted him and the other did not. He said: What is the matter with you? His companions said: He swore that he would not speak to the people today. Abdullah said: Speak to the people and greet them, for that is a woman who knows that no one will believe her that she became pregnant without a husband, meaning Mary, peace be upon her.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, when Jesus said to Mary, Do not grieve, she said: How can I not grieve when you are with me, neither a husband nor a slave? What excuse do I have before the people? I wish I had died before this and was in oblivion, forgotten. Jesus said to her: I will suffice you in speaking. But if you see anyone among mankind, say, ‘Indeed,
h
I have vowed to the Most Merciful a fast
, so I will not speak to any human being today.’ He said: All of this was Jesus’ speech to his mother.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, on the authority of someone
m: who is not accused, on the authority of Wahb ibn Munabbih: If you see anyone among mankind, say, ‘Indeed, I have vowed to the Most Merciful to fast, so I will not speak to any human being today.’ Then I will suffice you in speaking.

x: Others said: This was a sign for Mary and her son.
Who said that?

c: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement, Indeed,
h
I have vowed to the Most Merciful a fast

, he said in some of the letters: silence, and that is because you will not find an ignorant woman saying: I vowed as Mary vowed, not to speak one day until night, and God only made that a sign for Mary and her son, and it is not permissible for anyone to vow silence one day until night.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: so he recited: Indeed,
h
I have vowed to the Most Merciful a fast
. And it was read in the first letter: silence, and it was only a sign that God sent to Mary and her son.

x: Others said: Rather, she was fasting on that day, and the fasting person at that time was fasting from food, drink, and speaking to people, so Mary was permitted to speak for the amount of time that day while she was fasting.
Who said that?

c: Musa told us, he said: Amr told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of al-Suddi:
m: If you see anyone among mankind speaking to you, say, ‘Indeed,
h
I have vowed to the Most Merciful a fast
, so I will not speak to any human being today.’ So whoever fasted at that time would not speak until evening. So it was said to her: Do not say more than this.

evidence.text: And from this is His statement: Fried fresh dates fall upon you meaning: Fried fresh dates fall upon you, so the action was transferred to the ‘ayn, according to the reading of those who read it with the letter ya’.
In the reading of those who read it as tasaqat with a ta’, its meaning is: the dates of the palm tree fall on you, then the verb was changed to the palm tree.
The reciters differed in their recitation of his statement wa-qari.

As for the people of Medina, they recited it wa-qari with a fat-ha on the qaf, according to the language of those who say: I reqararat bi-makan, I reqara bi-hu, and I reqararat ‘ayn, I reqara bi-hu qurur.
This is the language of Quraysh, as was mentioned to me, and the recitation is based on it.

As for the people of Najd, they say: I reqararat bi-hu ‘ayn, I reqara bi-hu qarran, and I reqararat bi-hu, I reqara bi-hu, so the recitation is based on their language and wa-qari ‘ayn with a kasra on the qaf, and the recitation with us is based on the language of Quraysh with a fat-ha on the qaf.
And it was read in the first letter: silence, and it was only a sign that God sent to Mary and her son.

x: God Almighty says: When Jesus said that to his mother, she felt reassured, submitted to God’s command, and carried him until she brought him to her people.

c: Ibn Hamid also told us: Salamah told us on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, on the authority of someone
m: who is not accused, on the authority of Wahb ibn Munabbih, who said: He made her, meaning Mary, forget the distress of the affliction and the fear of the people because of what she had heard from the angels about the good report of Jesus, until he spoke to her, meaning Jesus, and the fulfillment of what God had promised her came to her, she bore it and then returned with it to her people. Al-Saddī said about this:

c: Musa told us, he said: Amr told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, he said:
m: When she gave birth to him, Satan went and informed the Children of Israel that Mary had given birth, so they came rushing forward, so they called her, and she brought him to her people, carrying him. And His saying, They said, ‘O Mary, you have certainly done a thing unprecedented.’ God Almighty says: So when they saw Mary, and saw with her the child she had given birth to, they said to her: O Mary, you have done a wondrous thing, and you have brought about a great event, and every doer of a work that he has done well and perfected has done it wonderfully, as the rajaz poet said: You fed me a stone date with which you used to scatter the fleas. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said.

x: Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: all on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding the statement of God Almighty, Fara’a, he said: Great.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement,
h
You have certainly done something unprecedented
, he said: great.

c: Musa told us, he said: Amr told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi,
m: h
You have certainly done something unprecedented
. He said: Great.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, on the authority of someone
m: who is not accused, on the authority of Wahb ibn Munabbih, who said: When they saw her and saw him with her, they said: O Mary, You have certainly done a thing outrageous: meaning, the immorality that is not close.

x: The people of interpretation differed about the reason for which she was called:
h
O sister of Aaron
, and who was this Aaron whom God mentioned, and he informed that they attributed Mary to her as his sister, so some of them said: She was called
h
O sister of Aaron
as an attribution from them to righteousness, because the righteous people among them were called Aaron, and not Aaron, the brother of Moses.
Who said that?

c: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement,
h
O sister of Aaron
, he said: There was a righteous man among the Children of Israel called Aaron, so they likened her to him, and they said: O you who resemble Aaron in righteousness.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement,
h
O sister of Aaron
, your father was not a man of evil, nor was your mother unchaste. He said: She was from a family known for their righteousness, and not for their corruption.

x: Some people are known for their righteousness and have children through it, and others are known for their corruption and have children through it. Aaron was a reformer who was beloved by his clan. He was not Aaron, the brother of Moses, but another Aaron. He said: It was mentioned to us that forty thousand people accompanied his funeral procession on the day he died, all of them named Aaron from the Children of Israel.

c: Yaqub told me, he said: Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Saʿid ibn Abi Sidqah, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Sirin, he said:
m: I was informed that Kaʿb said: His saying,
h
O sister of Aaron

, does not refer to Aaron, the brother of Moses. He said: Aisha said to him: You have lied. He said: O Mother of the Believers, if the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said it, then he is more knowledgeable and informed, otherwise I find that there are six hundred years between them. He said: So she was silent.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding his statement,
h
O sister of Aaron

, he said: A name that matches a name, how many nations are there between Aaron and them, many nations. Abu Kurayb, Ibn Al-Muthanna, Sufyan, Ibn Wakee’ and Abu Al-Sa’ib narrated: Abdullah Ibn Idris Al-Awdi narrated: I heard my father mention on the authority of Samak Ibn Harb, on the authority of Alqamah Ibn Wa’il, on the authority of Al-Mughirah Ibn Shu’bah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent me to the people of Najran, and they said to me: Do you not recite
h
O sister of Aaron

? I said: Yes, and you know what happened between Jesus and Moses. So I returned to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and informed him. He said: Why did you not tell them that they used to water their children through their prophets and the righteous before them?

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Al-Hakam bin Bashir told us: Amr told us, on the authority of Samak bin Harb, on the authority of Alqamah bin Wa’il, on the authority of Al-Mughirah bin Shu’bah, who said:
m: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent me to the people of Najran on some of his errands. They said: Didn’t your Prophet claim that Aaron, the brother of Mary, was the brother of Moses? I did not know what to say to them until I returned to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and mentioned that to him. He said: They used to name people after the names of those who came before them.

x: Some of them said: He meant Aaron, the brother of Moses, and Mary was attributed to him as his sister because she was from his descendants. It is said to the Tamimi: O brother of Tamim, and to the Mudarite: O brother of Mudar.
Who said that?

c: Musa told us, he said: Amr told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: h
O sister of Aaron
. He said: She was from the sons of Aaron, the brother of Moses, and it is as you say: O brother of the sons of so-and-so.

x: Others said: Rather, he was one of their men who was a wicked man who was openly wicked, so they attributed it to him.

The correct statement about this is what was reported from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, which we mentioned, and that she was attributed to a man from her people. His saying,
h
Your father was not a bad man
, means:
h
Your father was not a bad man
who committed indecencies. And your mother was not a prostitute, means: Your mother was not a fornicator.

c: As Musa told me, he said: Amr told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi,
m: And your mother was not a prostitute, he said: an adulteress. And he said: And your mother was not a prostitute, and he did not say: a prostitute, because that is something that describes women and not men, so it is treated like a menstruating or divorced woman.

x: Some of them likened that to their saying: a new cloak and a murdered woman. Surat Maryam 19:28
h
O sister of Aaron
, your father was not a man of evil, nor was your mother unchaste.
God Almighty says: When her people said that to her, she told them what Jesus had ordered her to say to them, then she motioned to Jesus to speak to him.

c: As Musa told us, he said: Amr told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, he said:
m: When they said to her, Your father was not a bad man, nor was your mother unchaste, she told them what God had commanded her to do. Then when they wanted her to speak after that, she pointed to it, to Jesus.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement,
h
So she pointed to him
, he said: She ordered them to speak to him.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, on the authority of someone
m: who is not accused, on the authority of Wahb ibn Munabbih: She pointed to him. He said: She pointed to him to speak to him.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj,
m: his saying
h
so she pointed to him

is that they spoke to him. And His statement, They said, ‘How can we speak to one who is in the cradle, a child?’ God Almighty says, Her people said to her: How can we speak to one who is in the cradle? And in His statement, who is in the cradle, a child, there is a meaning of completion, not that which requires report, and that is similar in meaning to the word was in His statement, Was I anything but a human messenger? (al-Isra’ 17:93). Rather, the meaning of that is: Am I anything but a human messenger? And was I found or sent? And as Zuhair ibn Abi Salma said: A free woman, Arhabiya, rebuked him, and the color of the night was like apricot. Meaning: It has become or has been found. It was said that what is meant by the cradle in this place is: his mother’s lap.

x: Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: Whoever is in the cradle as a child. The cradle is the stone.

x: We have explained the meaning of the cradle in the past with its evidence, so there is no need to repeat it in this place.

God Almighty says: When Mary's people said to her, How can we speak to one who is in the cradle, a child? and they thought that this was a mockery of them, Jesus said to them, speaking on behalf of his mother, "Indeed, I am the servant of God. He has given me the Scripture." And when she pointed to Jesus in what was mentioned about them, they became angry.

c: As Musa told me, he said: Amr told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, he said:
m: When she pointed to Jesus to them, they became angry and said: Her mockery of us when she ordered us to speak to this boy is more severe for us than her adultery. They said: How can we speak to one who is in the cradle, a child?

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, on the authority of someone
m: who is not accused, on the authority of Wahb ibn Munabbih: They said, ‘How can we speak to one who is in the cradle, a child?’ So Jesus answered them about it and said to them, “Indeed, I am the servant of God. He has given me the Scripture and made me a prophet.” . . . the verse.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, They said, ‘How can we speak to one who is in the cradle, a child?’ He said to them, “Indeed, I am a servant of God. He has given me the Scripture and made me a prophet.” So he recited until he reached, And has not made me a wretched tyrant. They said, Indeed, this is a great matter.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd ibn Sulayman told us, who said: I heard Ad-Dahhak say: “How can we speak to one who is in the cradle, a child? He said: I am the servant of God.” Jesus did not speak until that time, when “They said: How can we speak to one who is in the cradle, a child?” And his saying:
h
He has given me the Book

, means that the speaker says: Or He gave him the Book and the revelation before he was created in his mother’s womb, for the meaning of that is contrary to what is thought, rather its meaning is: And He decreed on the day He decreed the affairs of His creation until He gave me the Book.

c: As Bishr bin Adam told me, he said: Ad-Dahhak told us,
m: meaning Ibn Mukhallad, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Ikrimah, who said: He gave me the Book, meaning: He decreed that the Book would be given to me in the past.
