c: Muhammad bin Bashar told us: Abu Asim told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Ikrimah,
m: regarding his statement, “Indeed, I am a servant of God.
h
He has given me the Book
,” he said: the judgment.

c: Al-Hasan told us: Abd al-Razzaq told us, on the authority of Israel, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Ikrimah,
m: regarding God’s statement, “Indeed, I am the servant of God. He has given me the Scripture.” He said: He decreed that the Scripture should be given to me. And his saying,
h
And He made me a prophet

. I have explained the meaning of prophet and the differences of opinion among those who differ about it, and the correct statement about it according to us with its evidence in what has passed, which makes it unnecessary to repeat it. Mujahid used to say about the meaning of the Prophet alone what:

c: Muhammad bin Amr told us: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us,
m: all of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, who said: The Prophet alone is the one who speaks and to whom revelation is sent, and he is not sent.

x: And his saying,
h
And made me blessed
, the people of interpretation differed regarding the meaning of that.
Some of them said: Its meaning is: And made me beneficial.
Who said that?

c: Sulayman bin Abd al-Rahman bin Hammad al-Talhi told me: Al-Ala’ told us, on the authority of Aisha,
m: the wife of Layth, on the authority of Layth, on the authority of Mujahid: And He made me blessed, he said: beneficial.

x: Others said: His blessing was enjoining good and forbidding evil.
Who said that?

c: Sulayman ibn Abd al-Jabbar told me: Muhammad ibn Yazid ibn Khunais al-Makhzumi told us:
m: I heard Wahib ibn al-Ward, a client of Banu Makhzum, say: A scholar met another scholar who was above him in knowledge, and said to him: May God have mercy on you, what of my knowledge have you made public? He said: Enjoining what is right and forbidding what is wrong, for it is the religion of God with which He sent His prophets to His servants. The jurists have agreed upon the statement of God: And has made me blessed wherever I may be. It was said: What is its blessing? He said: Enjoining what is right and forbidding what is wrong wherever it may be.
b.via: Muhammad ibn Yazid ibn Khunais al-Makhzumi

x: Others said: The meaning of this is: He made me a teacher of goodness.
Who said that?

c: Yunus bin Abdul A’la told me: Sufyan told us
m: regarding his statement,
h
And He has made me blessed wherever I may be
, he said: A teacher of goodness.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Jarir told us, on the authority of Laith, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement,
h
And He has made me blessed wherever I may be
, he said: A teacher of goodness wherever I may be. And his saying,
h
And He enjoined upon me prayer and zakat

, means: And He decreed that He enjoined upon me prayer and zakat, meaning preserving the limits of prayer and performing it as He enjoined upon me. And zakat has two meanings: One of them is: The zakat of wealth, which is to be paid. And the other is: Purifying the body from the filth of sins, so its meaning is: And He enjoined upon me to abandon sins and avoid transgressions. His saying,
h
As long as I am alive

, means: As long as I was alive in this world and existing. This shows that the meaning of zakat in this context is: purifying the body from sins, because what Jesus, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, is described as is that he did not save anything for tomorrow, so zakat on money is obligatory upon him, unless the zakat that was imposed upon him was charity on everything that was in excess of his strength, in which case that would be a correct interpretation.

x: God Almighty says, informing about what Jesus said to the al-Nas 114:And He made me blessed and dutiful: meaning He made me dutiful to my mother. And dutifulness is being dutiful, it is said: He is dutiful to his father, and dutiful to him, and the readers of the regions read this letter with the opening of the ba.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Abu Nahik
m: that: Ibn Humayd narrated: Yahya ibn Wadeh narrated: Abdul-Mu'min narrated: Abu Nahik read, And be dutiful to my mother from the words of Jesus, peace be upon him. Abu Nahik said: He enjoined upon me prayer, zakat, and being dutiful to my parents, just as he enjoined upon me that. So Abu Nahik interpreted the words to mean, And be dutiful to my mother as being from the report of Jesus, from God's enjoining upon him that, just as his words, And enjoined upon me prayer and zakat are from his report of God's enjoining upon him that. So according to this opinion, the accusative of birr must mean the implementation of the enjoining in it, because prayer and zakat, even though they are in the genitive case in the wording, are in the accusative case because they are the objects of them. And His saying,
h
And He did not make me a wretched tyrant
, means: And He did not make me arrogant towards God in what He commanded me to do and what He forbade me from doing. And wretched, but He humbled me to obey Him and made me humble.

c: As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, he said:
m: It was mentioned to us that he - meaning Jesus - used to say: Ask me, for my heart is soft, and I am small in my soul, because of the humility God gave him.

c: And Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: And dutiful to my mother and did not make me a wretched tyrant. It was mentioned to us that a woman saw the son of Mary bringing the dead back to life, and healing the blind and the leper, in signs that God had given him authority over and permitted him to do. So she said: Blessed is the womb that bore you, and the breast that nursed you. So the Prophet of God, the son of Mary, said in response to her: Blessed is he who recites the Book of God and follows what is in it, And did not make me a wretched tyrant.

c: Al-Qasim narrated to us, he said: Al-Hussein narrated to us, he said: Muhammad bin Katheer narrated to us, on the authority of Abdullah bin Waqid Abu Raja, on the authority of some of the people of knowledge, he said:
m: You will not find a disobedient person except that you will find him a tyrant and a wretched person. Then he recited: And dutiful to my mother, and He has not made me a wretched tyrant. He said: And you will not find a person of bad character except that you will find him arrogant and proud. Then he recited: “And those whom your right hands possess. Indeed, God does not like anyone who is arrogant and boastful.”
r
(An-Nisa’: 36)
b.via: some of the people of knowledge

evidence.text: And dutifulness is being dutiful, it is said: He is dutiful to his father, and dutiful to him, and the readers of the regions read this letter with the opening of the ba.

x: And his saying, "
h
And peace be upon me the day I was born

, the day I die, and the day I am raised alive," means: And security from God upon me from Satan and his soldiers on the day I was born, lest they should harm me as they harm those who are born at birth, by stabbing them, and on the day I die, from the terror of the rising, and on the day I am raised alive on the Day of Resurrection, lest I be struck by the terror that befalls people when they witness the terrors of that day.

c: Ibn Hamid also told us, saying: Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, on the authority of someone
m: who is not accused, on the authority of Wahb ibn Munabbih, “
h
And peace be upon me the day I was born

and the day I die and the day I am raised alive.” He said: He tells them in the story of his report about himself, that he has no father and that he will die and then be raised alive. God Almighty says, That is Jesus, the son of Mary - the word of truth about which they are in dispute.

x: God Almighty says: This one whose description I have explained to you and whose report I have informed you of, regarding the matter of the boy whom Mary carried, is Jesus, son of Mary, and this description is his description, and this report is his report, and it is the word of truth, meaning that this report that I have related to you is the word of truth, and the speech that I have recited to you is the word of God and His report, not report other than it, in which there is confusion and doubt, addition and subtraction, according to what God Almighty used to say: So say about Jesus, O people, this statement that God has informed you about him, not what the Jews said, who claimed that he was not of sound mind and that he was a lying magician, nor what the Christians said, that he had a son for God, and that God did not take a son, and that is not appropriate for Him. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: his statement,
h
That is Jesus
, the son of Mary, the word of truth, he said: God is the Truth.

c: Yahya bin Ibrahim Al-Masoudi told me: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of his grandfather, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Ibrahim, who said:
m: They used to say about this letter in the recitation of Abdullah: He said the truth about which they are in doubt. He said: The word of God. If the interpretation of this is directed to:
h
That is Jesus

, son of Mary, the true word, meaning that is the true word, then the definite article is deleted from the word and added to the truth, as it was said: Indeed, this is the certain truth (al-Waqi’ah 56:95). And as it was said: The promise of truth which they were promised (al-Ahqaf 46:16), it would be a correct interpretation. The reciters differed in their reading of this. The reciters of Hijaz and Iraq read it as the saying of truth, with the saying raised, according to the meaning I described, and they made it in its parsing dependent on Jesus, like an adjective for him. The matter in its parsing, in my opinion, is not as said by those who claimed that it is raised as an adjective for Jesus, unless the meaning of the saying is the word, according to what we mentioned about Ibrahim, from his interpretation of that in this way, then it is correct for it to be an adjective for Jesus. Otherwise, in my opinion, it is raised by an implied word, which is this saying of truth, as a beginning. This is because the report had ended about the story of Jesus and his mother when he said,
h
That is Jesus

, son of Mary, then the report began with the truth in what the nations doubt about the matter of Jesus, is this saying, which God informed His servants about him, and no other. Asim bin Abi al-Najud and Abdullah bin Amir read it in the accusative case, as if they intended by that the source:
h
That is Jesus

, son of Mary, a true saying, then the definite article was inserted into it. As for what was mentioned by Ibn Masoud regarding his reading that Jesus, son of Mary, said the truth, it means saying the truth, like play and shame, and blame and blame.

x: The correct reading of this in our view is to raise it, due to the consensus of the authoritative reciters on it. As for the statement of God Almighty, about which they are in doubt, it means: about which they dispute and differ, from their saying: I disputed with so-and-so, if you argued with him and disputed with him. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement,
h
That is Jesus

, the son of Mary, the word of truth about which they are in dispute, the Jews and Christians were in dispute about him. As for the Jews, they claimed that he was a lying magician, and as for the Christians, they claimed that he was the son of God, the third of three, and a god, and they all lied, but he is the servant of God and His Messenger, and His Word and His Spirit.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Husayn told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj,
m: regarding his statement, about which they are in doubt, he said: They differed, and a group said: He is the servant and prophet of God, so they believed in him.

x: A group said: Rather, he is God.
A group said: He is the son of God. Blessed and exalted be He above what they say, far above. He said: That is what he said: Then the parties differed among themselves
r
(Maryam 19:37)

and what is in Az-Zukhruf. Decius, Nestorius, and Mar Ya’qub said: When God raised Jesus, one of them said: He is God, and the other said: The Son of God, and the other said: The Word of God and His servant. So the two slanderers said: My saying is more similar to your saying, and your saying is more similar to my saying than this one’s saying, so come, let us fight them. So they fought them and Israel subdued them. So they brought out four men from among them, each group brought out their scholar. So they doubted Jesus when he was raised. So one of them said: He is God, He descended to the earth and gave life to whomever He gave life, and caused death to whomever He caused to die, then He ascended to the heavens.

They are the Jacobites. So the three said: You have lied. Then two of them said to the third: You say about him. He said: He is the Son of God. They are the Nestorians. So the two said: You have lied. Then one of the two said to the other: Say about him. He said: He is the third of three: God is God, and he is God, and his mother is God. They are the Israelites, the kings of the Christians. The fourth said: You have lied. He is the servant of God, His Messenger, and His spirit. And his word, and they are the Muslims, so each man of them had followers for what he said, so they fought, and he prevailed over the Muslims, and that is the saying of God And they kill those who enjoin justice among the people
r
(Al Imran 3:21)
. Qatada said: They are the ones about whom God said So the parties differed
r
(Maryam 19:37)
, they differed about it and became parties.

evidence.text: Yahya bin Ibrahim Al-Masoudi told me: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of his grandfather, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Ibrahim, who said: They used to say about this letter in the recitation of Abdullah: He said the truth about which they are in doubt.
The reciters differed in their reading of this.

The reciters of Hijaz and Iraq read it as the saying of truth, with the saying raised, according to the meaning I described, and they made it in its parsing dependent on Jesus, like an adjective for him.

Asim bin Abi al-Najud and Abdullah bin Amir read it in the accusative case, as if they intended by that the source: That is Jesus, son of Mary, a true saying, then the definite article was inserted into it.
As for what was mentioned by Ibn Masoud regarding his reading that Jesus, son of Mary, said the truth, it means saying the truth, like play and shame, and blame and blame.
Abu Jaʿfar said: The correct reading of this in our view is to raise it, due to the consensus of the authoritative reciters on it.

x: God Almighty says: Those who said: Jesus is the son of God have certainly disbelieved, and they have greatly slandered him. It is not appropriate for God to take a son, and that is not appropriate for Him and will not happen. Rather, He created everything below Him. This is similar to the statement of Amr ibn Ahmar: In the head of a nobleman from a lofty phoenix, no plain or mountain can be sought beyond it. And from His saying that He should take in the nominative case with was. And His saying Glory be to Him He says: To glorify God and to acquit Him from having what the disbelievers who say: Jesus is the son of God have added to Him. And His saying When He decrees a matter, He only says to it, “Be, and it is. The Most High says: God only began the creation of Jesus in the beginning, and brought him into being, without a stallion, so that his mother would be fertile. But He said to him, Be, and he was, because that is how He creates and invents things. He only says when He decrees the creation of something or its bringing it into being: Be, and it is existing and new. His creation is not too great for Him, because He does not create it with difficulty and effort, nor does He bring it into being with treatment and hardship.

And his saying, And indeed, God is my Lord and your Lord, so worship Him. The reciters differed in reading that. The majority of the reciters of Medina and Basra read it as and God is my Lord and your Lord. The Arabists differed in the reason for opening the an when it is opened.

Some of the grammarians of Kufa said: It is opened in response to Isa and in apposition to it, meaning: That is Isa, son of Mary, and that is because God is my Lord and your Lord. If that is the case, then an is a nominative, and it can be interpreted as a genitive, as he said, That is because your Lord would not destroy the cities unjustly.
r
(Al-An'am: 131)
He said: If you opened it on his saying And He enjoined upon me that it is God, it would be a reason.

Some of the Basrans said: And this was also mentioned from Abu Amr ibn al-Ala, and he was one of those who read it with the opening. Rather, an is opened with the interpretation and He decreed that God is my Lord and your Lord. The majority of the Kufi readers read it as And God with a kasra on in meaning sequence, as in the saying He only says to him. It was mentioned on the authority of Abi bin Ka’b that he used to read it as He only says to him, ‘Be,’ and it is. Indeed, God is my Lord and your Lord,” without a waw.

The reading that we prefer in this regard is the kasra as a beginning. If it is read in this way, it has no place. It may be permissible for it to be in apposition to in which is with his statement, “He said, ‘Indeed, I am the servant of God. He has given me the Book’” and Indeed, God is my Lord and your Lord. If someone, among those who read it in the accusative case, were to say: It is in apposition to the Book, meaning: He gave me the Book, and He gave me that God is my Lord and your Lord, that would be a good interpretation. The meaning of the statement is: And I and you, O people, are all servants of God, so worship Him alone and no one else. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, on the authority of someone
m: who is not accused, on the authority of Wahb ibn Munabbih, who said: He made a covenant with them when he informed them about himself, his birth, his death, and his mission, that “God is my Lord and your Lord, so worship Him.
h
This is a straight path
.” That is, I and you are the servants of God, so worship Him and do not worship anyone other than Him. And his saying,
h
This is a straight path

, means: This that I have recommended to you and informed you that God has commanded me to do is the straight path, which whoever follows it will be saved and whoever follows it will be guided, because it is the religion of God that He commanded His prophets to do.

evidence.text: The reciters differed in reading that.
The majority of the reciters of Medina and Basra read it as and God is my Lord and your Lord.
Some of the Basrans said: And this was also mentioned from Abu Amr ibn al-Ala, and he was one of those who read it with the opening.
The majority of the Kufi readers read it as And God with a kasra on in meaning sequence, as in the saying He only says to him.
It was mentioned on the authority of Abi bin Ka’b that he used to read it as He only says to him, ‘Be,’ and it is.
Abu Jaʿfar said: The reading that we prefer in this regard is the kasra as a beginning.
If it is read in this way, it has no place.

If someone, among those who read it in the accusative case, were to say: It is in apposition to the Book, meaning: He gave me the Book, and He gave me that God is my Lord and your Lord, that would be a good interpretation.

x: God Almighty says: So the disputants differed about Jesus, and they became divided parties from among his people.

c: As Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told me, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, his statement,
h
Then the parties differed among themselves
, he said: The People of the Book.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement,
h
Then the parties differed among themselves

, it was mentioned to us that when the son of Mary was raised, the Children of Israel chose four of their jurists, and they said to the first: What do you say about Jesus? He said: He is God who descended to earth, created what He created, and gave life to what He gave life, then ascended to heaven.

x: Some people followed him in that, and the Jacobites were among the Christians, and the other three said: We bear witness that you are a liar. They said to the second: What do you say about Jesus? He said: He is the son of God.

Some people followed him in that, and the Nestorians were among the Christians, and the other two said: We bear witness that you are a liar. They said to the third: What do you say about Jesus? He said: He is a god, and his mother is a god, and God is a god.

Some people followed him in that, and the Israelite was from the Christians. The fourth said: I bear witness that you are a liar, but he is the servant and messenger of God, he is the word of God and His spirit. So the people argued, and the Muslim said: I ask you by God, do you know that Jesus used to feed people, and that God, the Blessed and Exalted, does not feed people? They said: By God, yes. He said: Do you know that Jesus used to sleep? They said: By God, yes. He said: So the Muslim argued with them. He said: So the people fought. He said: It was mentioned to us that the Jacobites appeared on that day and the Muslims were afflicted, so God revealed in that Quran: Indeed, those who disbelieve in the verses of God and kill the prophets without right and kill those who enjoin justice among the people - give them tidings of a painful punishment.
r
(Al Imran 3:21)
Al-Hasan told us, he said:

c: Ishaq told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
Then the parties differed among themselves
. They differed about it and became parties. And His saying,
h
So woe to those who disbelieve from the sight of a tremendous Day

, means: So woe to those who disbelieve in God, from those who claim that Jesus was born of God, and other disbelievers in Him from witnessing a tremendous Day, which is the Day of Resurrection. Qatada used to say in his interpretation of this:

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: God said: So woe to those who disbelieve from the scene of a tremendous Day. They witnessed a tremendous terror.

x: God Almighty says, informing about the state of those who disbelieve in Him, who make rivals for Him, and who claim that He has a son on the day they come to Him in the Hereafter: If they were blind in this world to seeing the truth, and to looking at the proofs of God that indicate His Oneness, and deaf to hearing the verses of His Book, and what God’s messengers called them to in it of acknowledging His Oneness, and what He sent His prophets with, then what will they hear on the day they come to their Lord in the Hereafter, and what will they see on that day when sight and hearing will not benefit them. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement,
h
I hear and see them
, that, by God, is on the Day of Resurrection. They heard when hearing did not benefit them, and they saw when sight did not benefit them.

c: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement,
h
I hear them and see them
, he said: I hear a people and I see them.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Abu Sufyan told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, he said:
m: I will hear about them and see them on the Day they come to us on the Day of Resurrection.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Abu Jaʿfar, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ bin Anas, on the authority of Abu Al-ʿAliyah, he said:
m: I hear their talk today and I see how they will be treated on the day they come to Us.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd, regarding His statement,
h
I will hear about them and see the Day they come to Us

, he said: This is the Day of Resurrection, but as for this world, no. There was a veil over their eyes, and in their ears was a deafness in this world. Then when the Day of Resurrection came, they saw and heard, but they did not benefit. And he recited, “Our Lord, we have seen and heard, so return us [to the world]; we will do righteousness. Indeed, we are [now] certain.” (al-Sajdah 32:12) And His statement, But the wrongdoers today are in manifest error, God Almighty says: But the disbelievers who attributed to Him what is not of His description, and fabricated lies about Him today in this world, are in manifest error. He says: In straying from the path of truth, and taking a non-straight path, clearly deviating from the path of guidance and right direction, for whoever contemplates it and thinks about it, and is guided to the right path.

x: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: And warn, O Muhammad, these polytheists of the Day of their regret and remorse, for what they neglected in the side of God, and their dwellings in Paradise will be inherited by the people of faith in God and obedience to Him, and they will enter the dwellings of the people of faith in God from the Fire, and both groups will be certain of eternal life, and the life after which there is no death, so what regret and remorse. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Bashar told us: Abd al-Rahman bin Mahdi told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Salamah bin Kuhail, who said: Abu al-Zura’ told us, on the authority of Abdullah,
m: in a story he mentioned, who said: There is no soul but that it looks at a house in Paradise and a house in Hell, and it is the Day of Regret. The people of Hell will see the house that God had prepared for them if they had believed, and it will be said to them: If you had believed and done righteous deeds, this that you see in Paradise would have been yours, so regret will overtake them, and the people of Paradise will see the house that is in Hell, and it will be said: If God had not been gracious to you. Abu al-Sa’ib narrated:

c: Mu’awiyah narrated to us, on the authority of al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Abu Sa’id, who said:
m: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘Death will be brought on the Day of Resurrection and will be made to stand between Paradise and Hell like a white ram. It will be said: O people of Paradise, do you recognize this?’ They will look up and say: ‘Yes, this is death.’ It will be said: O people of Hell, do you recognize this?’ They will look up and say: ‘Yes, this is death.’ Then it will be ordered to be slaughtered. It will be said: O people of Paradise, eternal life and no death. O people of Hell, eternal life and no death.’ Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited: ‘
h
And warn them of the Day of Regret
h
when the matter is decided
while they are in heedlessness and they do not believe.’ And he pointed with his hand to the world.”

c: Ubayd ibn Asbat ibn Muhammad told me: My father told me, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah,
m: “On the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, regarding this verse: ‘
h
And warn them of the Day of Regret

,’ he said: ‘O people of Paradise, it will be called out, and they will stretch out their heads and look. Then it will be called out, ‘O people of the Fire,’ and they will stretch out their heads and look. Then it will be said: ‘Do you know death?’ He said: ‘And they will say: ‘No.’ He said: ‘Then death will be brought in the form of a white ram, and it will be said: ‘This is death.’ Then it will be taken and slaughtered. He said: ‘Then it will be called out, ‘O people of the Fire, eternity and no death.’ O people of Paradise, eternity and no death.’ He said: Then he recited: ‘
h
And warn them of the Day of Regret
when the matter has been decided.’”

c: Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj,
m: saying: Ibn Abbas said, regarding His statement,
h
And warn them of the Day of Regret

, he said: God will depict death in the form of a white ram, which will be slaughtered. He said: The people of Hell will despair of death, and will not hope for it, and regret will overtake them because of their eternal stay in Hell. In it also is the greatest terror, and the people of Paradise will be safe from death, and will not fear it. They will be safe from death, which is the greatest terror, because they will remain eternal in Paradise. Ibn Jurayj said: The people of Hell will be gathered when death is slaughtered and the two groups will watch, so that is His statement,
h
When the matter is decided
, he said: Death is slaughtered, while they are in heedlessness.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of his father, that he told him that
m: he heard Ubayd ibn Umair say in his al-Qasas 28:Death is brought as if it were a beast, and it is slaughtered while the people watch.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement,
h
And warn them of the Day of Regret
, he said: The Day of Resurrection, and he recited, That a soul may say, ‘Oh, how I regret what I neglected in my duty to God!’ (al-Zumar 39:56).

c: Ali told me, he said: Abdullah told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his statement,
h
And warn them of the Day of Regret is one of the names of the Day of Resurrection
. God has made it great and warned His servants about it. His statement,
h
When the matter is decided

means: When He has finished ruling for the people of Hell to remain there forever, and for the people of Paradise to remain there forever, by slaughtering death. His statement, And they are in heedlessness means: And these polytheists are in heedlessness of what God will do to them on the Day when they come to Him, emerging from their graves, by His immortality in Hell, and His inheriting their dwellings in Paradise to others. And they do not believe God, the Exalted, says: And they do not believe in the Resurrection and the Resurrection, and God’s recompense to them for their evil deeds, with what He has informed us that He will recompense them with.

x: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: Do not be saddened by the denial of these polytheists towards you, O Muhammad, regarding the truth that you have brought them, for to Us is their return and their destiny and the destiny of all creation except them, and We are the inheritors of the earth and all the people on it, through their annihilation from it, and its remaining without any owner other than Us, then upon Us is the reward of every worker among them for his work, when he returns to Us, the good among them for his good, and the evildoer for his evil.

God Almighty says to His Prophet: And mention, O Muhammad, in the Book of God, Abraham, the friend of the Most Merciful. So tell these polytheists his stories and the stories of his father. He was a truthful man. He says: He was one of the people of truthfulness in his speech, report, and promises. He did not lie. The truthful man is the active participle of truthfulness. We have already explained this, so there is no need to repeat it here. A prophet means: God had informed him and revealed to him.
And His saying,
h
When he said to his father
, he says: Remember
h
when he said to his father

, O my father, why do you worship that which does not hear? He says: What do you do by worshipping an idol that does not hear, nor see anything, nor avail you at all? He says: Nor ward off any harm from you, it is only a pictured image that neither harms nor benefits. He says: What do you do by worshipping something that has this description? Worship the One who, when you call upon Him, hears your call, and when you are surrounded, sees you and supports you, and when harm befalls you, He wards it off. The Arabists differed about the reason for the inclusion of the letter ha’ in the word ya abat O father.

Some of the grammarians of Basra used to say: If you stop on it, you say: ya abah O father, and it is a ha’ that was added, like when you say: ya ummah O mother, then you say: ya umm O mother if you connect it. However, since the word father has two letters, it was as if he had omitted it, so the ha’ became necessary, and the ya’ became as if it came after it. That is why they said: ya aba aqbal O father, come, and the ta’ was made for femininity. It is permissible to shorten the word from ya aba aqbal, because it is permissible to call what you add to yourself in meaning with a damma, like the Arabs say: ya rab ighfir li O Lord, forgive me, and you stop in the Qur’an: ya aba fi al-kitab O father, in the book. Some Arabs may stop on the ha’ with the ta’. Some grammarians of Kufa said: The ha’ with ‘aba’ and ‘ummah is a ha’ of pause. It became so common in their speech that it became like the ha’ of femininity.

They introduced the addition to it. Whoever asks for the addition, it is with the ta’ and nothing else, because you ask for the ya’ after it, and the ha’ then is only a ta’, like when you say: ya abat, and nothing else. Whoever says: ya abah, he is the one who stops with the ha’, because he does not ask for the ya’ after it. Whoever says: ya abat, he stops with the ta’, and it is permissible with the ha’. As for the ta’, it is because of the request for the alif of lamentation, so the ha’ became a ta’ for that reason. Stopping with the ha’ is far-fetched, except for whoever says: ya Umaimah, making this fathah from the fathah of tarkhīm, as if this is the end of the noun. He said: This is far-fetched.

God Almighty says: Abraham said to his father: O my father, God has given me knowledge that He has not given you, so follow me. He says: So accept my advice. I will guide you to a straight path. He says: I will show you the guidance of the straight path in which you will not go astray if you adhere to it, and it is the religion of God in which there is no crookedness.

God Almighty says: O my father, do not worship Satan. Indeed Satan has been disobedient to God. The disobedient is the one who disobeys, just as the knowledgeable is the one who has knowledge. Some Arabs have said: The disobedient is the one who disobeys, the knowledgeable is the one who knows, and they have cited as evidence for their statement the words of Tarif bin Tamim al-Anbari: Or whenever a tribe came to Ukaz, they would send to their chief to look for They said: Their chief said, meaning: their most knowledgeable person, and God knows best.

He says: O my father, I know that if you die worshipping Satan, he will afflict you with a punishment from the punishment of God. Then you will be a friend of Satan. He says: You will be a friend to him instead of God, and God will disown you, and you will perish. Fear in this context means knowledge, just as awe means knowledge, in His statement: So we feared that he would overburden them through transgression and disbelief. (al-Kahf 18:80)

God Almighty says: Abraham's father said to Abraham, when Abraham called him to worship God and abandon the worship of Satan, and to disavow idols and statues: Do you want to worship my gods, O Abraham? If you do not stop mentioning them badly,
h
I will stone you
. He says:
h
I will stone you
with words, and that is cursing and ugly speech. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Musa told us, he said: Amr told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, he said:
m: Do you reject my gods, O Abraham?
h
If you do not desist
h
I will stone you
with insults and words.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, he said:
m: Ibn Jurayj said, regarding his statement,
h
If you do not desist
h
I will stone you
, he said: By word, I will curse you.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid bin Sulayman told us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding his statement,
h
I will stone you
, meaning: I will stone the statement. As for his saying,
h
And leave me alone for a long time
, the people of interpretation differed in its interpretation.

x: Some of them said: The meaning of that is:
h
And leave me alone for a long time
and an age. And they directed the meaning of al-mulla to the term al-mulla of time, which is the long term of it.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Bashar told us: Abd al-Rahman told us: Abu Dawud told us: Muhammad bin Abi al-Waddah told us, on the authority of Abd al-Karim, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement,
h
And leave me alone for a long time
, he said: for an age.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, his statement for a while he said: for a while.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Al-Hasan:
m: h
And leave me alone for a long time
. He said for a long time.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us: Abd al-Razzaq told us: Muammar told us, on the authority of al-Hasan,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And leave me alone for a long time
, he said: A long time.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq:
m: h
And leave me alone for a long time
. He said: for an age. And age means a long time.

c: Ibn Bashar told us: Abd al-Rahman told us: Israel told us, on the authority of Abu Hasin, on the authority of Saeed ibn Jubayr:
m: h
And leave me alone for a long time
. He said: For a long time.

c: Musa told us, he said: Amr told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: h
And leave me alone for a long time
, he said: Forever.

x: Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is: Leave me alone, safe from my punishment of you. They attributed the meaning of full to the people’s saying: So-and-so is full of this matter, meaning that he is well-versed in it and rich in it. It is as if the meaning of the statement was, for them,: Leave me alone, and your honor is safe from my punishment, and your body is free from my harm.
Who said that?

c: Ali bin Dawud told me, he said: Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah bin Saleh told us, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talha, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: And avoid me completely, meaning: avoid me completely.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his statement,
h
And avoid me for a long time
, he said: Avoid me safely before a punishment befalls you from me.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement,
h
And leave me alone for a long time
, he said: Safely.

c: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: the same.

c: Ibn Bashar told us: Yahya bin Katheer bin Dirham Abu Ghassan told us: Qara bin Khalid told us, on the authority of Atiyah al-Jadali:
m: h
And leave me alone for a long time
. He said: Safely.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd told us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement,
h
And avoid me for a long time
: Avoid me in peace, so that no reproach will befall you because of me.

x: The more correct of the two opinions regarding the interpretation of the verse, in my opinion, is the opinion of the one who said: Its meaning is: And leave me alone, safe from my punishment, because it follows His saying:
h
If you do not desist
h
I will stone you

. This is a threat from Him to him if he does not desist from mentioning his gods in a bad way, that He will stone him with a bad word, and what is more appropriate to follow that is to come forward to Him by desisting from it before the punishment befalls him. As for the command to leave him for a long time, there is no basis for it.

God the Almighty says: Abraham said to his father when he threatened him with evil words and punishment for his advice to him and his calling to God: Peace be upon you, my father. He says: It is a security from me to you that I will not return to what you hate, and for calling to me what you threatened me with punishment for, but I will ask forgiveness for you from my Lord meaning: But I will ask my Lord to cover your sins by pardoning you from punishing you for them. He has been gracious to me meaning: I have known my Lord to be gracious to me, answering my call when I call upon Him. It is said from him: So-and-so was gracious to me. I have explained that with its evidence previously, so there is no need to repeat it here. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Ali told me, he said: Abdullah told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his statement,
h
He was kind to me
, meaning: gentle.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding his statement, Indeed,
h
He was kind to me
, he said: Indeed, He was gentle with me, for kind means gentle.

x: And His statement:
h
And I will withdraw from you and what you call upon besides God

means: And I will avoid you and what you call upon besides God of idols and statues And I will call upon my Lord means: And I will call upon my Lord, with sincere worship of Him and singling Him out as Lord Perhaps I will not be wretched in calling upon my Lord means: Perhaps I will not be wretched in calling upon my Lord, but He will answer my call and give me what I ask of Him.

God Almighty says: So when Abraham had withdrawn from his people and from the worship of what they used to worship besides God of idols, We relieved his loneliness from being separated from them, and We replaced him with someone better than them and more honored by God than them, so We gave him his son Isaac, and his grandson Jacob, son of Isaac. And each of them We made a prophet. He says: And We made them all, meaning by all Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, prophets. God Almighty said: And each of them We made a prophet. So He made it singular, and did not say prophets, to make the word each singular.

And We bestowed upon them of Our mercy. God Almighty says: And We provided for all of them, meaning Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, of Our mercy. And what He bestowed upon them of His mercy was what He expanded for them in this immediate world of His abundant provision, and He enriched them with His grace. And His statement: And We made for them a high reputation for truthfulness. God Almighty says: And We granted them good praise and beautiful mention from the people.

c: Ali told me, he said: Abdullah told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his statement: And We made for them a tongue of truth, high, meaning: good praise. And the Most High described the tongue that was made for them as high, because all people of religions praise them well, and the Arabs say: The tongue of so-and-so has come to me, meaning his praise or his blame? And from this is the statement of Amer bin Al-Harith: I have been given a tongue that I do not delight in, from its loftiness, neither astonishment nor mockery. It is narrated: There is no lying or mockery in it. She came as a translator, I would have been wary of her if pity and caution had been of any use to me. Translated: It is thought of.

x: God Almighty says to His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: And mention, O Muhammad, in Our Book which We revealed to you, Moses, son of Imran, and tell your people that he was sincere. The readers differed in their reading of this. The majority of the readers of Medina and Basra and some of the Kufians read it as inna kan khulus with a kasra on the lam of mukhlis, meaning: he was sincere in his worship to God, and singled Him out in divinity, without making any partner for Him in it. The majority of the readers of Kufa, except for Asim, read it as inna kan khulus with a fatha on the lam of mukhlis, meaning: God had sincerely chosen Moses for His message, and made him a prophet and messenger.

The correct statement in this regard, in my opinion, is that he, may God bless him and grant him peace, was sincere in his worship of God, sincere in his message and prophethood, so whichever of them the reader recites, he is correct. And he was a messenger means: And God was a messenger to his people, the Children of Israel, and the one to whom He sent him was a prophet.

evidence.text: The readers differed in their reading of this.

The majority of the readers of Medina and Basra and some of the Kufians read it as inna kan khulus with a kasra on the lam of mukhlis, meaning: he was sincere in his worship to God, and singled Him out in divinity, without making any partner for Him in it.

The majority of the readers of Kufa, except for Asim, read it as inna kan khulus with a fatha on the lam of mukhlis, meaning: God had sincerely chosen Moses for His message, and made him a prophet and messenger.

x: God Almighty says: And We called to Moses from the side of the mountain, meaning by the right, the right of Moses, because the mountain has no right or left, but rather it is as it is said: He stood to the right of the qiblah and to the left of it. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us: Abd al-Razzaq told us: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
From the right side of the Mount

, he said: The right side of the mountain. We have explained the meaning of the Mount and the differences of opinion among those who differed about it, and we have indicated the correct statement in what has passed, so there is no need to repeat it in this place. And His statement:
h
And We brought him near
, in private conversation, the Most High says:
h
And We brought him near

, in private conversation, just as one says: So-and-so is the companion of so-and-so and his drinking companion, or the friend of so-and-so and his companions. And He mentioned that God, the Most High, brought him near, until he heard the scratching of the pen.

x: Who said that?

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Yahya told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Ata’ ibn al-Sa’ib, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: h
And We brought him near for a private conversation
. He said: He brought him near until he heard the scratching of the pen.

c: Muhammad ibn Mansur al-Tusi told us: Yahya ibn Abi Bakr told us: Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, who said:
m: I think it was on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement:
h
And We brought him near for a private conversation

, he said: Between the fourth heaven, or he said: the seventh, and the Throne there are seventy thousand veils: a veil of light, a veil of darkness, a veil of light, and a veil of darkness. So he kept bringing Moses near until there was a veil between him and Him, and he heard the scratching of the pen. “He said: My Lord, show me, that I may look at You.” (al-A’raf 7:143) Ali bin Sahl told us:

c: Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Abu Jaafar, on the authority of Al-Rabi’, on the authority of Abu Al-Aaliyah, who said:
m: He brought him close to him until he heard the scratching of the pen.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Jarir told us, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Maysarah:
m: h
And We brought him near for a private conversation
. He said: He brought him near until he heard the scratching of the pen on the tablet. Shu’bah said: Gabriel, peace be upon him, accompanied him. Qatada said about this:

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us: Abd al-Razzaq told us: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And We brought him near for a private conversation
, he said: He was saved by his truthfulness.

x: And His statement:
h
And We bestowed upon him
, out of Our mercy, his brother Aaron, meaning: And We bestowed upon Moses, out of Our mercy, his brother Aaron, a prophet, meaning: We supported him with his prophethood and aided him with it.

c: As Yaqub told me, he said: Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Dawud, on the authority of Ikrimah, he said:
m: Ibn Abbas said, regarding his statement,
h
And We bestowed upon him
, out of Our mercy, his brother Aaron, a prophet, he said: Aaron was older than Moses, but he meant that He bestowed upon him his prophethood.

x: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: And mention, O Muhammad, in this Book, Ishmael, son of Abraham, and relate his story. Indeed, he did not lie about his promise, nor did he break it. But when he promised his Lord, or one of His servants, a promise, he fulfilled it.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj,
m: his statement:
h
He was true to his promise
, he said: He did not make a promise to his Lord without fulfilling it.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Amr ibn al-Harith told me that Sahl ibn Aqil told him that
m: Ismail, peace be upon him, promised a man a place to come to, but he came and the man forgot. Ismail stayed with him and spent the night until the man came the next day. He said: Have you not left here? He said: No. He said: I forgot. He said: I would not leave until you came. So he was truthful in that.

x: God Almighty says: And he used to enjoin his family to establish prayer and to give “zakat, and his work was acceptable to his Lord, praised for what his Lord had charged him with, not falling short in his obedience to Him.
God Almighty says: And mention, O Muhammad, in this Book of Ours, Idris. He was a man of truth, he did not tell lies, a prophet, to whom We revealed of Our command whatever We willed.
h
And We raised him to a high station
. It was mentioned that God raised him while he was alive to the fourth heaven. This is the meaning of His statement:
h
And We raised him to a high station
, meaning to a place of height and elevation.
Some of them said: He was raised to the sixth heaven.
Others said: The fourth.
The novel mentioned that:

c: Yunus bin Abdul A'la told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Jarir bin Hazim told me, on the authority of Sulayman Al-A'mash, on the authority of Shammar bin Atiyah, on the authority of Hilal bin Yasaf, who said:
m: Ibn Abbas asked Ka'b while I was present, and he said to him: What is the saying of God the Almighty to Idris,
h
And We raised him to a high station

? Ka'b said: As for Idris, God revealed to him: I will raise for you every day the equivalent of the deeds of all the children of Adam, so I would like you to increase your deeds. Then a close friend of his from the angels came to him and said: God revealed to me such and such, so the Angel of Death spoke to me, so let him delay me until I increase my deeds. So he carried him between his wings, then he headed with him to the heaven. When he was in the fourth heaven, the Angel of Death met him descending and spoke to the Angel of Death about what Idris had spoken to him about. He said: Where is Idris? He said: He is on my back. The Angel of Death said: It is amazing that I was sent to take the soul of Idris in the fourth heaven, and I kept saying: How can I take his soul in the fourth heaven while he is on earth? So his soul was taken there, and that is what God Almighty said:
h
And We raised him to a high station

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us
And Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, his statement:
h
And We raised him to a high station
, he said: Idris was raised and did not die, just as Isa was raised.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same, except that he said: And he did not die.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: h
And We raised him to a high station
. He said: He was raised to the sixth heaven, and he died there.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid bin Sulayman told us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement,
h
And We raised him to a high station
, that Idris was overtaken by death in the sixth heaven.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Abd al-Rahman told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: h
And We raised him to a high station
, he said: the fourth heaven.

c: Abu Kuraib told us: Ibn Yaman told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Abu Harun al-Abdi, on the authority of Abu Saeed al-Khudri:
m: h
And We raised him to a high station

. He said: In the fourth heaven. Ali bin Suhayl narrated: Hajjaj narrated: Abu Jaʿfar al-Razi narrated: Ar-Rabiʿ bin Anas narrated: Abu al-ʿAliyah al-Riyahi narrated: Abu Hurayrah or someone else - Abu Jaʿfar al-Razi was not sure - said: When the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was taken on the Night Journey, Gabriel ascended with him to the fourth heaven. He asked to be admitted and it was said: Who is this? He said: Gabriel. They said: And who is with him? He said: Muhammad. They said: Has he been sent to? He said: Yes. They said: May God give him life, he is a brother and a successor. What a good brother, what a good successor, and what a good coming he has been. He said: So he entered and saw a man. He said: This is Idris, may God raise him to a high station.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement,
h
And We raised him to a high station
, he said: Anas bin Malik told us that the Prophet of God was told that when he was taken up to heaven, he said: I came upon Idris in the fourth heaven.

x: The Almighty says to His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: These are the ones whose report I have related to you in this Surah, O Muhammad, whom God has blessed with His guidance, so He guided them to the path of righteousness from the prophets from the descendants of Adam, and from the descendants of those whom We carried with Noah in the ark, and from the descendants of Abraham, the friend of the Most Merciful, and from the descendants of Israel, and from those whom We guided to believe in God and to work in obedience to Him and chose, He says: And from those whom We have chosen and selected for Our message and revelation, so the one who is meant from the descendants of Adam is Idris, and the one who is meant from the descendants of those whom We carried with Noah is Abraham, and the one who is meant from the descendants of Abraham is Isaac, Jacob, and Ishmael, and the one who is meant from the descendants of Israel is Moses, Aaron, Zachariah, Jesus, and his mother Mary, and for this reason the Almighty differentiated their lineages even though He gathers them all with Adam because among them is one who was not from the offspring of the one who was with Noah in the ark, and he is Idris, and Idris is the grandfather of Noah.

And the saying of the Most High, When the verses of the Most Gracious are recited to them, meaning: When the proofs and arguments of God that He sent down to them in His books are recited to these prophets whom God has blessed, they fall down in prostration to God, in submission to Him, humility, obedience to His command, and obedience, and weeping, meaning: They fall down in prostration while weeping. Weeping is the plural of weeping, just as ‘ati is the plural of ‘ata, and ‘jathi is the plural of jaath, so it is pluralized and it is fa’ul, just as al-qa’id qu’udan and al-jalis jilusan make it plural. The analogy would have been: and they wept and ‘atwaan, but the waw was disliked after the damma, so it was changed to a ya’, just as it was said in the plural of dalū adlā, and li the plural of bahu abah, and the origin of that is af’al adlu and abhu, so the waw was changed to a ya’ because it came after the damma due to its being too heavy.

And there are two widespread dialects for that, and scholars of the reciters of the Qur’an have recited each one of them: they wept and ‘atwaan with the damma, and bkiyan and ‘atyaan with the kasra. It may be possible that crying is crying itself.

c: Ibn Bashar told us: Abd al-Rahman told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of al-A’mash, on the authority of Ibrahim, who said:
m: Umar ibn al-Khattab recited Surah Maryam and prostrated and said: This is the prostration, but where is the weeping? He meant: Where is the weeping?

evidence.text: And there are two widespread dialects for that, and scholars of the reciters of the Qur’an have recited each one of them: they wept and ‘atwaan with the damma, and bkiyan and ‘atyaan with the kasra.

x: God Almighty says: Then after those whom I mentioned of the prophets upon whom I bestowed favor, and whose characteristics I described in this surah, there occurred an evil successor who left them on the earth and neglected the prayer. Then the people of interpretation differed regarding the description of their wasting the prayer.
Some of them said: Their wasting it was their delaying it from its appointed times and their wasting its times.
Who said that?

c: Ali bin Saad Al-Kindi told me: Isa bin Yunus told us, on the authority of Al-Awza’i, on the authority of Musa bin Sulayman, on the authority of Al-Qasim bin Mukhaymara,
m: regarding his statement,
h
Then there came after them a generation who neglected the prayer
, he said: They only neglected the times, and if it had been abandonment, it would have been disbelief.

c: Ishaq bin Zaid Al-Khattabi told us: Al-Faryabi told us, on the authority of Al-Awza’i, on the authority of Al-Qasim bin Mukhaimira,
m: something similar.

c: Abdul Karim bin Abi Umair told us: Al-Walid bin Muslim told me, on the authority of Abu Amr, on the authority of Al-Qasim bin Mukhaimira, who said:
m: They lost the timings, and if they had abandoned them, they would have become infidels because of their abandonment.

c: Yunus bin Abdul A’la told me: Al-Walid bin Muslim told us, on the authority of Al-Awza’i, on the authority of Al-Qasim,
m: something similar. Al-Qasim narrated: Al-Husayn narrated: Isa narrated: Al-Awza’i narrated: Ibrahim bin Yazid narrated: Umar bin Abdul Aziz sent a man to Egypt on an urgent matter for the Muslims. He went out to his guards, and he had previously instructed them not to stand up if they saw him. They made room for him, and he sat among them and said: Who among you knows the man we sent to Egypt? They said: We all know him. He said: Let the youngest of you stand up and leave him. The messenger came to him and said: Do not hurry me, I will tighten my clothes on myself. He came to him and said: Today is Friday, so do not leave until you pray. We have sent you on an urgent matter for the Muslims, so do not hurry what we have sent you for by delaying the prayer from its appointed time, for you will inevitably pray it. Then he recited: “
h
Then there came after them a generation who neglected prayer and pursued desires
. So they are going to meet with error.” Then he said: Their waste was not abandoning it, but they wasted time.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us: My father told us, on the authority of Al-Mas’udi, on the authority of Al-Qasim bin Abd Al-Rahman and Al-Hasan bin Mas’oud, on the authority of Ibn Mas’oud,
m: that it was said to him: God mentions prayer frequently in the Qur’an: Those who are heedless of their prayers and are constant in their prayers and maintain their prayers. Ibn Mas’oud, may God be pleased with him, said: At its appointed times. They said: We only saw that as neglect. He said: That is disbelief.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Omar Abu Hafs Al-Abar told us, on the authority of Mansour bin Al-Mu'tamir, he said: Masruq said:
m: No one maintains the five prayers, so he is recorded among the heedless, and in their excess is destruction, and their excess is: wasting them from their time. And others said: Rather, their wasting them is: abandoning them.

x: Who said that?

c: Yunus bin Abdul A’la told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Abu Sakhr told us, on the authority of Al-Qurazi, that he said
m: regarding this verse,
h
Then there came after them a generation who neglected prayer and pursued desires
, meaning: they abandoned prayer.

x: The most correct of the two interpretations of this, in my opinion, is the interpretation of the verse, which says: Their wasting it means their abandoning it, because the statement of God, the Most High, after it indicates that this is the case, and that is His statement, the Most High: Except for those who repent, believe, and do righteous deeds. So if those whom He described as having wasted it were believers, He would not have excluded from them those who believed and were believers, but they were disbelievers who did not pray to God or perform any obligatory prayer for Him, and they were wicked who preferred their own desires over obeying God. It has been said: Those whom God described with this description are people from this nation who will be at the end of time.

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: all on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, “
h
Then there came after them a posterity who neglected prayer and pursued desires

. So they are going to meet with destruction.” He said: When the Hour comes and the righteous people of the nation of Muhammad (peace and blessings of God be upon him) go, they will seduce one another in the alleys. Muhammad ibn Amr said: Adultery. Al-Harith said: Adulterers.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: similarly, and he said: Adultery, Surat Maryam 19:59
h
Then there came after them a posterity who neglected prayer and pursued desires
. So they are going to meet with perdition. as Ibn Amr said.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Abu Tamila told us, on the authority of Abu Hamza, on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of Ikrimah,
m: Mujahid, and Ata’ bin Abi Rabah, Then there succeeded them a generation the verse, he said: They are the nation of Muhammad.

c: Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Ashib told us, he said: Sharik told us, on the authority of Abu Tamim bin Muhajir,
m: regarding the statement of God:
h
Then there came after them a generation who neglected the prayer

, he said: They are in this nation, they swarm like cattle and donkeys on the roads, they do not fear God in the heavens, nor do they feel shy of people on the earth. As for his saying, They will encounter Ghayān, it means that these successors who came after those prophets whom God bestowed His blessings upon will enter Ghayān, which is the name of a valley in Hell, or the name of a well in it.

c: Abbas bin Abi Talib told me, he said: Muhammad bin Ziyad bin Razan told us, he said: Sharqi bin Qatami told us, on the authority of Luqman bin Amir Al-Khuza’i, he said:
m: I came to Abu Umamah Siddi bin Ajlan Al-Bahili, and I said: Tell us a hadith that you heard from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. He said: So he called for food, then he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: If a rock weighing ten ounces were thrown from the edge of Hell, it would not reach its bottom for fifty autumns, then it would end in Ghayyah and Atham. He said: I said: What is Ghayyah and Atham? He said: Two wells at the bottom of Hell in which the pus of the people of Hell flows, and they are the two that God mentioned in His Book: “They neglected the prayer and followed their desires. So they are going to meet Ghayyah,” and His saying in al-Furqan 25:And they do not commit adultery, and whoever does that will meet sin.

c: Muhammad bin Bashar told us: Amr bin Asim told us: Al-Mu’tamir bin Sulayman told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Abu Ayoub, on the authority of Abdullah bin Amr:
m: Then they will meet Ghayyan meaning: a valley in Hell.

c: Muhammad bin Bashar told us: Abd al-Rahman told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Abu Ubaidah, on the authority of Abdullah:
m: h
Then they will meet with error
. He said: A valley in the Fire.

c: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told us: Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar told us: Shuʿbah told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Abu Ubaydah, on the authority of Abdullah, that he said
m: regarding this verse,
h
Then they will meet with error
. He said: A river in Hell, foul-tasting and deep in the bottom.

c: Muhammad bin Ubaid Al-Maharbi told me: Abu Al-Ahwas told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Abu Ubaidah, on the authority of his father,
m: regarding his statement, “
h
Then there came after them a generation who neglected prayer and pursued desires
. So they are going to meet with error.” He said: Error is the river of Hell in the Fire, in which those who followed desires are tormented.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Abu Al-Ahwas told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Abu Ubaidah, on the authority of his father,
m: regarding his statement, “
h
Then there came after them a posterity who neglected prayer and pursued desires
. So they are going to meet with error.” He said: Error is the river of Hell in the Fire, in which those who followed desires are tormented.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Abu Al-Ahwas told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Abu Ubaidah, on the authority of Abdullah,
m: They neglected the prayer and followed desires, so they are going to meet with error. He said: A river in the Fire into which those who followed desires will be thrown.

x: Others said: Rather, what I meant in this context is: loss.
Who said that?

c: Ali told me, he said: Abdullah told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his statement,
h
Then they will meet with error
, meaning: loss.

x: Others said: Rather, he meant evil.
Who said that?

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement,
h
Then they will meet with error
, he said: Error means evil, and from it is the saying of the poet: Whoever finds good, people praise him for his actions, and whoever goes astray will not lack someone to blame him for his error.

x: All of these sayings have similar meanings, and that is that whoever visits the two wells mentioned by the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the valley mentioned by Ibn Masʿud in Hell, and enters that, will encounter loss and evil, and that is enough evil for him.

God the Almighty says: Then these evil successors whose description He described will encounter error, except for those who repent and review the command of God, and believe in Him and His Messenger, and do righteous deeds, meaning: and obey God in what He commanded and forbade, and perform His obligations, and avoid what He has forbidden, for those will enter Paradise, meaning: for those among them in particular will enter Paradise, not those who perished among them due to their disbelief, and their neglect of prayer, and their following of desires. And His statement, and they will not be wronged at all, meaning: and they will not be reduced in the reward for their deeds at all, and they will not be included with those of the evil successors who perished before their repentance from their misguidance, and before their return to obeying their Lord in Hell, but they will enter as the people of faith.
God the Most High says: Then those will enter Paradise,
h
Gardens of Eden
. His saying
h
Gardens of Eden is an accusative translation of Paradise
. What He means by His saying
h
Gardens of Eden

: gardens of residence. I have explained that previously with its evidence that suffices from repeating it. And His saying which the Most Gracious has promised His servants in the unseen means: These gardens are the gardens which the Most Gracious has promised His believing servants that they will enter in the unseen, because they have not seen them or witnessed them, so they are unseen to them. And His saying Indeed, His promise was fulfilled means, Almighty God the Most High: God's promise was, and His promise in this place is His promise, and it is Paradise that is coming, and His friends and those who obey Him will come to it, whom God will admit into it.

Some of the grammarians of Kufa said: The report came out on the basis that the promise is what is coming, and its meaning is: that it is the one who will come, and he did not say: and his promise was coming, because everything that comes to you, you come to it. And he said: Do you not see that you say: I came upon fifty years, and fifty years came upon me, and all of that is correct. And I have explained the statement about it, and the ha’ in his saying that it is from the mention of the Most Gracious.

God Almighty says: Those who enter Paradise will not hear therein any idle talk, which is guidance and falsehood of speech and talk, “except peace.” This is from the disconnected exception, and its meaning is: But they will hear peace, which is the angels’ greeting to them. And His statement,
h
And they will have their provision therein

, morning and evening, means: And they will have their food and whatever they desire of food and drink in the amount of time in the morning and the amount of time in the evening of the days of this world. Rather, He means that what is between their lunch and their dinner in Paradise is the amount of time between one of us in this world and his dinner, and likewise what is between dinner and lunch, because there is no night or day in Paradise, and this is like His statement, He created the earth in two days and He created the heavens and the earth in six days, meaning by that: of the days of this world.

c: Ali bin Sahl told us: Al-Walid bin Muslim told us:
m: I asked Zuhair bin Muhammad about the statement of God:
h
And they will have their provision therein

, morning and evening. He said: There is no night in Paradise. They will be in light forever, and they will have the amount of night and day. They will know the amount of night by the lowering of the veils and the closing of the doors, and they will know the amount of day by the raising of the veils and the opening of the doors.

c: Ali told us, he said: Al-Walid told us, on the authority of Khalid, on the authority of Al-Hasan,
m: and he mentioned the gates of Paradise, and he said: Gates whose exterior can be seen from their interior, so speak and speak, and they whisper, Open and close, and you do.

c: Ibn Harb told me: Musa bin Ismail told us: Amer bin Yassaf told us, on the authority of Yahya, who said:
m: The Arabs in their time, if they had dinner and lunch, that was a comfort to them. So God revealed:
h
And they will have their provision therein
, morning and evening: the amount of time between your lunch in this world and your evening.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us: Abd al-Razzaq told us: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement,
h
And they will have their provision therein
, morning and evening, he said: When one of the Arabs had lunch and dinner, he was amazed, so God informed them that they would have in Paradise morning and evening, the amount of lunch and dinner.

c: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Al-Thawri told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, he said:
m: It is not morning or evening, but they will be given it according to what they desired in this world.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement,
h
And they will have their provision therein
, morning and evening, there are two hours in it, morning and evening, for that is for them, there is no night, but rather it is light and brightness.

x: God Almighty says: This Paradise, whose description I have described to you, O people, is the Paradise that we will inherit. He says: We will inherit the dwellings of the people of Hell in it. Among Our servants is he who was righteous. He says: he who was fearful of God’s punishment by performing His obligations and avoiding His sins.

It was mentioned that this verse was revealed because the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was slow to receive the revelation from Gabriel. I mentioned some of the narration, and we will mention, God willing, the rest of what we have prepared to mention that we did not mention before.

Who said that? Abu Kuraib narrated: Abdullah narrated: Abdullah bin Abaan Al-Ajli, Qubaysah and Wakee’ narrated: Sufyan bin Wakee’ narrated: My father narrated: All of them on the authority of Umar bin Dhir: I heard my father mention on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, that Muhammad said to Gabriel: What prevents you from visiting us more often than you visit us? Then this verse was revealed: “
h
And we do not descend except by the command of your Lord
. To Him belongs what is before us and what is behind us and what is in between. And your Lord is not forgetful.” He said: This is the answer to Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace.

c: Muhammad bin Muammar told me: Abdul Malik bin Amr told us: Omar bin Dhir told us: My father told me, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to Gabriel: What prevents you from visiting us more often than you do? Then the verse was revealed: We do not descend except by the command of your Lord.

c: Muhammad ibn Saʿd told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn ʿAbbas,
m: regarding his statement,
h
And we do not descend except by the command of your Lord to And your Lord is not forgetful

. He said: Gabriel was delayed from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was distressed by that and was saddened, so Gabriel came to him and said: O Muhammad, “
h
And we do not descend except by the command of your Lord
. To Him belongs what is before us and what is behind us and what is in between. And your Lord is not forgetful.”

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us: Abd al-Razzaq told us: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada, who said:
m: Gabriel was away from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and it seemed as if the Prophet was slow to see him. When he came to him, Gabriel said to him: We do not descend except by the command of your Lord verse.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
And we do not descend except by the command of your Lord

. To Him belongs what is before us and what is behind us.” He said: This is what Gabriel said. Gabriel was delayed in some of the revelation, so the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: You did not come until I missed you. Gabriel said to him: “
h
And we do not descend except by the command of your Lord
. To Him belongs what is before us and what is behind us.”

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: all of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding the statement of God Almighty, And We do not descend except by the command of your Lord, he said: The statement of the angels when Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, asked them to pray, is like that in the forenoon.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Husayn told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, he said:
m: Gabriel stayed away from Muhammad for twelve nights, and they were saying: Say something. So when he came to him, he said: O Gabriel, you have pitied me so much that the polytheists have suspected every suspicion. Then the verse was revealed: “
h
And we do not descend except by the command of your Lord
h
To Him belongs what is before us and what is behind us and what is between
that. And your Lord is not forgetful.”

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh, who said: Ubayd narrated to us, who said: I heard Ad-Dahhak say regarding His statement,
h
And we do not descend except by the command of your Lord

, that He was held back from the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, until the polytheists spoke about that, and that was difficult for the Prophet of God, so Gabriel came to him and said: Our being held back from you is difficult for you, and the polytheists speaking about that, but I am only the servant of God and His Messenger, if He commands me to do something I obey Him.
h
And we do not descend except by the command of your Lord
, meaning: by the word of your Lord. Then the people of interpretation differed in the interpretation of his saying,
h
To Him belongs what is before us and what is behind us and what is between
