that.

x: Some of them said: By his saying, what is before us, he means the world, and by his saying, what is behind us, he means the Hereafter, and what is between that, the two blasts.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Hakam told us, on the authority of Abu Jaʿfar, on the authority of al-Rabiʿ:
m: For Him belongs what is before us, meaning the world, and what is behind us, the Hereafter, and what is between that, the two trumpets.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Abu Jaʿfar, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ, on the authority of Abu Al-ʿAliyah, he said:
m: What is before us of this world, and what is behind us of the matter of the Hereafter, and what is between that between the two blasts.

x: Others said: What is before us is the Hereafter, what is behind us is this world, and what is between that is between this world and the Hereafter.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: Before us is the Hereafter and what is behind us of this world.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: To Him belongs what is before us of the matter of the Hereafter, and what is behind us of the matter of this world, and what is between that between this world and the Hereafter, and your Lord is not forgetful.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us: Abd al-Razzaq told us: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: He has what is before us of the Hereafter, and what is behind us of this world, and what is between that between the two blasts.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd told us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement, what is before us of the Hereafter, and what is behind us of the world.

x: Others said about this:

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj,
m: What is before us he said: What has passed before us of this world, and what is behind us what will come after us of this world and the Hereafter, and what is between that he said: What is between what has passed before them and what will come after them.

x: Some of the Arab scholars from Basra interpreted this to mean what is before us before we were created, what is behind us after annihilation, and what is between that when we were.

The most correct of the sayings on this matter is the saying of the one who said: Its meaning is: He has what is before us of the matter of the Hereafter, because that has not come and has come, so it is before them. For the most common usage of people when they say this matter is before you, is that they mean what has not come and has come, so we said: That is more correct. And what we have left behind of the matter of this world, that is what they left behind and it has passed, so it became behind them by their leaving it behind. And likewise the Arabs say about what a person has passed and what he has left behind, it is behind him and behind him, and what is between that: what is between what has not passed of the matter of this world and the Hereafter, because that is what is between those two times. We said: This is the most appropriate interpretation for it, because this is the most apparent and most likely interpretation, and the interpretation of the Qur’an is based on the most likely of its meanings, unless something prevents it from being accepted.

So ponder the statement: Do not be impatient, O Muhammad, for us to be late with you, for we do not descend from the heaven to the earth except by the command of your Lord to descend to it. To God belongs whatever is new of the affairs of the Hereafter that have not yet come and are coming, and whatever has passed and we have left behind of the affairs of this world, and what is between this time and the Day of Resurrection, in His hand is all that, and He is its Owner and Disposer, and none possesses that but Him, so it is not for us to invent a matter in His authority except by His command to us. And your Lord is not forgetful means: And your Lord is not forgetful, so my descent to you is delayed by His forgetting you, rather He is the One from whom nothing in the heaven or on the earth is hidden, so blessed and exalted is He, but He is the Most Knowing of what He manages and decrees in His creation, may His praise be glorified.
And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the Surat Maryam 19:64 And We do not descend except by the command of your Lord.
h
To Him belongs what is before us and what is behind us and what is between
that. And your Lord is not forgetful. people of interpretation said.
Who said that?

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: And your Lord is not forgetful. He said: Your Lord has not forgotten you.

x: God the Most High says: Your Lord, O Muhammad, is not the Lord of the heavens and the earth and what is between them, because if He had been forgotten, that would not have been right, and he would have perished had it not been for His preservation of him. So the Lord is raised in response to His saying, your Lord. And His saying, Worship Him, means: So adhere to His obedience, and submit to His commands and prohibitions. And be patient in His worship, means: And make yourself patient in carrying out His commands and prohibitions, and working in His obedience, and you will win His pleasure with you, for He is the God who has no equal, no equal, and no likeness in His goodness, generosity, and grace.
h
Do you know of anyone similar to Him

? He says: Do you know, O Muhammad, that this Lord whom We have commanded you to worship, and to be patient in obeying Him, has an example in His generosity and munificence, so you worship Him hoping for His grace and bounty without Him?
No, that does not exist. And in a similar manner to what we said in interpreting that, the people of interpretation said.
Who said that?

c: Ali told me, he said: Abdullah told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his statement,
h
Do you know of anyone similar to Him
? means: Do you know of an example or likeness for the Lord?

c: Saeed bin Othman Al-Tanukhi told me: Ibrahim bin Mahdi told us, on the authority of Ibad bin Awam, on the authority of Shu’bah, on the authority of Al-Hasan bin Amara, on the authority of a man, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement,
h
Do you know of anyone similar to Him
? He said: Someone similar.

c: Yahya bin Ibrahim Al-Masoudi told me: My father told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of his grandfather, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding this verse:
h
Do you know of anyone similar to Him
? He said:
h
Do you know of anyone similar to Him
? Do you know of an example for Him, blessed and exalted be He.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement,
h
Do you know of anyone with a similar name

? God has no similar name nor is He equal to Him. All of His creation acknowledges Him and admits that He is their Creator, and knows that. Then he recites this verse, And if you ask them, ‘Who created them?’ they will surely say, ‘God.’

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj,
m: regarding his statement,
h
Do you know of anyone similar to Him
? He said: He says: He has no partner or equal.

evidence.text: Then he recites this verse, And if you ask them, ‘Who created them?’ they will surely say, ‘God.’

x: God Almighty says: And man says, the disbeliever who does not believe in resurrection after death: I will be brought out alive so that I may be resurrected after death, after affliction and annihilation! Denying that.

God Almighty says, Does not man remember? The one who is amazed by this denial of God's ability to revive him after his annihilation, and to bring him into existence after his nonexistence in the creation of himself, that God created him before his death, and created him as a perfect human being from nothing, and he was not before his creation of him, a thing. So he takes that into consideration and knows that the One who created him from nothing is not incapable of bringing him back to life after his death, and bringing him into existence after his annihilation. The reciters differed in their reading of the statement: Or does man not remember?

Some of the reciters of Medina and Kufa read it: Or does he not remember with a light dhal. The majority of the reciters of Kufa, Basra and Hijaz read it as or does he not remember with a shaddah on the dhal and the kaf, meaning: or does he not remember. The shaddah is more pleasing to me, although the other is permissible, because the meaning of that is: or does he not think and consider.

evidence.text: The reciters differed in their reading of the statement: Or does man not remember?
Some of the reciters of Medina and Kufa read it: Or does he not remember with a light dhal.
The majority of the reciters of Kufa, Basra and Hijaz read it as or does he not remember with a shaddah on the dhal and the kaf, meaning: or does he not remember.

x: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: By your Lord, O Muhammad, We will surely gather those who say: When we die, will we indeed be brought out alive on the Day of Resurrection from their graves, joined by their allies from among the devils?
h
Then We will surely bring them around Hell
on their knees. Al-Jathi is the plural of al-Jathi.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Then We will surely bring them around Hell
, kneeling, meaning: sitting, and it is like his statement: And you will see every nation kneeling.

x: God Almighty says, Then We will take from every group of them the most rebellious and obstinate against God, and We will begin with them. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Abd al-Rahman told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Ali ibn al-Aqmar, on the authority of Abu al-Ahwas,
m: Then We will extract
h
from every sect
those of them who are most rebellious against the Most Merciful. He said: We will begin with the greatest, then the greatest in crime.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Then We will surely extract from every sect those of them who were most rebellious against the Most Merciful
, meaning: those of them who were most disobedient to the Most Merciful, which is disobeying Him in polytheism.

c: Ali told me, he said: Abdullah told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his statement:
h
Which of them is most rebellious against the Most Merciful
? means: disobedient.
Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us.

c: And Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: all of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, his statement:
h
From every sect
he said: A nation. And his statement: obstinate he said: disbelief.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same, and Ibn Jurayj added to it: So we will begin with them.

x: The Shiites are the group who cooperate in a matter. It is said of this: the people cooperated, if they cooperated, and from this is their saying to the brave man: he is a Shiite, meaning he is a supporter, so the meaning of the statement is: then we will extract from every group that cooperated in disbelief in God, the most rebellious of them against God, and we will begin by burning him in Hell. And the word shi’i in other than this place means: division? And from this is the statement of God the Almighty: And they were sects meaning: groups, and from this is the statement of Ibn Mas’ud or Sa’d: I hate to come to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he says: I have divided my nation. Meaning: I have divided.
The Almighty says: Then We know better than those whom We remove from every sect who are most deserving of severe punishment and most deserving of great chastisement.
It was mentioned on the authority of Ibn Jurayj that he used to say about this:

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj:
m: Then We are most knowing of those who are most deserving of it to be burned. He said: Those most deserving of eternal damnation in Hell.

x: What Ibn Jurayj said is a meaningless statement, because God, the Most High, mentioned that those whom He removes from every sect of the infidels are the most severe in disbelief, and there is no doubt that there is no disbeliever in God except that he will abide eternally in the Fire, so there is no reason, and all of them will abide eternally in Hell, for it to be said: Then We know best those who are more deserving of eternal life than these immortals, but the meaning of that is what we mentioned, and it may be possible that it means: Then We know best those who are more deserving of some of the levels of Hell, salaan. As-Sali is the infinitive of salita tasalla salaan, and as-Sali is faʿul, but its waw was changed to a ya’ and was assimilated into the ya’ that comes after it, which is the lam of the verb, so it became a shaddah ya’.

God Almighty says: There is not one of you, O people, but will pass over to Hell. It was incumbent upon your Lord, O Muhammad, that they should pass over to it, a decree already decreed. He has decreed that and made it obligatory in the Mother of the Book. Scholars differed about the meaning of the word Wurood that God mentioned in this place.
Some of them said: Entering.
Who said that?
Al-Hasan bin Yahya narrated: Abd al-Razzaq narrated: Ibn Uyaynah narrated on the authority of Amr:

c: Someone told me that
m: heard Ibn Abbas arguing with Nafi’ bin al-Azraq. Ibn Abbas said: Wurood means entering. Nafi’ said: No. Ibn Abbas recited: “Indeed, you and what you worship besides God are fuel for Hell. You will be entering it.” Was he entering it or not? And he said: He will precede his people on the Day of Resurrection and lead them into the Fire, and wretched is the place to be entered. Was he entering it or not? As for you and I, we will enter it, so see if we will emerge from it or not. And I do not see that God will bring you out of it by denying you.” Nafi’ laughed. Al-Qasim narrated: Al-Husayn narrated: Hajjaj narrated: On the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ata’ ibn Abi Rabah, who said: Abu Rashid Al-Haruri said: They mentioned this and Al-Haruri said: They do not hear its hissing. Ibn Abbas said: Woe to you, are you crazy? Where is the saying of God Almighty: He will precede his people on the Day of Resurrection and will lead them into the Fire - and wretched is the place they are led to, “And We will drive the criminals to Hell in droves,” and His saying:
h
And there is not one of you but will pass over it

, and by God, if the supplication of those who have passed away was: O God, take me out of the Fire unharmed and admit me into Paradise victorious. Ibn Jurayj said: He says: The arrivals that God mentioned in the Qur’an: the entrance, so that every righteous and wicked person may enter it in the Qur’an, four arrivals: Then He will lead them into the Fire, “And gravel of Hell, you will be entering it,” And We will drive the criminals to Hell in droves, and His saying:
h
And there is not one of you but will pass over it

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement: “
h
And there is not one of you but will pass over it

: this is upon your Lord an inevitability decreed.” He knows the righteous and the wicked. Have you not heard the statement of God Almighty to Pharaoh: He will precede his people on the Day of Resurrection and will lead them into the Fire, and wretched is the place they are led to. And He said: And We will drive the criminals to Hell, in droves. So He called entering the Fire entering, not going out.

c: Al-Hasan bin Arafa told us: Marwan bin Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Bakkar bin Abi Marwan, on the authority of Khalid bin Ma’dan, who said:
m: The people of Paradise said after they entered Paradise: Did not our Lord promise us to pass through the Fire? He said: You passed by it while it was extinguished. Ibn Arafa said: Marwan bin Muawiyah said: Bakkar bin Abi Marwan said, or he said: solid.

c: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told us: Marhum ibn Abd al-Aziz told us: Abu Imran al-Joni told us, on the authority of Abu Khalid, who said:
m: The earth will be a fire one day, so what have you prepared for it? He said: That is what God said: “
h
And there is not one of you but will pass over it
: this is upon your Lord an inevitability decreed. Then We will save those who feared God and leave the wrongdoers therein on their knees.”

c: Yaqub ibn Ibrahim told me, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Al-Jariry, on the authority of Abu Al-Saleel, on the authority of Ghanim ibn Qays, he said:
m: They mentioned the arrival of the Fire, so Ka’b said: The Fire will be held by the people as if it were the back of a sack, until the feet of all creatures, both the righteous and the wicked, will be level on it. Then a crier will call out to it: Hold back your companions, and leave my companions. He said: Then every guardian of it will be swallowed up, and it knows them better than a man knows his own son, and the believers will emerge with their bodies fresh. He said: And Ka’b said: From what is between the shoulders of the treasurer of its treasurers is a year’s journey, with each one of them is a column with two branches, with which he pushes, and with it seven hundred thousand will be thrown into the Fire.

c: Abu Kuraib told us: Ibn Yaman told us, on the authority of Malik ibn Mughul, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, who said:
m: Whenever Abu Maysarah went to bed, he would say: I wish my mother had not given birth to me. Then he would cry. It was said: What makes you cry, Abu Maysarah? He said: He told us that we were entering it, but he did not tell us that we were leaving it.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Hakam told us, on the authority of Ismail, on the authority of Qais, who said:
m: Abdullah bin Rawaha cried during his illness, and his wife cried too. He said: What makes you cry? She said: I saw you crying, so I cried too. Ibn Rawaha said: I know that I will enter Hell, but I do not know whether I will be saved from it or not.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Abu Amr Dawud bin Al-Zubayr told us, he said:
m: I heard Al-Suddi mentioning on the authority of Marra Surat Maryam 19:71
h
And there is not one of you but will pass over it
. This is upon your Lord an inevitability decreed. Al-Hamadani, on the authority of Ibn Masoud,
h
And there is not one of you but will pass over it
, he said: enter it.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And there is not one of you but will pass over it
, he said: He will enter it.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us: Abd al-Razzaq told us, on the authority of Ibn Uyaynah, on the authority of Ismail bin Abi Khalid, on the authority of Qais bin Abi Hazim, who said:
m: Abdullah bin Rawahah had his head on his wife’s lap, and he cried, so his wife cried. He said: What makes you cry? She said: I saw you crying, so I cried. He said: I remembered the words of God,
h
There is not one of you but will pass over it
, and I do not know whether I will be saved from it or not.

x: Others said: Rather, it is bitter.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
And there is not one of you but will pass over it
, meaning Hell, which people will pass over.

c: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And there is not one of you but will pass over it
, he said: He is the one who passes by it.

c: Khallad bin Aslam told us: An-Nadr told us: Israel told us: Abu Ishaq told us, on the authority of Abu Al-Ahwas, on the authority of Abdullah,
m: regarding His statement,
h
There is not one of you but will pass over it

, he said: The path over Hell is like the edge of a sword. The first layer will pass like lightning, the second like the wind, the third like the best of horses, and the fourth like the best of beasts. Then they will pass and the angels will say, O God, save, save.

x: Others said: Rather, the arrival is the entry, but he meant the infidels, not the believers.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna told us: Abu Dawud told us: Shu’bah told us: Abdullah bin Al-Sa’ib told me, on the authority of a man
m: who heard Ibn Abbas recite it:
h
And there is not one of you but will pass over it
, meaning the disbelievers. He said: No believer will pass over it.

c: Muhammad bin Bashar told us: Abd al-Rahman told us: Amr bin al-Walid al-Shani told us:
m: I heard Ikrimah say:
h
There is not one of you but will pass over it
, meaning the infidels.

x: Others said: Rather, the entrance is general for every believer and disbeliever, except that the entrance of the believer is passing through, and the entrance of the disbeliever is entering.
Who said that?

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement:
h
And there is not one of you but will pass over it

, the Muslims’ passing over the bridge between its two sides and the polytheists’ passing over it to enter it. He said: And the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The men and women who slip on that day will be many, and two rows of angels will surround the bridge, and their supplication on that day will be: O God, save, save.

x: Others said: The believer will suffer from fever and illness in this world.
Who said that?

c: Abu Kuraib told us: Ibn Yaman told us, on the authority of Uthman ibn al-Aswad, on the authority of Mujahid, who said:
m: Fever is the portion of every believer from the Fire. Then he recited:
h
And there is not one of you but will pass over it

c: Imran bin Bakkar Al-Kila’i told me: Abu Al-Mughira told us: Abd Al-Rahman bin Yazid bin Tamim told us: Ismail bin Ubaid God told us, on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said:
m: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, went out to visit a man from among his companions who had an illness, and I was with him. Then he said: God says: It is My Fire which I unleash upon My believing servant so that it may be his portion of the Fire in the Hereafter.

x: Others said: Everyone will return it, then the believers will issue from it with their deeds.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna told us: Yahya bin Saeed told us, on the authority of Shu’bah, who said: Al-Suddi told us, on the authority of Marra, on the authority of Abdullah:
m: h
And there is not one of you but will pass over it
. He said: They will pass over it and then depart from it with their deeds.

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna told us: Abd Al-Rahman Ibn Mahdi told us: Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, on the authority of Marra, on the authority of Abdullah,
m: something similar.

c: Muhammad ibn Ubayd al-Maharbi told me: Asbat told us, on the authority of Abd al-Malik, on the authority of Ubayd God, on the authority of Mujahid, who said:
m: I was with Ibn Abbas when a man called Abu Rashid, who was Nafi’ ibn al-Azraq, came to him and said to him: O Ibn Abbas, what do you think of the statement of God, “
h
And there is not one of you but will pass over it
: this is upon your Lord an inevitability decreed.” He said: As for you and me, O Abu Rashid, we will pass over it, so see if we will depart from it or not.

c: Ibn Bashar told us: Abu Asim told us: Ibn Jurayj told us: Abu al-Zubayr told me that
m: he heard Jabir ibn Abdullah being asked about the roses, and he said: On the Day of Resurrection, we will be on windows or skylights, above the people, and the nations will be called with their idols and what they used to worship, one after the other, and they will be taken away and they will follow him. He said: And every person, hypocrite and believer, will be given a light, and darkness will cover them, then they will follow him. And on the bridge of Hell will be hooks that will seize whomever God wills, and the light of the hypocrite will be extinguished, and the believers will be saved, and the first group will be saved like the moon on the night of the full moon, and seventy thousand will not be held accountable, then those who follow them will be like the brightest star in the sky, then likewise, then intercession will be established and they will intercede, and whoever said there is no god but God and in whose heart is the weight of a barley grain of goodness will be taken out of the Fire, then they will be thrown towards Paradise, and the people of Paradise will pour water over them, and they will grow like something growing in a flood, then they will be asked and they will be given the world and ten times its like.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Al-Mubarak, on the authority of Al-Hasan, he said:
m: A man said to his brother: Has it come to you that you will enter Hell? He said: Yes. He said: Has it come to you that you will leave it? He said: No. He said: Then why are you laughing? He said: So he was not seen laughing until he met God.

c: Yunus narrated to us, he said: Ibn Wahb narrated to us, he said: Amr ibn al-Harith narrated to us that Bakir narrated to him that he said
m: to Basr ibn Saʿid: So-and-so says: The entrance to Hellfire is standing on it. Basr said: As for Abu Hurairah, I heard him say: When the Day of Resurrection comes, the people will gather and a crier will call out: Let each group join what they used to worship. So one will stand towards a stone, another towards a horse, and another towards a piece of wood, until only those who worshipped God remain. God will come to them, and when they see Him, they will stand towards Him. He will take them and lead them on the Sirat, and in it will be burning bushes. At that time, the call to intercession will be made, and the people will pass by, and the prophets will say: O God, save, save. Bakir said: Ibn ʿUmairah used to say: Then a Muslim will be saved, and another will be upside down in Hell and scratched, then another will be saved. The most correct of the sayings is the one that says: Everyone will return to it, then the believers will emerge from it, and God will save them, and the disbelievers will fall into it. Their arrival into it is what the reports from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, have shown about their passing over the bridge erected over the surface of Hell, with a Muslim being saved and one being piled up in it. Mentioning the report narrated from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, regarding this: Abu Kuraib narrated:

c: Ibn Idris narrated to us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu Sufyan, on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of Umm Mubashar,
m: the wife of Zayd ibn Haritha, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said while he was in Hafsa’s house: No one who witnessed Badr and Al-Hudaybiyyah will enter the Fire. Hafsa said: O Messenger of God, does not God say, ‘
h
There is not one of you but will pass over it
’? The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Then God will save those who feared God.

c: Al-Hasan bin Mudrik told us: Yahya bin Hammad told us: Abu Awana told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu Sufyan, on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of Umm Mubashar, on the authority of the Messenger of God,
m: may God bless him and grant him peace, similarly.

c: Abu Kuraib told us: Abu Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu Sufyan, on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of Umm Mubashar, on the authority of Hafsah, who said:
m: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I hope that no one who witnessed Badr and Al-Hudaybiyyah will enter the Fire. She said: I said: O Messenger of God, does not God say:
h
There is not one of you but will pass over it
? He said: Did you not hear Him say: Then We will save those who feared God and leave the wrongdoers therein on their knees?

c: Yaqub ibn Ibrahim told me: Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ishaq: Ubaydullah ibn al-Mughira ibn Mu'ayqib told me, on the authority of Sulayman ibn Amr ibn Abd al-'Atwari,
m: one of the Banu Laith, who was in the care of Abu Sa'id. He said: I heard Abu Sa'id al-Khudri say: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: "The bridge will be placed between the two sides of Hell, and there will be thorns on it like the thorns of the Sa'dan tree. Then people will seek passage, and some will be saved, some will be wounded by it, some will be saved, some will be detained, and some will be piled up in it. Then, when God has finished judging between His servants, the believers will miss men who were with them in this world, praying as they pray, paying their zakat, fasting as they fast, performing the pilgrimage as they do, and fighting as they do. They will say: 'O our Lord, there are servants from among Your servants who were with us in this world, praying as we pray, paying our zakat, fasting as we fast, performing the pilgrimage as we do, and fighting as we do. We do not see them. Then He will say: 'Go to the Fire.' So they will bring them out, and they will find that the Fire has seized them according to their deeds.
b.via: Sulayman ibn Amr ibn Abd al-'Atwari

x: Some of them will be seized up to their feet, some up to half of their shins, some up to their knees, some up to their breasts, and some up to their necks, but their faces will not be covered. So they will extract them from it and throw them into the Water of Life. It was said: What is the Water of Life, O Messenger of God? He said: The people of Paradise will be washed, and they will grow as a plant grows in the scum of a torrent. Then the prophets will intercede for everyone who testified sincerely that there is no god but God, and they will extract them from it. Then God will bestow His mercy upon those in it, and He will not leave in it a servant in whose heart there is an atom’s weight of faith except that He will bring him out of it.”

c: Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Abdul-Hakam told me: My father and Shuʿayb ibn al-Layth told us, on the authority of al-Layth ibn Khalid, on the authority of Yazid ibn Abi Hilal, on the authority of Zayd ibn Aslam, on the authority of ʿAta’ ibn Yasar, on the authority of Abu Saʿid al-Khudri,
m: that the Messenger of God, may Surat Maryam 19:71
h
And there is not one of you but will pass over it

. This is upon your Lord an inevitability decreed. God bless him and grant him peace, said: “The bridge will be brought - meaning on the Day of Resurrection - and will be placed between the two sides of Hell. We said: O Messenger of God, what is the bridge? He said: A flat, slippery place, with hooks and claws on it and flattened thorns with curved spikes that lead to Najd, called al-Saʿdan. The believers will pass over it like lightning and wind, and like the best horses and riders. One Muslim will be saved, another Muslim will be scratched, and another will be crushed in Hell. Then the last of them will pass, dragged. You will not be more fervent in your plea to me for the truth, which has become clear to you, than the believers on that day to the Almighty, Blessed and Exalted, when they see that they have been saved and their brothers have remained.”

c: Ahmad bin Isa told me: Saeed bin Katheer bin Ufayr told us, on the authority of Malik: Ibn Lahi’ah told us, on the authority of Abu al-Zubayr, who said:
m: I asked Jabir bin Abdullah about the entrance, and he said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “It is the entrance. They will enter the Fire until they emerge from it, and the last one to remain will be a man on the Sirat, crawling, and God will raise a tree for him. He said: He will say: O Lord, bring me closer to it. He said: So God, the Blessed and Exalted, will bring him closer to it. He said: Then he will say: O Lord, admit me to Paradise. He said: He will say: Ask. He said: So he will be asked. He said: He will say: That is for you and ten times that or something like that? He said: He will say: O Lord, are you mocking me? He said: So he will laugh until his uvula and molars are visible.”

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Yahya ibn Ayoubih told me, and Abu Kurayb told us, he said: Muhammad ibn Zayd told us, on the authority of Rushdin,
m: all of them, on the authority of Ziyad ibn Fa’id, on the authority of Sahl ibn Mu’adh, on the authority of his father, “on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: Whoever guards behind the Muslims in the way of God voluntarily, and the ruler does not seize him by guarding, he will not see the Fire with his own eyes except by fulfilling the oath, for God Almighty says: ‘
h
There is not one of you but will pass over it

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us: Abd al-Razzaq told us: Muammar told us: Al-Zuhri told me, on the authority of Ibn al-Musayyab, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah,
m: that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever has three things die, the Fire will not touch him except for the oath meaning: the watering place. As for his saying:
h
It was a decree that was decreed by your Lord
, the people of interpretation differed in their interpretation of it.

x: Some of them said that its meaning is:
h
It was a decree that was decreed by your Lord
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, his statement: Inevitably he said: Fate.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj:
m: It is a decreed event. He said: It is a decree.

x: Others said: Rather, its meaning is: It was an obligatory oath upon your Lord.
Who said that?

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Abu Amr Dawud bin Al-Zubayr told us, he said:
m: I heard Al-Suddi mentioning on the authority of Marra Al-Hamadani, on the authority of Ibn Masoud, It was a decree that was decreed upon your Lord. He said: An obligatory oath.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: It was a decree that was decreed upon your Lord. He said: an obligatory oath.

x: I have explained the statement on that.

evidence.text: Ibn Al-Muthanna told us: Abu Dawud told us: Shu’bah told us: Abdullah bin Al-Sa’ib told me, on the authority of a man who heard Ibn Abbas recite it: And there is not one of you but will pass over it, meaning the disbelievers.

x: God the Most High says: Then We will save from the Fire after they have all entered it, those who feared Him and feared Him, by performing His obligations and avoiding His disobedience. And We will leave the wrongdoers therein on their knees. God the Most High says: And We will leave those who wronged themselves, so they worshipped other than God, disobeyed their Lord, and went against His commands and prohibitions, in the Fire. On their knees, meaning: kneeling on their knees. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
And He will leave the wrongdoers therein on their knees

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us: Abd al-Razzaq told us: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
And He will leave the wrongdoers therein on their knees

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding His statement,
h
And He will leave the wrongdoers therein on their knees
, he said: The kneeling is the worst of sitting. A man does not sit on his knees except when distress befalls him.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement,
h
Then We will save those who feared God and leave the wrongdoers therein on their knees

, that people will enter Hell while it is equal and dark. As for the believers, their good deeds will shine for them, so they will be saved from it. As for the disbelievers, their deeds will destroy them, and they will be detained because of their sins.

x: God the Almighty says: And when Our verses which We sent down to Our Messenger Muhammad are recited to the people as clear proofs, meaning clear to whoever contemplates them and thinks about them that they are evidence for what God made them evidence for for His servants, those who disbelieved in God and His Book and His verses, and they are the Quraysh, say to those who believed and affirmed it, and they are the companions of Muhammad, Which of the two parties is better in position? He means by position: their place of residence, which is their dwellings and homes, and better in company, which is the assembly, it is said from it: I gathered the people, I gathered them in a assembly, and it is said: he is in the assembly of his people and in their club: meaning the same, and from the assembly Hatim said: I was invited to the first assembly, but he did not look at me with squinting eyes. The interpretation of the words:
h
And when Our clear verses are recited to them

, those who disbelieve say to those who believe: Which of the two parties - us and you - has more spacious life, more comfortable life, better dwelling, better assembly, and more numerous and more omnipresent in assembly - us or you?
And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Bashar told us: Muammil told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu Dhibyan, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement, The best place to stay and the best place to gather. He said: The place is the home, and the gathering is the assembly.

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna told us: Ibn Abi Uday told us, on the authority of Shu’bah, on the authority of Sulayman, on the authority of Abu Dhibyan, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: similarly.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: h
And when Our clear verses are recited to them
, those who disbelieve say to those who believe, ‘
h
Which of the two parties is better in position and better in company

?’ He said: The place of residence is the dwelling place, and the assembly is the council, the blessings and the joy in which they were, and it is as God said to the people of Pharaoh when He destroyed them and narrated their story in the Qur’an, saying, How many gardens and springs did they leave behind, and crops and noble dwellings, and comfort in which they used to rejoice. (al-Dukhan 44:5-6) So the place of residence is the place of residence and the assembly is the council and gathering in which they used to gather. And God said in what He narrated to His Messenger regarding the matter of Lot when He said, And you commit evil in your assemblies. (al-Ankabut 29:29). The Arabs call the assembly: the club.

c: Ali told me, he said: Abdullah told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his statement, and the best company, means a gathering.

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding the statement of God, Which of the two parties? He said: Quraysh say it to the companions of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. And the best company. He said: Their gatherings, they also say it.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: something similar.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement,
h
And when Our clear verses are recited to them
, those who disbelieve say to those who believe, ‘
h
Which of the two parties is better in position and better in company

?’ They saw the companions of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, in their rough living, and among them were harshness, so the polytheists presented what you hear his statement, and better in company, meaning: a gathering.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us: Abd al-Razzaq told us: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement,
h
Which of the two parties is better in position and better in company
? He said: The company is the assembly. And he recited the statement of God Almighty, Then let him call his assembly (al-Alaq 96:7), and he said: His assembly.

x: God Almighty says: And how many have We destroyed before these, O Muhammad, those who said to the believers, when the verses of the Most Gracious were recited to them, which of the two groups is better in position, and better in company, and whose councils are better than those of a generation, and whose dwellings are more comfortable than these, and whose appearance is better than theirs, and whose forms are more beautiful. So We destroyed their wealth, and changed their forms. And from that is the saying of Alqamah bin Abdah: A dead man, the color of purple, I spread out to sell the worn-out in cubic flint. By Swan means: the bed in which clothes are kept. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Bashar told us: Muammil told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu Dhibyan, on the authority of Abu Abbas:
m: h
The best furniture and appearance
. He said: The appearance is the appearance, and the furniture is the goods.

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna told us: Ibn Abi Uday told us, on the authority of Shu’bah, on the authority of Sulayman, on the authority of Abu Dhibyan, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said:
m: The vision is the sight.

c: Ali told me, he said: Abdullah told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his statement, the best in furniture and appearance, meaning: in appearance.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
The best furniture and appearance
. Furniture means money, and appearance means sight.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Hudha told us, he said: Aouf told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan,
m: regarding his statement, furniture and property, he said: Furniture is the best of goods, and property, he said: money.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: God Almighty says: And how many generations before them have We destroyed who were better in furnishings and appearance: meaning more enjoyment and a better position and settlement, so God destroyed their wealth and corrupted their images for them, Almighty and Exalted.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us: Abd al-Razzaq told us: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement, the most beautiful furniture and appearance, he said: the most beautiful image and the most wealth.

c: Muhammad Bani Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: Furnishment he said: the goods, and vision he said: in what people see.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: something similar.

c: Ibn Hamid and Bishr bin Muadh told us: Jarir bin Qabus told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: Furniture means money, and the view means a beautiful appearance.

c: Al-Qasim told us: Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ata’ al-Khurasani, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: And they were seen as a sight in color and beauty.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding his statement,
h
The best furniture and appearance
, he said: The appearance is the view, and the furniture is the furnishings, the best furnishings, and the best appearance.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh say regarding his statement, the best furniture, meaning money, and appearance, meaning: the beautiful view. The reciters differed in reading this, so the majority of the reciters of the people of Medina read it as wariya without a hamza, and if it is read in this way, it has two meanings: One of them is that the reciter intended the hamza, so he replaced it with a ya, so the ya that was replaced from the hamza and the ya that is the lam of the verb came together, so they were assimilated, and they became one doubled ya to make it similar, since it was the beginning of a verse, to its counterparts from all the beginnings of verses before and after it. The other is that it is from ruwayt arwi ruwayt wa riya, and if that is intended by it, the meaning of the statement is: And how many generations before them did We destroy, who were better in provision, better in looking after their wealth, and better in knowing how to manage it, because the Arabs say: How good is the vision of so-and-so in this matter if he had good insight into it and knowledge of it. The majority of the reciters of Iraq, Kufa, and Basra read it as wariya with a hamza, Surat Maryam 19:74 And how many generations before them have We destroyed who were better in furnishings and appearance? meaning: the vision of the eye, as if he meant: the best provision and mirror. It was narrated that some of them read: The best furniture and clothing, with a z, as if he meant the best furnishings, appearance, and view. This is because the cloth is the appearance and view from their saying: I decorated the girl, meaning: I adorned her and made her look good.

x: The most correct of the readings in this regard is the reading of the one who reads athathan wa ruʿya with the ra’ and the hamza, because of the consensus of the hujjat from the people of interpretation that its meaning is: the view, and that is from seeing with the eye, not from seeing, so therefore the hamzat is more appropriate for it. If a reader reads it without the hamza, and he means this meaning, then he is not mistaken in his reading. As for his reading with the zay, then it is a reading outside the reading of the readers, so I do not permit reading with it because it is contrary to their reading, even though they have a correct interpretation. The Arab scholars differed as to whether a single word for athath is plural or singular. Al-Ahmar, as he was told, said: It is the plural of the singular word aathathah, just as the singular word for hamam is the plural of hamama, and the singular word for sahab is the plural of sahabah.

As for Al-Farra’, he used to say: It has no singular, just as mataa’ has no singular. He said: The Arabs pluralize mataa’ as amaghtah, “amati’,” and mataa’. Qala’ said: If you had pluralized athath, you would have said: three athah and athath. As for ra’i, its plural is ra’a.

evidence.text: God Almighty says: And how many have We destroyed before these, O Muhammad, those who said to the believers, when the verses of the Most Gracious were recited to them, which of the two groups is better in position, and better in company, and whose councils are better than those of a generation, and whose dwellings are more comfortable than these, and whose appearance is better than theirs, and whose forms are more beautiful.

The reciters differed in reading this, so the majority of the reciters of the people of Medina read it as wariya without a hamza, and if it is read in this way, it has two meanings: One of them is that the reciter intended the hamza, so he replaced it with a ya, so the ya that was replaced from the hamza and the ya that is the lam of the verb came together, so they were assimilated, and they became one doubled ya to make it similar, since it was the beginning of a verse, to its counterparts from all the beginnings of verses before and after it.

The majority of the reciters of Iraq, Kufa, and Basra read it as wariya with a hamza, Surat Maryam 19:74 And how many generations before them have We destroyed who were better in furnishings and appearance? meaning: the vision of the eye, as if he meant: the best provision and mirror.

Abu Jaʿfar said: The most correct of the readings in this regard is the reading of the one who reads athathan wa ruʿya with the ra’ and the hamza, because of the consensus of the hujjat from the people of interpretation that its meaning is: the view, and that is from seeing with the eye, not from seeing, so therefore the hamzat is more appropriate for it.
If a reader reads it without the hamza, and he means this meaning, then he is not mistaken in his reading.

As for his reading with the zay, then it is a reading outside the reading of the readers, so I do not permit reading with it because it is contrary to their reading, even though they have a correct interpretation.

x: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: Say, O Muhammad, to these polytheists who say, when Our verses are recited to them: Which of the two parties, from us and from you, is better in position and better in company? Whoever from us and from you is in error, deviating from the path of truth, taking a path other than that of guidance, then let the Most Merciful extend for him a period. He says: Let God prolong his error for him, and let him have respite in it. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement, In error, then let the Most Merciful extend for him a term, then let God leave him in his transgression.

c: Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same. And His statement,
h
Until when they see what they are promised

, either the punishment or the Hour, God Almighty says: Say to them: Whoever among us and among you is in error, let the Most Merciful prolong his error until God’s command comes to them, either an immediate punishment, or they meet their Lord at the establishment of the Hour which God has promised His creation that He will gather them for. For when God’s promise of one of these two matters comes to them, they will know who is worse in position and dwelling than you and them and weaker in soldiers, are they or you? And then they will know which of the two groups is better in position and better in company.

x: God Almighty says: And God increases the one who follows the straight path, and is guided to the path of righteousness, so he believes in his Lord, and believes in His verses, and does what He commands him to do, and refrains from what He forbids him from, guidance through what he rereport of faith in the obligations that He imposes upon him, and he acknowledges the necessity of imposing them upon him, and he works with them, so that is an increase from God in his guidance by His verses, guidance upon His guidance, and that is similar to His saying: And when a surah is revealed, some of them say, ‘Which of you has this increased in faith?’ As for those who believe, it increases them in faith, and they rejoice. (al-Tawbah 9:124) Some of them interpreted this as: And God increases those who are guided in guidance by the abrogating and abrogated verses of the Qur’an, so he believes in the abrogating verse, just as he believed in the abrogated verse before.

This is an increase in guidance from God to him in addition to his previous guidance. And the lasting good deeds are better with your Lord as reward. God the Most High says: “And the deeds that God has commanded His servants to do and is pleased with from them, the lasting good deeds for them, not the transient ones, are better with your Lord as a reward for their people. “And better as a return” for them than the positions of these polytheists and their clubs that they boast about over the people of faith in this world. We have explained the meaning of the lasting good deeds, and we have mentioned the differences of opinion among those who differ on this, and we have demonstrated the correctness of what is said about it in the past, which makes it unnecessary to repeat it in this place. Al-Hasan bin Yahya narrated: Abd al-Razzaq narrated: Umar bin Rashid narrated: Yahya bin Abi Katheer narrated: Abu Salamah bin Abd al-Rahman bin Awf narrated: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, sat down one day and took a dry stick, crushed its leaves and then said: ‘Saying La ilaha illa God, Allahu Akbar, al-Hamdulillah, and subhan God erases sins, just as the wind erases the leaves of this tree.

Take them, O Abu al-Darda’, before you are prevented from them. They are the lasting good deeds, and they are from the treasures of Paradise.’” Abu Salamah said: Whenever Abu al-Darda’ mentioned this hadith, he would say: ‘I will glorify God, declare His greatness, and praise God, until when an ignorant person sees me, he will think I am crazy.’”

God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: “Have you seen, O Muhammad, the one who disbelieved in Our signs and did not believe in them and denied Our threat from the people of disbelief and said, while he was a disbeliever in God and in His Messenger, ‘I will surely be given wealth and children’ in the Hereafter?” He mentioned that these verses were revealed about Al-‘As ibn Wa’il Al-Sahmi Abu ‘Amr ibn Al-‘As. The novel mentioned that: Abu Al-Sa'ib and Sa'id bin Yahya narrated: Abu Mu'awiyah narrated on the authority of Al-A'mash on the authority of Muslim on the authority of Masruq on the authority of Khabbab who said: I was a blacksmith, and Al-'As bin Wa'il owed me a debt. I came to him to collect it, but he said: By God, I will not pay you until you disbelieve in Muhammad. I said: By God, I will not disbelieve in Muhammad until you die and are resurrected.
He said: So he said: So if I die and am resurrected as you say, you come to me with wealth and children. He said: Then God revealed:
h
Have you seen he who disbelieved in Our verses and said
, 'I will surely be given wealth and children?' Has he known the unseen, or has he taken a covenant from the Most Merciful? . . . until His saying: and he comes to Us alone.

c: Abu Al-Saib told me
m: about it, and he read in the hadith: And a child.

c: Muhammad ibn Saʿd told me: My father told me: My uncle told me: My father told me:
m: On the authority of his father: On the authority of Ibn ʿAbbas: Some men from among the companions of the Messenger of God (may God bless him and grant him peace) were seeking a debt from Al-ʿAs ibn Waʿil As-Sahmi, so they came to him to collect it. He said: Do you not claim that in Paradise there is silver, gold, silk, and all kinds of fruits? They said: Yes. He said: Your appointed time is in the Hereafter, and by God, I will be given wealth and children, and I will be given the like of the book that you brought. So God gave an example of it in the Qur’an, and said:
h
Have you seen he who disbelieved in Our verses and said
, ‘I will certainly be given wealth’... until His saying: and he will come to Us alone.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding the statement of God, I will be given wealth and children, he said: Al-Amir bin Wa’il says it.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same. Bishr bin Muadh narrated: Yazid narrated: Saeed narrated: Qatada said: His statement,
h
Have you seen he who disbelieved in Our verses and said

, ‘I will surely be given wealth and children,’ He mentioned to us that some men from among the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came to a polytheist man to collect a debt from him. He said: Doesn’t your companion claim that there is silk and gold in Paradise? They said: Yes. He said: Then your appointment is Paradise. By God, I will not believe in the book that you have brought - mocking the Book of God - and I will be given wealth and children.

x: Al-Hasan bin Yahya narrated: Abd al-Razzaq narrated: Ath-Thawri narrated: Al-A'mash narrated: Abu al-Duha narrated: Masruq narrated: Khabbab bin al-Arat said: I was a blacksmith in Mecca, and I worked for al-'As bin Wa'il. I owed him money, so I came to collect it from him, but he said to me: I will not pay you until you disbelieve in Muhammad. I said: I will not disbelieve in Muhammad until you die and are resurrected. He said: Then when I am resurrected, I will have wealth and children. I mentioned that to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and God, the Blessed and Exalted, revealed: Have you seen he who disbelieved in Our verses and said, 'I will surely be given wealth and children'? to and he will come to Us alone. The reciters differed in their reading of His statement, and a son. The majority of the reciters of Medina and Basra, and some of the people of Kufa, read it as and a son with a fat-ha on the waw from son in the entire Qur’an.
However, Abu Amr ibn al-Ala’ specifically mentioned the one in Surat Nuh with a damma, so he read it as his wealth and his son
r

. As for the majority of the reciters of Kufa, other than Asim, they read from this surah from His statement, wealth and son to the end of the surah, and the two in Az-Zukhruf, and the one in Nuh, with a damma and a sukoon on the lam. The Arabists differed about the meaning of this if its waw is closed.

Some of them said: It is the same to have a closed and a open, but they are two languages, like their saying al-‘adām and al-‘adām, and al-ḥuzn and al-ḥuzn. They cited as evidence for their saying the following poet’s saying: I wish so-and-so was in his mother's womb, and I wish so-and-so was the son of a donkey. Al-Harith bin Halza says: I have seen people who have produced wealth and children. And the saying of Ru'bah: Praise be to God, the Almighty, the One, Who has not taken from a son a son. And the Arabs say in a similar way: Your son is from my blood, your descendants. He said: And all of this is one, meaning son. And it was mentioned to me that Qais makes son a plural, and son is one. Perhaps those who read it with the dammah in what they chose in it, only read it that way to differentiate between the plural and the one.

What is more correct than what I say about this is that the fat-ha in the waw of al-walad and the damma in it have the same meaning, and they are two languages, so whichever one the reader reads with, he is correct, except that the fat-ha is the more famous of the two languages in it, so reading with it is more pleasing to me for that reason. And His statement, He has knowledge of the unseen, means, the Almighty says: This speaker of this statement has knowledge of the unseen, so he knows that he will have wealth and children in the Hereafter by being informed of the knowledge of what is hidden from him. Or has he taken a covenant from the Most Merciful? He says: Or has he believed in God and done what He commanded him to do, and refrained from what He forbade him from doing, so that he has a covenant with God that He will give him what he said of wealth and children.

c: As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: Has he known the unseen or has he taken a covenant with the Most Merciful? with a good deed he had done.

evidence.text: The reciters differed in their reading of His statement, and a son.
The majority of the reciters of Medina and Basra, and some of the people of Kufa, read it as and a son with a fat-ha on the waw from son in the entire Qur’an.
However, Abu Amr ibn al-Ala’ specifically mentioned the one in Surat Nuh with a damma, so he read it as his wealth and his son (Nuh: 21).

As for the majority of the reciters of Kufa, other than Asim, they read from this surah from His statement, wealth and son to the end of the surah, and the two in Az-Zukhruf, and the one in Nuh, with a damma and a sukoon on the lam.
Perhaps those who read it with the dammah in what they chose in it, only read it that way to differentiate between the plural and the one.

Abu Jaʿfar said: What is more correct than what I say about this is that the fat-ha in the waw of al-walad and the damma in it have the same meaning, and they are two languages, so whichever one the reader reads with, he is correct, except that the fat-ha is the more famous of the two languages in it, so reading with it is more pleasing to me for that reason.

x: God the Most High means by His saying: No, that is not the case. He did not know the unseen, so He knew the truth of what he says, and the reality of what he mentions, nor did he take a covenant with the Most Merciful to believe in God and His Messenger, and to work in obedience to Him, but rather he lied and disbelieved. Then God the Most High said: We will record what he says: meaning, We will record what this disbeliever says about his Lord, who says, I will surely be given wealth and children, and We will extend for him a great deal of punishment: meaning, We will increase his punishment in Hell for his false and invalid speech in this world, in addition to his punishment for his disbelief in God.
And His saying,
h
And We will inherit from him what he says

, the Almighty says: And We will deprive this speaker: I will be given in the Hereafter wealth and children, his wealth and children, and his wealth and children will be ours without him, and he will come to us on the Day of Resurrection alone, with no wealth or children with him. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa H told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, his statement,
h
And We inherit from him what he says
: his wealth and his children, and that is what Al-Aasi bin Wa’il said.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement,
h
And We will inherit from him what he says
, and he will come to Us alone, meaning he has no money or children.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement,
h
And We will inherit from him what he says
, he said: What he has. And what! His statement, I will be given wealth and children, and in the wording of Ibn Masoud: And We will inherit from him what he has.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement,
h
And We will inherit from him what he says
, he said: What he collected from the world and what he did in it. He said, And he comes to us alone. He said, One of those, not followed by a few or many.

c: Ali told me, he said: Abdullah told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his statement,
h
And We inherit from him what he says
: We inherit from him.

x: God the Almighty says: And O Muhammad, these polytheists from your people have taken gods to worship besides God, so that these gods may be a source of honor for them, protecting them from the punishment of God, and they take their worship of them as a means of nearness to God. And His saying, No, God the Almighty says: The matter is not as they thought and hoped from these gods that they worship besides God, that they will save them from the punishment of God, and deliver them from it, and from the evil that their Lord intended for them. And His saying,
h
They will disbelieve in their worship

, God the Almighty says: But the gods will disbelieve in the Hereafter because of the worship of these polytheists on the Day of Resurrection, and their disbelief in it is their saying to their Lord: We disavow to You that they used to worship us, so they denied that they worshipped them or ordered them to do so, and they disavowed them, and that is their disbelief in their worship.
As for his saying,
h
And they will be against them
, the people of interpretation differed in their interpretation.
Some of them said: The meaning of that is: And their gods will be a help to them. And they said: The opposite means the help.
Who said that?

c: Ali told us, he said: Abdullah told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his statement,
h
and they will be against them
, meaning: helpers.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa H told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
h
And they will be against them
, he said: A helper against them, quarreling with them and lying to them.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: h
And they will be against them
, he said: Their idols will be in the Fire on the Day of Resurrection.

x: Others said: Rather, he meant the opposite in this place: the peers.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his statement,
h
And they will be opponents to them
, meaning: they will be companions to them.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement,
h
and they will be opponents to them
, they will be companions in the Fire, cursing each other and disowning each other.

c: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement opposite, he said: Companions in the Fire.

x: Others said: The meaning of the opposite here is: the enemy.
Who said that?

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd told us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement,
h
And they will be opponents to them
, he said: Enemies.

x: Others said: The meaning of the opposite in this place is: affliction.
Who said that?

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement,
h
and they will be against them

, he said: They will be a calamity against them. The opposite is the calamity, and the opposite in the speech of the Arabs is: disagreement. It is said: So-and-so opposes so-and-so in such-and-such, if he disagrees with him in his actions, so he spoils what he has corrected, and corrects what he has corrupted. And since that is its meaning, and the gods of these polytheists whom God mentioned in this place disavow them, and deny them on that day, they became their opposites, and they were described as such. The Arabists differed about the reason for unifying the opposite, which is an attribute of a group.

x: Some of the grammarians of Basra used to say: wahad because it can be a group and one, like rasad and arsad. He said: rasad can also be for a group.
Some of the grammarians of Kufa used to say: wahad because its meaning is helper, and he mentioned that Abu Nahik used to read it that way.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said: Yahya bin Wadh told us, he said: Abdul-Mumin told us, he said:
m: I heard Abu Nahik Al-Azdi reading No, they will disbelieve, meaning all the gods will disbelieve in their worship.

evidence.text: Some of the grammarians of Kufa used to say: wahad because its meaning is helper, and he mentioned that Abu Nahik used to read it that way.

x: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: Have you not seen, O Muhammad, that We have sent the devils upon the disbelievers in God? To incite them means to move them by tempting and misleading them, so they disturb them to commit God’s sins and tempt them with them until they commit them. To incite means to incite and tempt. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said.
Who said that?

c: Ali told us, he said: Abdullah told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his saying Aza means: He tempts them with temptation.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said: Ibn Abbas said:
m: “You incite the disbelievers to polytheism. Go ahead, go ahead with this matter until you cause them to fall into the Fire. Go ahead with error, go ahead.”

c: Abu Kuraib told us: Abu Idris told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak,
m: regarding his statement,
h
You tempt them with temptation
, he said:
h
You tempt them with temptation

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement,
h
It disturbs them with disturbance
, he said:
h
It disturbs them with disturbance
in disobeying God.

c: Muhammad bin Bashar told us: Ibn Uthma told us: Saeed bin Bashir told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding God’s statement,
h
It drives them to disobey God
, he said:
h
It drives them to disobey God

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us: Abd al-Razzaq told us: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement,
h
You will disturb them with a disturbance
, he said:
h
You will disturb them with a disturbance
in disobeying God.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement,
h
Have you not seen that We send the devils upon the disbelievers

, to incite them with [a] great incitement? Then he recited, And whoever turns away from the remembrance of the Most Merciful - We appoint for him a devil, and he is to him a companion. (al-Zukhruf 43:36), he said: Incite them with [a] great incitement, he said: “He drives them to pieces to disobey God Almighty, and tempts them to do it, as a person tempts another to do something. It is said from this: I incited so-and-so to do such-and-such,” if you tempted him with it, I incite him with a great incitement and a great incitement, and I heard the sizzling of the pot: which is the sound of it boiling on the fire. From this is the hadith of Mutraf from his father, that he came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, while he was praying, and there was a sizzling sound in his stomach like the sizzling of a cauldron.

x: And His statement, "So do not hasten upon them. We are only preparing for them a [decreed] number." The Almighty says: So do not hasten upon these disbelievers by seeking punishment and destruction for them, O Muhammad. We are only preparing for them a [decreed] number. He says: We only delay their destruction so that they may increase in sin, and We count all their deeds and enumerate them, even their very breaths, so that We may reward them for all of them. We did not leave their destruction untimely for any good that We intended for them. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said.
Who said that?

c: Ali told us, he said: Abdullah told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his statement, We only count for them a count, meaning: their breaths that they take in this world, so they are counted like their years and their life spans.

x: God the Most High says: The Day We shall gather those who feared Him in this world and feared His punishment, so they avoided His disobedience and performed His duties to their Lord. As a delegation, meaning by delegation: the riders. It is said: I came to someone if you went to him. And the people sent a delegation to their leader if they sent an expedition from before them. And the delegation in this place means gathering, but it is singular because it is a source and their singular is wafid. And the delegation may be plural: delegations, as some of the Banu Hanifa said: I am praising what the head of the delegations, Muzahim bin Jassas, is doing. In this case, delegations may be the plural of delegate, just as sitting is the plural of sitting. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said.
Who said that?

c: Zakariya bin Yahya bin Abi Zaida told me: Ibn Fadil told us, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman bin Ishaq, on the authority of al-Nu’man bin Sa’d, on the authority of Ali,
m: regarding His statement,
h
On the Day We shall gather the righteous to the Most Merciful as a delegation

, he said: By God, the delegation will not be gathered on their feet, nor will they be driven in a cart, but they will be brought she-camels the likes of which mankind has never seen, on which are saddles of gold and their reins are of emerald, and they will ride on them until they knock on the gates of Paradise.

c: Muhammad bin Al-Muthanna told us: Abd Al-Rahman bin Mahdi told us, on the authority of Shu’bah, on the authority of Ismail, on the authority of a man, on the authority of Abu Hurairah:
m: On the Day We will gather the righteous to the Most Merciful as a delegation. He said: On camels.

c: Ali told us, he said: Abdullah told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his statement,
h
On the Day We shall gather the righteous to the Most Merciful as a delegation
, meaning: as riders.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Al-Hakam bin Bashir told us: Amr bin Qais Al-Mala’i told us:
m: When the believer emerges from his grave, he will be met by the most beautiful image and the most fragrant. He will say: Do you recognize me? He will say: No, except that God made your scent pleasant and your image beautiful. He will say: That is how I was in this world. I was your righteous deeds. As long as I rode you in this world, ride me today. And he recited: The Day We will gather the righteous to the Most Merciful as a delegation.

c: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: To the Most Gracious a delegation. He said: A delegation to Paradise.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj,
m: regarding his statement,
h
On the Day We shall gather the righteous to the Most Merciful as a delegation
, he said: On the best of horses.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, he said:
m: I heard Sufyan al-Thawri say: On the Day We will gather the righteous to the Most Merciful as a delegation. He said: On camels, female camels.

x: And His statement,
h
And We will drive the criminals to Hell

, thirsty. God Almighty says: And We will drive the disbelievers in God who committed crimes to Hell, thirsty. And the word flow is a noun derived from the saying of the speaker: I brought such-and-such, I brought it flowing, and for this reason it was not pluralized, and it was described by the word shaddah as a plural. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said.
Who said that?

c: Ali told me, he said: Abdullah told me, he said: Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his statement,
h
And We will drive the criminals to Hell
, thirsty, meaning: thirsty.

c: Muhammad bin Al-Muthanna told us: Abd Al-Rahman bin Mahdi told us, on the authority of Shu’bah, on the authority of Ismail, on the authority of a man, on the authority of Abu Hurairah:
m: h
And We will drive the criminals to Hell
, thirsty. He said: Thirsty.

c: Yaqub and Al-Fadl bin Sabah told me: Ismail bin Aliyah told us, on the authority of Abu Raja’, who said:
m: I heard Al-Hasan say regarding His statement,
h
And We will drive the criminals to Hell
, thirsty. He said: Thirsty.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Yunus, on the authority of Al-Hasan,
m: the same.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement, to Hell in a state of thirst, he said: thirsty for the Fire.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
And We will drive the criminals to Hell
, thirsty and thirsty. They will be driven to it while they are thirsty and thirsty.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, he said:
m: I heard Sufyan say regarding His statement,
h
And We will drive the criminals to Hell
, thirsty. He said: Thirsty.

x: God Almighty says: These disbelievers in their Lord, O Muhammad, will not have the power to intercede on the Day when God will gather the righteous to Him as a delegation, when the people of faith will intercede for each other with God, and some of them will intercede for each other except for those among them who have taken a covenant with the Most Merciful in this world, with faith in Him, believing in His Messenger, acknowledging what he brought, and doing what he commanded.
