c: As Ali told me, he said: Abdullah told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement,
h
Except for he who has taken a covenant with the Most Merciful
, he said: The covenant is the testimony that there is no god but God, and he disavows before God any power and strength and hopes only in God.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Husayn told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj,
m: his statement,
h
They do not possess intercession except for one who has made a covenant with the Most Merciful
, he said: The believers on that Day will be intercessors for one another, except for one who has made a covenant with the Most Merciful, he said: a righteous deed.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement,
h
They do not possess intercession except for one who has taken a covenant with the Most Merciful
: meaning, by obeying Him. And he said in another verse, Intercession does not benefit except for one to whom the Most Merciful has given permission and whose word is acceptable
r

so that they may know that on the Day of Resurrection, God will intercede for some believers for others. “It was mentioned to us that the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to say: ‘There is a man in my nation through whose intercession God will admit more people into Paradise than the Banu Tamim.’ And we used to tell stories about a martyr who would intercede for seventy of his family members.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Abu al-Malih, on the authority of Awf ibn Malik, he said:
m: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘My intercession is for whoever dies from my nation who does not associate anything with God.’” And min in his statement except for is in the accusative case as an exception, and it is not a genitive with the pronoun lam, but it may be in the accusative case in speech in a place other than this, and that is like the saying of the one who says: I wanted to pass by today except the enemy, for I will not pass by him, so he excludes the enemy from the meaning, and that is not the case in his statement: except for those who have taken a covenant with the Most Merciful, because the meaning of the statement is: These disbelievers do not have the power except for those who believe in God, so the believers are not from the number of disbelievers. And whoever puts it in the accusative case on the basis that its meaning is except for those who have taken a covenant with the Most Merciful, then his statement they do not have the power to intercede should be made for the righteous, so the meaning of the statement then is on the Day when We gather the righteous to the Most Merciful as a delegation, they do not have the power to intercede, except for those who have taken a covenant with the Most Merciful, so its meaning then is: except for those who have taken a covenant with the Most Merciful. The Most Gracious has made a covenant. But if he made they do not possess intercession a predicate for the criminals, then whoever would then be in the accusative case as a disjunctive exception, so the meaning of the statement would be: they do not possess intercession, but whoever takes a covenant with the Most Gracious has it.

x: God Almighty says: And these disbelievers in God said, The Most Gracious has taken a son. You have certainly done a terrible thing. God Almighty says to those who say that among His creation: You have certainly done, O people, a terrible thing in speech.
And similar to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said.
Who said that?

c: Ali told me, he said: Abdullah told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his saying something great means: a great saying.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement,
h
You have certainly done something terrible
, meaning:
h
You have certainly done something terrible
, which is the reprehensible speech.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us
m: both, Ibn Abi Nujayh told us, on the authority of Mujahid, his statement something great he said: great.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us: Abd al-Razzaq told us: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement, something great, he said: great.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said
m: about His statement,
h
You have certainly done something terrible

, he said: You have done something great in the matter, when they attributed a son to the Most Gracious. And there are three dialects for idd, it is said: Laqad ja’it shay’an iddan, with a kasra on the alif, and ada with a fatha on the alif, and ada with a fatha on the alif and a long vowel, on the example of mad fa’il. And the reciters of the regions read it, and we read it like that, and it was mentioned from Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami that he read it with a fatha on the alif, but I do not see his reading it like that because it is different from the reading of the reciters of the regions. And the Arabs say for every great matter: id, “imr,” and nkar, and from it is the saying of the rajaz poet: The enemies have suffered from me a terrible, terrible and bitter punishment. And from it is the saying of another: In his panting and sluggishness if

evidence.text: And the reciters of the regions read it, and we read it like that, and it was mentioned from Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami that he read it with a fatha on the alif, but I do not see his reading it like that because it is different from the reading of the reciters of the regions.

x: And His saying,
h
The heavens almost burst from it

, the Almighty says: The heavens almost burst into pieces because of their saying, The Most Gracious has taken a son, and from this it is said: his fang burst: if it split. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Ali told me, he said: Abdullah told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement,
h
The heavens almost burst from it

, and the earth splits open, and the mountains collapse in devastation, because they attribute to the Most Merciful a son, he said: Indeed, polytheism terrified the heavens, the earth, the mountains, and all of creation except the two heavy ones, and they almost disappeared because of it due to the greatness of God. Just as the good deeds of the polytheist do not benefit with polytheism, so we hope that God will forgive the sins of the monotheists. “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Teach your dead to bear witness that there is no god but God, and whoever says it at his death, Paradise is obligatory for him.” They said, O Messenger of God, but whoever says it when he is healthy? He said, That is more obligatory and more obligatory. Then he said, “By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, if the heavens and the earths and whatever is in them and what is between them and what is beneath them were brought and placed on one side of the scale, and the testimony that there is no god but God were placed on the other side, it would outweigh them.”

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: h
The heavens almost burst from it

, the earth splits open, and the mountains collapse in devastation. It was mentioned to us that Ka’b used to say: The angels became angry, and Hell was inflamed, when they said what they said. His saying,
h
And the earth will split open

, means: The earth will almost split open, and will crack from that. And the mountains will almost fall down in heap, means: The mountains will almost fall down on one another in a falling down. Falling down is the source of the verb threatened, so I will throw down a falling down. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.

x: Who said that?

c: Ali told me, he said: Abdullah told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his statement,
h
And the mountains will collapse in ruins
, meaning: demolition.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said: Ibn Abbas said:
m: And the mountains will collapse in devastation. He said: Devastation? The collapse.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement,
h
And the mountains shall fall down in ruins

, he said: In anger for God. He said: And those who made this for God, for whom the heavens, the earth, and the mountains were angry, called upon them to repent and said, They have certainly disbelieved who say, ‘God is the third of three.’ (al-Ma’idah 5:73) They said: He, his wife, and his son, they made them two gods. And there is no god except one God. (al-Ma’idah 5:73)... to His statement, And they seek His forgiveness, and God is Forgiving and Merciful. (al-Ma’idah 5:73)

x: God Almighty says: And the mountains almost fall down in a fit of turmoil, because they attribute to the Most Merciful a son. So, according to some Arab scholars, an is in the accusative case because of its connection to the verb, and according to others, it is in the genitive case with the prepositional pronoun - and we have explained the correct statement about that in more than one place in this book of ours - so that there is no need to repeat it in this place.

i: He said, That they attribute to the Most Gracious a son, meaning by his saying, that they attribute: that they made a son for Him, as the poet said:
x: Is there not a Lord whom you call to be sincere, and if you are absent you will find him absent and not sincere?
Ibn Ahmar said: I love her with a sharp knife, and I make her shine, and I call her kohl-like dirt the monkey.
And his saying,
h
And it is not befitting for the Most Merciful to take a son

, means: And it is not befitting for God to take a son, because He is not like the creation who are overcome by desires, and are compelled by pleasures to have intercourse with females, and no child occurs except from a female, and God is exalted above being like His creation, and that is like the saying of Ibn Ahmar: In the head of a nobleman, a towering phoenix, beyond which there is no plain or mountain Meaning: It is not suitable and will not be.

There is none in the heavens and the earth but will come to the Most Merciful as a servant. He says: There is none in the heavens from the angels, and on the earth from the humans, mankind, and jinn but will come to the Most Merciful as a servant. He says: He will come to his Lord on the Day of Resurrection as a servant to Him, humbled and submissive, acknowledging servitude to Him, with no kinship between him and Him. And His saying
h
I will come to the Most Merciful is only the subject of the verb I come to Him
, so I will come to Him.

God Almighty says: The Most Gracious has counted all of His creation, and has counted them. Nothing is hidden from Him as to the number of all of them, and He knows their number, so not one of them is hidden from Him.

And all of them will come to Him alone on the Day of Resurrection. He says: And all of His creation will come to Him alone on the Day of Resurrection, with no helper from God, and no defender from Him. So God will decide concerning him what He will decide, and will do to him what He will do.

God Almighty says: Indeed, those who believed in God and His Messengers, and believed in what came to them from their Lord, and acted upon it, making lawful what He made lawful, and making unlawful what He made unlawful, the Most Merciful will appoint for them love in this world, in the hearts of His believing servants. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said.
Who said that?

c: Yahya bin Talha told me: Sharik told us, on the authority of Muslim Al-Mala’i, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement,
h
The Most Gracious will bestow upon them love
, he said: Love among people in this world.

c: Ali told me, he said: Abdullah told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement,
h
The Most Gracious will bestow upon them affection
, he said: Love.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement,
h
The Most Gracious will bestow upon them love
, he said: Love from the Muslims in this world, good provision, and a truthful tongue.

c: Yahya bin Talha told me: Sharik told us, on the authority of Ubayd al-Maktab, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement,
h
The Most Gracious will bestow upon them love
, he said: Love among the Muslims in this world.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Hakam told us, on the authority of Anbasa, on the authority of Al-Qasim bin Abi Bazza, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement:
h
The Most Gracious will grant them love
, he said: He will love them and make them beloved to His creation.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, The Most Gracious will make for them love, he said: He will love them and make them beloved to the believers.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Ali bin Hashim told us, on the authority of Abu Laila, on the authority of Al-Hakam, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: He loves them and makes them beloved.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Al-Hakam bin Bashir told us: Amr told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement,
h
The Most Gracious will bestow upon them love
, he said: No servant turns to God except that God turns the hearts of the servants to him, and increases it from Him.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement, Indeed, those who have believed and done righteous deeds - the Most Merciful will appoint for them love: Yes, by God, in the hearts of the people of faith. It was mentioned to us that Harim bin Hayyan used to say: No servant turns his heart to God, except that God turns the hearts of the believers to him, until He grants him their love and mercy.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: that Uthman bin Affan used to say: There is no servant among the people who does good or evil, except that God clothes him in the garment of his deeds.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us: Abd al-Razzaq told us, on the authority of al-Thawri, on the authority of Muslim, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement,
h
The Most Gracious will bestow upon them affection
, he said: Love. And he mentioned that this verse was revealed about Abd al-Rahman bin Awf.

c: Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Saeed al-Wasiti told me: Yaqub ibn Muhammad told us: Abdul Aziz ibn Imran told us, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Uthman ibn Abi Sulayman ibn Jubayr ibn Mut’im, on the authority of his father, on the authority of his mother Umm Ibrahim,
m: daughter of Abi Ubaydah ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf, on the authority of her father, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf, that when he migrated to Medina, he felt sorry for his companions in Mecca, including Shaiba ibn Rabi’ah, Utbah ibn Rabi’ah, and Ummatah ibn Khalaf. Then God Almighty revealed: Indeed, those who believe and do righteous deeds - the Most Merciful will appoint for them love. Surat Maryam 19:96 Indeed, those who have believed and done righteous deeds - the Most Merciful will appoint for them love.

x: And His statement,
h
We have only made it easy for you in your language that you may give good tidings thereby to the righteous

. God Almighty says: We have only made this Qur'an easy, O Muhammad, for you to recite, so that you may give good tidings thereby to the righteous who fear God's punishment, by performing His obligations and avoiding His disobedience, of Paradise. And to warn with it a people who are obstinate. He says: And to warn with this Qur'an your people from Quraysh of God's punishment, for they are people of obstinacy and false argument, who do not accept the truth. And obstinacy means intense argument. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, his statement Ladda he said: they do not stand upright.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his statement,
h
And to warn with it a hostile people
, meaning: to warn with it an unjust people.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: And you warn with it a people who are argumentative with falsehood, meaning, who are stubborn and quarrelsome.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Muhammad bin Fadil told us, on the authority of Laith, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement,
h
And you warn thereby a hostile people
, he said: wicked.

c: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement, a quarrelsome people, he said: arguing with falsehood.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement,
h
And you warn thereby a hostile people
, he said: The hostile is the unjust, and he recited the statement of God, And He is the most hostile of opponents (al-Baqarah 2:204).

c: Abu Saleh Al-Darari told us: Al-Ala’ bin Abdul-Jabbar told us: Mahdi bin Maymun told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan,
m: regarding the statement of God Almighty, And you warn thereby a people who are obstinate, he said: Deaf to the truth.

c: Ibn Sinan told me: Abu Asim told us, on the authority of Harun, on the authority of Al-Hasan,
m: the same. We have previously explained the meaning of al-ald with its evidence, so there is no need to repeat it here.

x: God the Almighty says: And many, O Muhammad, have We destroyed before your people from the polytheists of Quraysh. From a generation, meaning from a group of people, when they followed my opposition and committed the sins of their path. Do you sense any of them? He says: Do you sense any of them, O Muhammad, so that you see them and witness them or hear their sound meaning: Or hear their voice? Rather, they have perished and died, and their homes have become empty of them, and their dwellings have become desolate of them, and they have gone to a home in which nothing will benefit them except the good deeds they have done. So too are your people, they will end up in what those have ended up in, if they do not hasten to repent before destruction. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Ali told me, he said: Abdullah told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his statement,
h
Or do you hear them making a sound
? He said: A voice.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us: Abd al-Razzaq told us: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement,
h
Do you perceive anyone from them or hear a sound from them
? He said: Do you see an eye or hear a sound?

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement,
h
Do you sense anyone from them or hear a sound from them
? He said: Do you hear a sound, or see an eye?

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid narrated to us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say, in his statement,
h
Or do you hear them making a sound
? He meant: a voice.

c: Abu Kuraib told us: Ibn Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Amr, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said:
m: The noise of the people is their voices. Abu Kuraib said: Sufyan said: Do you sense anyone from them or hear them making noise?

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement,
h
Do you sense anyone from them or hear a sound from them
? He said: Or do you hear a sound from them. He said: And the sound is the sound.

x: In Arabic speech, the word rakz means a low voice, as the poet said: So she was apprehensive about the mention of the companion, and it frightened her from behind her back, while the companion is her illness.

notes.en: Al-Bayhaqī transmitted it in al-Asmāʾ wa-l-ṣifāt, 1/231 (no. 165); al-Thawrī in his Tafsīr, p. 181; and al-Ḍiyāʾ in al-Mukhtārah, 10/56, through Ḥuṣayn. Al-Suyūṭī attributed it in al-Durr al-manthūr, 4/258, to al-Firyābī, Saʿīd ibn Manṣūr, Ibn Abī Ḥātim, Ibn Mardawayh, Ibn al-Mundhir, ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd, and Ibn Abī Shaybah.
notes.ar: أخرجه البيهقى في الأسماء والصفات 1/ 231 (165)، والثورى في تفسيره ص 181، والضياء في المختارة 10/ 56، من طريق حصين به. وعزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 4/ 258 إلى الفريابي وسعيد بن منصور وابن أبي حاتم وابن مردويه وابن المنذر وعبد بن حميد وابن أبي شيبة.

notes.en: Al-Ḥāfiẓ mentioned it in al-Fatḥ, 8/427.
notes.ar: ذكره الحافظ في الفتح 8/ 427.

notes.en: Al-Thawrī’s Tafsīr, p. 181.
notes.ar: تفسير الثورى ص 181.

notes.en: No textual authority is established for the phrase “His name, which is Yamīn.” The names of God are established only by revealed text. Ibn al-Athīr said: “He intended the yāʾ of yamīn. It comes from the expression yammana Allāhu al-insāna, yuyamminuhu, meaning God made a person blessed; thus he is maymūn. God is called Yāmin and Yamīn, just as He is called Qādir and Qadīr.” See al-Nihāyah, 5/300.
notes.ar: قوله: "اسمه الذي هو يمين". لم يثبت فيه نص، وأسماء الله توقيفية. وقال ابن الأثير: أراد الياء من يمين وهو من قولك: يَمن الله الإنسان يُيَمِّنه فهو ميمون. والله يامن ويمين مثل قادر وقدير. النهاية 5/ 300.

notes.en: ʿĀṣim, Ḥamzah, and al-Kisāʾī read {mukhlaṣan} with the lām vowelled fatḥah; the others read it with kasrah. As for the author’s statement, “except ʿĀṣim,” the qirāʾāt works say that ʿĀṣim read it with fatḥah. See al-Taysīr, p. 121; al-Ḥujjah, pp. 444–445; and al-Nashr, 2/221. Ibn Mujāhid, however, states that ʿĀṣim read it with kasrah in Abū Bakr’s transmission and with fatḥah in Ḥafṣ’s transmission. See al-Sabʿah, p. 410.
notes.ar: قرَأ عاصم وحمزة والكسائي: {مُخْلَصًا} بفتح اللام. وقرأ الباقون بكسرها. أما قول المصنف: "خلا عاصم". ففى كتب القراءات أن عاصمًا قرأ بفتح اللام. وينظر التيسير ص 121، والحجة ص 444، 445، والنشر 2/ 221. على أن ابن مجاهد قد ذكر أن عاصمًا قرأ بكسر اللام في رواية أبي بكر عنه وأنه قرأ بفتحها في رواية حفص عنه. وينظر السبعة ص 410.

notes.en: Abū Yaʿlā transmitted it (2914) through Yazīd; Aḥmad, 21/279–280 (13739), and al-Tirmidhī (3157) transmitted it through another chain from Qatādah. Al-Suyūṭī attributed it in al-Durr al-manthūr, 4/274, to Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Mardawayh.
notes.ar: أخرجه أبو يعلى (2914) من طريق يزيد، به، وأخرجه أحمد 21/ 279، 280 (13739)، والترمذي (3157) من طريق آخر عن قتادةَ وعزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 4/ 274 إلى ابن المنذر وابن مردويه.

notes.en: Omitted in Ṣ, M, T1, and F.
notes.ar: سقط من: ص، م، ت 1، ف.

notes.en: In the original: “and bukūyan”; in Ṣ, M, T1, T2, and F: “and they wept.”
notes.ar: في الأصل: "وبكويا"، وفى ص، م، ت 1، ت 2، ف: "وبكوا".

notes.en: Omitted in Ṣ, M, T1, T2, and F.
notes.ar: سقط من: ص، م، ت 1، ت 2، ف.

notes.en: Ibn Kathīr, Nāfiʿ, Abū ʿAmr, and Ibn ʿĀmir, as well as ʿĀṣim in Abū Bakr’s transmission, read these words with ḍammah on their initial letters. Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read all of them with kasrah on their initial letters. Ḥafṣ, transmitting from ʿĀṣim, reads all with kasrah except {wa-bukiyyan}, whose initial letter has ḍammah. Ibn Mujāhid, al-Sabʿah, p. 407.
notes.ar: قرأ ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو وابن عامر وعاصم في رواية أبى بكر، بضم أوائل هذه الحروف، وقرأ حمزة والكسائي بكسر أوائل هذه الحروف كلها وقرأ حفص عن عاصم بكسر أوائل هذه الحروف كلها إلا {وَبُكِيًّا}، فإنه يضم أوله. السبعة لابن مجاهد ص 407.

notes.en: Omitted from the manuscripts; Ibn Kathīr explicitly noted the omission. See the sources documenting the report.
notes.ar: سقط من النسخ، ونص ابن كثير على سقوطه، وينظر مصادر التخريج.

notes.en: Ibn Abī al-Dunyā transmitted it in al-Riqqah wa-l-bukāʾ (423), pp. 123–124, and al-Bayhaqī in Shuʿab al-īmān (2059), through ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, with the addition of Abū Maʿmar, from ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb. Ibn Kathīr, 5/238, attributed it to the author and Ibn Abī Ḥātim through Sufyān. Al-Suyūṭī attributed it in al-Durr al-manthūr, 4/277, to Ibn Abī Ḥātim.
notes.ar: أخرجه ابن أبي الدنيا في الرقة والبكاء (423) 123، 124 والبيهقى في شعب الإيمان (2059) من طريق عبد الرحمن بزيادة أبي معمر عن عمر بن الخطاب، وعزاه ابن كثير 5/ 238 إلى المصنف وابن أبي حاتم من طريق سفيان به وعزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 4/ 277 إلى ابن أبي حاتم.

notes.en: In Ṣ, M, T1, and F: “Saʿd.” He is ʿAlī ibn Saʿīd ibn Masrūq al-Kindī. See Tahdhīb al-kamāl, 20/450.
notes.ar: في ص، م، ت 1، ف: "سعد". وهو على بن سعيد بن مسروق الكندى. ينظر تهذيب الكمال 20/ 450.

notes.en: Abū Nuʿaym transmitted it in al-Ḥilyah, 6/80, through al-Awzāʿī. Al-Suyūṭī attributed it in al-Durr al-manthūr, 4/277, to Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abī Ḥātim.
notes.ar: أخرجه أبو نعيم في الحلية 6/ 80، من طريق الأوزاعي به، وعزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 4/ 277 إلى ابن المنذر وابن أبي حاتم.

notes.en: Tafsīr al-Thawrī, p. 186.
notes.ar: تفسير الثورى ص 186.

notes.en: In T2, after it: “by leaving it.”
notes.ar: بعده في ت 2: بتركها".

notes.en: In Ṣ, M, T1, and F: “something like it.”
notes.ar: في ص، م، ت 1، ف: "نحوه".

notes.en: In M: “for a matter I hasten to.”
notes.ar: في م: "لأمر أعجله".

notes.en: Al-Khaṭīb transmitted it in al-Muttafiq wa-l-muftariq, 1/197–198, through al-Awzāʿī. Al-Suyūṭī attributed it in al-Durr al-manthūr, 4/277, to Ibn Abī Ḥātim.
notes.ar: أخرجه الخطيب في المتفق والمفترق 1/ 197، 198 من طريق الأوزاعى به، وعزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 4/ 277 إلى ابن أبي حاتم.

notes.en: In M and T1: “Masʿūd.” See Tahdhīb al-kamāl, 6/163.
notes.ar: في م، ت 1 ف: "مسعود" وينظر تهذيب الكمال 6/ 163.

notes.en: Al-Baghawī mentioned it in his Tafsīr, 2/415; Ibn Kathīr also mentioned it in his Tafsīr, 5/238.
notes.ar: ذكره البغوي في تفسيره 2415، وابن كثير في تفسيره 5/ 238.

notes.en: Ibn Kathīr mentioned it in his Tafsīr, 5/238.
notes.ar: ذكره ابن كثير في تفسيره 5/ 238.

notes.en: Al-Suyūṭī attributed it in al-Durr al-manthūr, 4/277, to Ibn Abī Ḥātim.
notes.ar: عزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 4/ 277 إلى ابن أبي حاتم.

notes.en: Omitted in M and T2.
notes.ar: سقط من: م، ت 2.

notes.en: In Ṣ, M, T1, T2, and F: “for him.”
notes.ar: في ص، م، ت 1، ت 2، ف: "له".

notes.en: Tafsīr Mujāhid, p. 456. Al-Suyūṭī attributed it in al-Durr al-manthūr, 4/277, to ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd.
notes.ar: تفسير مجاهد ص 456، وعزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 4/ 277 إلى عبد بن حميد.

notes.en: Al-Qurṭubī mentioned it in his Tafsīr, 11/121–122, and Ibn Kathīr in his Tafsīr, 5/239.
notes.ar: ذكره القرطبي في تفسيره 11/ 121، 122، وابن كثير في تفسيره 5/ 239.

notes.en: Tafsīr al-Thawrī, p. 186, through Jābir from Mujāhid, with similar wording. Ibn Kathīr mentioned it, 5/239, through Jābir.
notes.ar: تفسير الثورى ص 186 من طريق جابر عن مجاهد بنحوه، وذكره ابن كثير 5/ 239 عن طريق جابر به.

notes.en: In Ṣ, M, T1, and F: “Abū Tamīm.” See Tahdhīb al-kamāl, 2/211.
notes.ar: في ص، م، ت 1 ف: "أبي تميم". وينظر تهذيب الكمال 2/ 211.

notes.en: Omitted in Ṣ, M, T1, and F. See the sources documenting the report.
notes.ar: سقط من: ص، م، ت 1 ف. وينظر مصادر التخريج.

notes.en: In Ṣ, M, T1, T2, and F, after it: “and the donkeys.”
notes.ar: بعده في ص، م، ت 1، ت 2، ف: "والحمر".

notes.en: Omitted in Ṣ, M, T1, T2, and F.
notes.ar: سقط من: ص، م، ت 1، ت 2، ف.

notes.en: Tafsīr al-Thawrī, p. 186, through Ibrāhīm from Mujāhid. Al-Suyūṭī attributed it in al-Durr al-manthūr, 4/277, to ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd.
notes.ar: تفسير الثورى ص 186 من طريق إبراهيم عن مجاهد به، وعزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 4/ 277 إلى عبد بن حميد.

notes.en: In Ṣ, T1, and F: “Zabān”; in M: “Razān”; in T2: “Zarān.” See al-Dāraquṭnī’s al-Muʾtalif wa-l-mukhtalif, 2/1087.
notes.ar: في ص، ت 1، ف: "زبان"، وفى م: "رزان" وفى ت:2 "زران" وينظر المؤتلف والمختلف للدارقطني 2/ 1087.

notes.en: In M: “awāqin.” The adopted wording agrees with Ṣifat al-nār. ʿAsharāwāt is the plural of ʿashrāʾ, a she-camel that has reached ten months of pregnancy. See al-Nihāyah, 3/240.
notes.ar: في م: "أواقٍ" والمثبت موافق لما في صفة النار. والعشراوات: جمع عشراء وهى الناقة التي أتي على حملها عشرة أشهر. ينظر النهاية 3/ 240.

notes.en: Ibn Kathīr mentioned it in his Tafsīr, 5/240, from the author. Al-Ṭabarānī transmitted it (7731) through al-ʿAbbās ibn Abī Ṭālib; Muḥammad ibn Naṣr in Kitāb al-ṣalāh (36) and al-Bayhaqī in al-Baʿth (522) through Muḥammad ibn Ziyād; and Ibn Abī al-Dunyā in Ṣifat al-nār (17) through Sharqī. Al-Suyūṭī attributed it in al-Durr al-manthūr, 4/278, to Ibn Mardawayh.
notes.ar: ذكره ابن كثير في تفسيره 5/ 240 عن المصنف، وأخرجه الطبراني (7731) من طريق العباس بن أبي طالب به، وأخرجه محمد بن نصر في كتاب الصلاة (36)، والبيهقى في البعث (522) من طريق محمد بن زياد به، وأخرجه ابن أبي الدنيا في صفة النار (17) من طريق شرقى به، وعزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 4/ 278 إلى ابن مردويه.

notes.en: Abū Ḥayyān mentioned it in al-Baḥr al-muḥīṭ, 6/201, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr.
notes.ar: ذكره في البحر المحيط 6/ 201 عن عبد الله بن عمرو.

notes.en: Tafsīr al-Thawrī, p. 187; through him, al-Ṭabarānī in al-Kabīr (9110). Al-Ṭabarānī also transmitted it (9106, 9107) through Abū Isḥāq.
notes.ar: تفسير الثورى ص 187، ومن طريقه الطبراني في الكبير (9110)، وأخرجه الطبراني (9106، 9107) من طريق أبي إسحاق به.

notes.en: Abū Nuʿaym transmitted it in al-Ḥilyah, 4/206, through Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar. Al-Ḥākim, 2/374; al-Ṭabarānī in al-Kabīr (9111); and al-Bayhaqī in al-Baʿth (518) transmitted it through Shuʿbah.
notes.ar: أخرجه أبو نعيم. جه أبو نعيم في الحلية 4/ 206 من طريق محمد بن جعفر به، وأخرجه الحاكم 2/ 374، والطبراني في الكبير (9111)، والبيهقى في البعث (518) من طريق شعبة به.

notes.en: Al-Ṭabarānī transmitted it in al-Kabīr (9108), and al-Bayhaqī in al-Baʿth (519), through Abū al-Aḥwaṣ. Ṣ, M, T1, and F add after this: “Al-Qāsim told us: al-Ḥusayn told us: Abū al-Aḥwaṣ told us, from Abū Isḥāq, from Abū ʿUbaydah, from his father, who said regarding ‘Then after them came successors who neglected prayer and followed desires, so they will encounter ruin’: ‘Ghayy is a river in Hell, in which those who followed their desires are punished.’”
notes.ar: أخرجه الطبراني في الكبير (9108)، والبيهقى في البعث (519) من طريق أبى الأحوص به. وبعده في ص، م، ت 1، ف: "حدثنا القاسم قال ثنا الحسين قال ثنا أبو الأحوص عن أبي إسحاق عن أبي عبيدة عن أبيه قوله: {فَخَلَفَ مِنْ بَعْدِهِمْ خَلْفٌ أَضَاعُوا الصَّلَاةَ وَاتَّبَعُوا الشَّهَوَاتِ فَسَوْفَ يَلْقَوْنَ غَيًّا} قال: الغى نهر جهنم في النار يعذب فيه الذين اتبعوا الشهوات".

notes.en: Abū al-Aḥwaṣ is Sallām ibn Sulaym. See Tahdhīb al-kamāl, 33/16.
notes.ar: أبو الأحوص: سلام بن سليم ينظر تهذيب الكمال 33/ 16.

notes.en: In M: “ʿUbaydah.” He is Abū al-Aḥwaṣ al-Jushamī, ʿAwf ibn Mālik. See Tahdhīb al-kamāl, 33/16.
notes.ar: في م: "عبيدة". وهو أبو الأحوص الجشمى؛ عوف بن مالك. ينظر تهذيب الكمال 33/ 16.

notes.en: In the original: “he is punished.” The adopted wording agrees with the sources documenting the report.
notes.ar: في الأصل: "يعذب". والمثبت موافق لما في مصادر التخريج.

notes.en: Ibn Abī al-Dunyā transmitted it in Ṣifat al-nār (38) through Abū al-Aḥwaṣ.
notes.ar: أخرجه ابن أبي الدنيا في صفة النار (38) من طريق أبى الأحوص به.

notes.en: Al-Suyūṭī attributed it in al-Durr al-manthūr, 4/278, to Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abī Ḥātim. Ibn Kathīr mentioned it in his Tafsīr, 5/240, from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭalḥah.
notes.ar: عزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 4/ 278 إلى ابن المنذر وابن أبي حاتم، وذكره ابن كثير في تفسيره 5/ 240 عن علي بن عباس به.

notes.en: Al-Qurṭubī mentioned it in his Tafsīr, 5/125; see also al-Tibyān, 7/121.
notes.ar: ذكره القرطبي في تفسيره 5/ 125، وينظر التبيان 7/ 121.

notes.en: The verse is by al-Muraqqish al-Aṣghar, in al-Mufaḍḍaliyyāt, p. 247; al-Aghānī, 6/139; and al-Marzubānī’s Muʿjam al-shuʿarāʾ, p. 5.
notes.ar: البيت للمرقش الأصغر في المفضليات ص 247، والأغانى 6/ 139، ومعجم الشعراء للمرزبانى ص 5.

notes.en: In M: “the meaning.”
notes.ar: في م: "المعنى".

notes.en: Omitted in Ṣ, M, T1, and F.
notes.ar: سقط من: ص، م، ت 1، ف.

notes.en: In Ṣ, M, and F: “their error.”
notes.ar: في ص، م، ف: "ضلالهم".

notes.en: In the original, after it: “and they will not be wronged.”
notes.ar: بعده في الأصل: "ولا يظلمون".

notes.en: Cited earlier, 11/559 ff.
notes.ar: تقدم في 11/ 559 وما بعدها.

notes.en: Al-Farrāʾ, Maʿānī al-Qurʾān, 2/170.
notes.ar: الفراء في معاني القرآن 2/ 170.

notes.en: In M: “the guidance.”
notes.ar: في م: "الهدى".

notes.en: In M: “and.”
notes.ar: في م: "و".

notes.en: Omitted in Ṣ, M, T1, T2, and F.
notes.ar: سقط من: ص، م، ت 1، ت 2، ف.

notes.en: In Ṣ, M, T1, T2, and F, after it: “just as.”
notes.ar: بعده في ص، م، ت 1، ت 2، ف: "كما".

notes.en: Ibn Kathīr mentioned it in his Tafsīr, 5/242, from the author. Al-Suyūṭī attributed it in al-Durr al-manthūr, 4/278, to the author, Ibn al-Mundhir (repeated in the source), and Ibn Abī Ḥātim.
notes.ar: ذكره ابن كثير في تفسيره 5/ 242 عن المصنف، وعزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 4/ 278 إلى المصنف وابن المنذر وابن المنذر وابن أبي حاتم.

notes.en: In Ṣ, T1, and F: “son.”
notes.ar: في ص، ت 1، ف: "بن".

notes.en: In the original, after it: “Paradise.”
notes.ar: بعده في الأصل: "الجنة".

notes.en: Omitted in Ṣ, T1, and F. M and Tafsīr Ibn Kathīr read: “so they overwhelm them.”
notes.ar: سقط من: ص، ت 1، ف، وفى م، وتفسير ابن كثير: "فتهمهم".

notes.en: Ibn Kathīr mentioned it in his Tafsīr, 5/242, from the author. Al-Suyūṭī attributed it in al-Durr al-manthūr, 5/318, to the author and Ibn al-Mundhir; see also Fayḍ al-Qadīr, 1/37.
notes.ar: ذكره ابن كثير في تفسيره 5/ 242 عن المصنف، وعزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 5/ 318 إلى المصنف وابن المنذر، وينظر فيض القدير 1/ 37.

notes.en: Al-Suyūṭī attributed it in al-Durr al-manthūr, 4/278, to Ibn al-Mundhir.
notes.ar: عزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 4/ 278 إلى ابن المنذر.

notes.en: Tafsīr ʿAbd al-Razzāq adds after it: “their provision.”
notes.ar: بعده في تفسير عبد الرزاق: "رزقهم".

notes.en: Tafsīr ʿAbd al-Razzāq, 2/9.
notes.ar: تفسير عبد الرزاق 2/ 9.

notes.en: Tafsīr al-Thawrī, p. 187; through him, ʿAbd al-Razzāq in his Tafsīr, 2/9, and Hannād in al-Zuhd (59). Al-Suyūṭī attributed it in al-Durr al-manthūr, 4/278, to ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abī Ḥātim.
notes.ar: تفسير الثورى ص 187، ومن طريقه عبد الرزاق في تفسيره 2/ 9، وهناد في الزهد (59) وعزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 4/ 278 إلى عبد بن حميد وابن المنذر وابن أبي حاتم.

notes.en: In the original: “in the evening.”
notes.ar: في الأصل: "عشيا".

notes.en: In T2: “he said.”
notes.ar: في ت 2: "قال".

notes.en: Ibn Kathīr mentioned it in his Tafsīr, 5/242, from Qatādah.
notes.ar: ذكره ابن كثير في تفسيره 5/ 242 عن قتادة.

notes.en: In Ṣ, M, T1, and F: “punishment.”
notes.ar: في ص، م، ت 1، ف: "عذاب".

notes.en: Omitted in Ṣ, M, T1, T2, and F. See the earlier discussion, 15/144.
notes.ar: سقط من: ص، م، ت 1، ت 2، ف. وينظر ما تقدم في 15/ 144.

notes.en: In the original, Ṣ, M, T1, and F: “whoever said that.”
notes.ar: في الأصل، ص، م، ت 1، ف: "من قال ذلك".

notes.en: M adds after it: “He said: ʿAbd Allāh told us.” See al-Jarḥ wa-l-taʿdīl, 5/10.
notes.ar: بعده في م: "قال: ثنا عبد الله". وينظر الجرح والتعديل 5/ 10.

notes.en: Omitted in Ṣ, M, T1, T2, and F.
notes.ar: سقط من: ص، م، ت 1، ت 2، ف.

notes.en: Aḥmad, 3/502 (2078); al-Bukhārī (3218); and al-Tirmidhī (3158) transmitted it through Wakīʿ, without its ending. Aḥmad, 5/363 (3365), and al-Bukhārī (7455) transmitted it through ʿUmar ibn Dharr. With the additional ending, al-Suyūṭī attributed it in al-Durr al-manthūr, 4/278, to Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abī Ḥātim; without the addition, he attributed it to ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd and Ibn Mardawayh.
notes.ar: أخرجه أحمد 3/ 502 (2078)، والبخارى (3218)، والترمذى (3158) من طريق وكيع به - دون آخره - وأخرجه أحمد 5/ 363 (3365)، والبخارى (7455) من طريق عمر بن ذر به، وبالزيادة في آخره عزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 4/ 278 إلى ابن المنذر وابن أبي حاتم، ودون الزيادة عزاه إلى عبد بن حميد وابن مردويه.

notes.en: Omitted in Ṣ, M, T1, T2, and F.
notes.ar: سقط من: ص، م، ت 1، ت 2، ف.

notes.en: Aḥmad, 3/481–482 (2013); al-Bukhārī (3218, 4731), and in Khalq afʿāl al-ʿibād (574); al-Tirmidhī (3158); al-Nasāʾī in al-Sunan al-kubrā (11319); al-Ṭabarānī (12385); al-Ḥākim, 2/611; al-Bayhaqī in al-Asmāʾ wa-l-ṣifāt (4625) and al-Dalāʾil, 7/60; al-Wāḥidī in Asbāb al-nuzūl, p. 203; Abū Nuʿaym in al-Ḥilyah, 4/298; and al-Baghawī in his Tafsīr, 5/243, transmitted it through chains from ʿUmar ibn Dharr.
notes.ar: أخرجه أحمد 3/ 481، 482 (2013)، والبخارى (3218، 4731)، وفى خلق أفعال العباد (574)، والترمذى (3158)، والنسائى في الكبرى (11319)، والطبرانى (12385)، والحاكم 2/ 611، والبيهقى في الأسماء والصفات (4625)، وفى الدلائل 7/ 60، والواحدى في أسباب النزول ص 203، وأبو نعيم في الحلية 4/ 298، والبغوى في تفسيره 5/ 243 من طرق عن عمر بن ذر به.

notes.en: Ibn Kathīr mentioned it in his Tafsīr, 5/244, from al-ʿAwfī.
notes.ar: ذكره ابن كثير في تفسيره 5/ 244 عن العوفى به.

notes.en: In Ṣ, M, T1, T2, and F: “the verse.” The report appears in Tafsīr ʿAbd al-Razzāq, 2/10.
notes.ar: في ص، م، ت 1، ت 2، ف: "الآية". والأثر في تفسير عبد الرزاق 2/ 10.

notes.en: In the original: “stagnant.” Abū ʿUbayd transmitted the report in Gharīb al-ḥadīth, 4/346—and al-Bayhaqī transmitted it through him in Shuʿab al-īmān following report 373—from Marwān ibn Muʿāwiyah. Ibn al-Mubārak transmitted it in al-Zuhd (407); Abū ʿUbayd, 4/347; Ibn Abī Shaybah, 13/561; Hannād in al-Zuhd (231); and Abū Nuʿaym in al-Ḥilyah, 5/212, through Sufyān, from Thawr (in Ibn al-Mubārak: “a man”), from Khālid. Al-Suyūṭī attributed it in al-Durr al-manthūr, 4/281, to ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd, al-Ḥakīm, and Ibn al-Anbārī in al-Maṣāḥif.
notes.ar: في الأصل: "جامدة". والأثر أخرجه أبو عبيد في غريب الحديث 4/ 346 - ومن طريقه البيهقى في الشعب عقب الأثر (373) - عن مروان بن معاوية به. وأخرجه ابن المبارك في الزهد (407)، وأبو عبيد في 4/ 347، وابن أبى شيبة 13/ 561، وهناد في الزهد (231)، وأبو نعيم في الحلية 5/ 212 من طريق سفيان، عن ثور - وعند ابن المبارك: رجل - عن خالد. وعزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 4/ 281 إلى عبد بن حميد والحكيم وابن الأنبارى في المصاحف.

notes.en: ʾIhālah means any fat used as a condiment, such as olive or sesame oil. It is also said to mean fat rendered from a camel’s hump or other fat. Matn al-ihālah (“the solidified fat”) is its upper surface when it settles in a vessel. See Abū ʿUbayd’s Gharīb al-ḥadīth, 4/346.
notes.ar: الإهالة: كل شيء من الأدهان مما يؤتدم به مثل الزيت ودهن السمسم، وقيل: ما أذيب من الألية والشحم. ومتن الإهالة: ظهرها إذا سكنت في الإناء. ينظر غريب الحديث لأبى عبيد 4/ 346.

notes.en: Abū Nuʿaym transmitted it in al-Ḥilyah, 5/367, through al-Jarīrī, without its ending. Ibn al-Mubārak in al-Zuhd (405); Abū ʿUbayd in Gharīb al-ḥadīth, 4/346; Ibn Abī Shaybah, 13/169; and Abū Nuʿaym in al-Ḥilyah, 5/369, transmitted it through al-Jarīrī, from Abū al-Salīl, from Ghunaym ibn Qays, from Abū al-ʿAwwām, in both longer and shorter forms. Al-Suyūṭī cited it in al-Durr al-manthūr, 4/281, from Abū al-ʿAwwām, from Kaʿb, and attributed it to ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd and Ibn Abī Ḥātim.

Al-Suyūṭī attributed it in al-Durr al-manthūr, 4/282, to Saʿīd ibn Manṣūr, ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd, and al-Bayhaqī in Shuʿab al-īmān.

Al-Suyūṭī attributed it in al-Durr al-manthūr, 4/281, to Ibn Abī Ḥātim, all as a report stopped at Ibn Zayd and without the beginning of the portion traced to the Prophet. For the marfūʿ version, see al-Bayhaqī’s Shuʿab al-īmān (367), from Anas.

notes.en: (9676)—and, through Ibn Abī Shaybah and Aḥmad, al-Ṭabarānī in Musnad al-Shāmiyyīn (561)—as well as Hannād in al-Zuhd (391), al-Tirmidhī (2088), Abū Nuʿaym in al-Ḥilyah, 6/86, Ibn ʿAbd al-Barr in al-Tamhīd, 6/359 (which omits Abū Ṣāliḥ), al-Ḥākim, 1/345, and al-Bayhaqī in Shuʿab al-īmān (9844) transmitted it through Abū Usāmah, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Yazīd ibn Jābir, from Ismāʿīl. Abū Dāwūd said—as recorded in al-Ājurrī’s Questions (327)—that ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Yazīd ibn Tamīm was munkar al-ḥadīth. Abū Usāmah narrated from him but mistakenly gave his name as ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Yazīd al-Sulamī ibn Jābir. Whenever Abū Usāmah says “ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Yazīd narrated to us,” he means Ibn Tamīm. See Tahdhīb al-kamāl, 17/482 and 18/5.
notes.ar: = (9676) - ومن طريق ابن أبي شيبة وأحمد أخرجه الطبراني في مسند الشاميين (561) - وهناد في الزهد (391)، والترمذى (2088) وأبو نعيم في الحلية 6/ 86، وابن عبد البر في التمهيد 6/ 359 - وسقط منه ذكر أبى صالح - والحاكم 1/ 345، والبيهقى في الشعب (9844) من طريق أبى أسامة، عن عبد الرحمن بن يزيد بن جابر، عن إسماعيل به. قال أبو داود - كما في سؤالات الآجرى (327) - عن عبد الرحمن بن يزيد بن تميم: منكر الحديث، حدث عنه أبو أسامة وغلط في اسمه فقال: نا عبد الرحمن بن يزيد بن جابر السلمى، وكل ما جاء عن أبي أسامة: حدثنا عبد الرحمن بن يزيد. فهو ابن تميم. وينظر تهذيب الكمال 17/ 482، 18/ 5.

notes.en: Al-Tirmidhī transmitted it (3160) through Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd; al-Ḥākim, 4/587, through Shuʿbah. Ibn Kathīr attributed it in his Tafsīr, 5/249, to Ibn Abī Ḥātim. notes.en: In Ṣ, M, T1, T2, and F: “kawā or karā.” The sources documenting the report read “such-and-such”; Ibn Mandah’s version has “kawā”; and another has “such-and-such—or such-and-such.” See which applies. This is how the report appears in all the manuscripts, but it has undergone extensive alteration and corruption. Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ said its correct wording is: “We will come on the Day of Resurrection upon heaps…” All this shows how the report was altered: this word was unclear to the transmitter or had been erased, so he rendered it “such-and-such” and explained it as “above the people,” writing “see” as a note. Later transmitters gathered all of this and arranged it as part of the report’s text, as it now appears. See Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim with al-Nawawī’s commentary, 3/47.
notes.ar:
في ص، م، ت 1، ت 2، ف: "كوى أو كرى"، والذي في مصادر التخريج: كذا - وفى رواية لابن منده: كوا - وكذا - أو كذا - انظر أي ذلك. هذه صورة الحديث في جميع النسخ، وفيه تغيير كثير وتصحيف. قال: وقال القاضي عياض: وصوابه: نجئ يوم القيامة على كوم 
…. فهذا كله يبين ما تغير من الحديث وأنه كان أظلم هذا الحرف على الرواى، أو امحى فعبر عنه بكذا وكذا وفسره بقوله: أي: فوق الناس. وكتب عليه: انظر. تنبيها، فجمع النقلة الكل ونسقوه على أنه من متن الحديث كما تراه. ينظر صحيح مسلم بشرح النووى 3/ 47.

notes.en: ʿAlīq is a small thorny shrub. Anything caught in it is difficult to free because of its many thorns, which are sharp and jagged. Lisān al-ʿArab (root ʿ-l-q).

Al-Baghawī mentioned it in his Tafsīr, 5/255; Ibn Kathīr reproduced its chain and wording in his Tafsīr, 5/259; al-Suyūṭī attributed it in al-Durr al-manthūr, 4/284, to Ibn al-Mundhir.

Ibn Ḥajar transmitted it in Taghlīq al-taʿlīq, 3/509, through ʿAbd Allāh. Al-Bayhaqī cited it without a full chain in Shuʿab al-īmān, 1/317, from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭalḥah.
notes.ar: أخرجه البخارى معلقا عن ابن عباس (فتح البارى 8/ 427)، وأخرجه ابن أبي حاتم في تفسيره من طريق عبد الله به، كما في تغليق التعليق 3/ 509، وأخرجه الحافظ ابن حجر في التغليق 3/ 509 من طريق عبد الله به، وعلقه البيهقي في شعب الإيمان 1/ 317 عن علي بن أبي طلحة به.

notes.en: Abū Ḥayyān mentioned it in al-Baḥr al-muḥīṭ, 6/217, and al-Qurṭubī in his Tafsīr, 11/152–153. Al-Suyūṭī attributed it in al-Durr al-manthūr, 4/286, to Ibn al-Mundhir.
notes.ar: ذكره أبو حيان في البحر المحيط 6/ 217، والقرطبي في تفسيره 11/ 152، 153، وعزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 4/ 286 إلى ابن المنذر.

notes.en: Ibn Abī Shaybah transmitted it, 13/172 (16025), and Hannād in al-Zuhd (286, 287), through two other chains from al-Ḥasan.
notes.ar: أخرجه ابن أبي شيبة 13/ 172 (16025)، وهناد في الزهد (286، 287) من طريقين آخرين عن الحسن.

notes.en: Ṣ, M, T1, and F add after it: “He said: Saʿīd told us.” Saʿīd ibn Abī ʿArūbah did not narrate from Yūnus ibn ʿUbayd. See Tahdhīb al-kamāl, 11/5 and 32/124, 517.
notes.ar: بعده في ص، م، ت 1، ف: "قال: ثنا سعيد". وسعيد بن أبي عروبة لم يرو عن يونس بن عبيد. ينظر تهذيب الكمال 11/ 5، 32/ 124، 517.

notes.en: In T1: “Qatādah.”
notes.ar: في ت:1: "قتادة".

notes.en: Tafsīr ʿAbd al-Razzāq, 2/13, from Maʿmar. Al-Suyūṭī attributed it in al-Durr al-manthūr, 4/286, to ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd.
notes.ar: تفسير عبد الرزاق 2/ 13 عن معمر به، وعزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 4/ 286 إلى عبد بن حميد.

notes.en: In Ṣ, M, T1, T2, and F: “drive them.”
notes.ar: في ص، م، ت 1، ت 2 ف: "سوقوا".

notes.en: In M: “thirst.”
notes.ar: في م: "ظمء".

notes.en: That is, these unbelievers will intercede for one another just as the people of faith intercede for one another.
notes.ar: أي فيشفع هؤلاء الكفار بعضهم لبعض، كما يشفع أهل الإيمان بعضهم لبعض.

notes.en: Omitted in Ṣ, T1, and F.
notes.ar: سقط من: ص، ت 1، ف.

notes.en: Al-Ṭabarānī transmitted it in al-Duʿāʾ, 3/1518 (1570), and al-Bayhaqī in al-Asmāʾ wa-l-ṣifāt, 1/272 (206), both through ʿAbd Allāh. Al-Duʿāʾ reads “and it is the root of all piety” instead of “and he hopes in none but God.” Al-Suyūṭī attributed it in al-Durr al-manthūr, 4/286, to Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abī Ḥātim.
notes.ar: أخرجه الطبراني في الدعاء 3/ 1518 (1570)، والبيهقى في الأسماء والصفات 1/ 272 (206)، كلاهما من طريق عبد الله به، وفى الدعاء: "وهى رأس كل تقوى" بدل "ولا يرجو إلا الله"، وعزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 4/ 286 إلى ابن المنذر وابن أبي حاتم.

notes.en: Al-Suyūṭī attributed its first half in al-Durr al-manthūr, 4/286, to Ibn al-Mundhir. Al-Ṭūsī in al-Tibyān, 7/134, and Abū Ḥayyān in al-Baḥr al-muḥīṭ, 6/217, mentioned its second half.
notes.ar: عزا السيوطي في الدر المنثور 4/ 286 شطره الأول إلى ابن المنذر، وذكر الطوسي في التبيان 7/ 134، وأبو حيان في البحر المحيط 6/ 217 شطره الأخير.

notes.en: In M: “so they may know”; in T1 and F: “they know”; in T2: “so they may know.” Taʿallamū means “know.” See Lisān al-ʿArab (root ʿ-l-m).
notes.ar: في م: "ليعلموا، وفى ت 1، ف: "يعلمون"، وفى ت 2: "يعلموا". وتعلَّموا: اعلَمُوا. ينظر اللسان (ع ل م).

notes.en: In M: “They will intercede on the Day of Resurrection.” Al-Durr al-manthūr has: “The believers will intercede on the Day of Resurrection.”
notes.ar: في م: "يوم القيامة يشفع". وجاءت العبارة في الدر المنثور: يشفع المؤمنين يوم القيامة.

notes.en: Al-Suyūṭī cited it at length in al-Durr al-manthūr, 6/285, attributing it to ʿAbd al-Razzāq, ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd, and Ibn al-Mundhir. His version omits “that is, by obedience to Him … and He approved his speech.” Al-Ṭabarānī in al-Kabīr, 22/76 (188); Abū Nuʿaym in al-Ḥilyah, 10/304–305; and al-Khaṭīb in Tārīkh Baghdād, 5/26, transmitted the Prophet’s words “There is a man in my community,” identifying him as Tamīm, through Qatādah, from Abū al-Malīḥ, from Wāthilah ibn al-Asqaʿ. As for Qatādah’s statement, “We used to say that the martyr …,” Abū Dāwūd (2522); Ibn Ḥibbān (4660); al-Ājurrī in al-Sharīʿah, 3/1244–1245 (813, 814); and al-Bayhaqī in al-Sunan al-kubrā, 9/164, transmitted it from Abū al-Dardāʾ, may God be pleased with him.
notes.ar:
ذكره السيوطي في الدر المنثور 6/ 285 مطولا، وعزاه إلى عبد الرزاق وعبد بن حميد وابن المنذر، وليس عنده قوله: "أي بطاعته 
…. ورضى له قولا". وأخرج الطبراني في الكبير 22/ 76 (188)، وأبو نعيم في الحلية 10/ 304، 305، والخطيب في تاريخ بغداد 5/ 26 من طريق قتادة عن أبي المليح عن واثلة بن الأسقع مرفوعا، قوله: "إن في أمتى رجلا" "تميم". أما قول قتادة: وكنا نحدث أن الشهيد أخرج هذا الحديث مرفوعا: أبو داود (2522)، وابن حبان (4660)، والآجرى في الشريعة 3/ 1244، 1245 (813، 814)، والبيهقى في السنن الكبرى 9/ 164، من حديث أبي الدرداء عنه رضي الله عنه.

notes.en: Aḥmad, 6/29, and al-Tirmidhī (2441) transmitted it through Saʿīd, at length, both adding material at the beginning. Aḥmad, 6/28–29, and al-Tirmidhī (2441) also transmitted it through Abū ʿAwānah, from Qatādah, at length, likewise with an addition at the beginning.
notes.ar: أخرجه أحمد 6/ 29، والترمذى (2441)، كلاهما من طريق سعيد به، مطولًا بزيادة في أوله عندهما. وأخرجه أحمد 6/ 28، 29، والترمذى (2441) كلاهما من طريق أبي عوانة عن قتادة به، مطولا بزيادة أوله عندهما.

notes.en: In Ṣ, T1, and F: “punishment”; in M: “numbers.”
notes.ar: في ص، ت 1، ف: "عذاب"، وفى م: "أعداد".

notes.en: Al-Bukhārī cited it without a full chain from Ibn ʿAbbās (Fatḥ al-bārī, 8/427). Ibn Abī Ḥātim transmitted it through Abū Ṣāliḥ ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ṣāliḥ, as cited in Taghlīq al-taʿlīq, 4/249. Al-Suyūṭī attributed it in al-Durr al-manthūr, 4/286, to Ibn al-Mundhir.
notes.ar: علقه البخاري عن ابن عباس (الفتح 8/ 427)، وأخرجه ابن أبي حاتم - كما في تغليق التعليق 4/ 249 - من طريق أبي صالح عبد الله بن صالح به، وعزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 4/ 286 إلى ابن المنذر.

notes.en: Al-Ṭūsī mentioned it in al-Tibyān, 7/134, with the wording “a great abomination”; al-Baghawī in his Tafsīr, 5/256, with “an abomination”; and al-Qurṭubī in his Tafsīr, 11/156, with a negation of the wording found in al-Tibyān.
notes.ar: ذكره الطوسى في التبيان 7/ 134 بلفظ "منكرا عظيما"، والبغوى في تفسيره 5/ 256 بلفظ "منكرا"، والقرطبي في تفسيره 11/ 156 بنفى لفظ التبيان.

notes.en: In Ṣ, M, and F: “he told us.”
notes.ar: في ص، م، ف: "ثنا".

notes.en: Tafsīr Mujāhid, p. 459, through Warqāʾ. Al-Firyābī transmitted it through Warqāʾ, as cited in Taghlīq al-taʿlīq, 4/249. Al-Baghawī mentioned it in his Tafsīr, 5/256, and Ibn Kathīr in his Tafsīr, 5/261.
notes.ar: تفسير مجاهد ص 459 من طريق ورقاء به، وأخرجه الفريابي - كما في تغليق التعليق 4/ 249 - عن ورقاء به، وذكره البغوي في تفسيره 5/ 256، وابن كثير في تفسيره 5/ 261.

notes.en: Tafsīr ʿAbd al-Razzāq, 2/13, from Maʿmar. Al-Baghawī mentioned it in his Tafsīr, 5/256, and Ibn Kathīr in his Tafsīr, 5/261.
notes.ar: تفسير عبد الرزاق 2/ 13 عن معمر به وذكره البغوي في تفسيره 5/ 256، وابن كثير في تفسيره 5/ 261.

notes.en: Al-Ṭūsī mentioned it in al-Tibyān, 7/134, with the wording “a great abomination.”
notes.ar: ذكره الطوسى في التبيان 7/ 134 بلفظ "منكرا عظيما".

notes.en: Omitted in M.
notes.ar: سقط من: م.

notes.en: ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib read it likewise. See Ibn Khālawayh’s Mukhtaṣar al-shawādhdh, p. 89; Tafsīr al-Qurṭubī, 11/156; and al-Baḥr al-muḥīṭ, 6/218.
notes.ar: وكذا قراءة: على بن أبى طالب، ينظر مختصر الشواذ لابن خالويه ص 89، وتفسير القرطبي 11/ 156، والبحر المحيط 6/ 218.

notes.en: Cited earlier, p. 337, where it reads “peers” instead of “enemies.”
notes.ar: تقدم في ص 337، وفيه "الأقران" بدلا من "الأعداء".

notes.en: The verse is in al-Tibyān, 7/134, unattributed.
notes.ar: البيت في التبيان 7/ 134 غير منسوب.

notes.en: Lahath and luhāth mean the burning thirst deep inside the body. Lisān al-ʿArab (root l-h-th).
notes.ar: اللَّهث واللُّهاث: حرُّ العطش في الجوف. اللسان (ل هـ ث).

notes.en: In Ṣ, M, T1, and F: “kathal”; al-Tibyān reads “ḥabal.” Khatl means to deceive someone unawares. Lisān al-ʿArab (root kh-t-l).
notes.ar: في ص، م، ت 1، ف: "حثل"، وفي التبيان: "حبل". والخَتْل: تَخَادُعٌ عن غفلةٍ. اللسان (خ ت ل).

notes.en: In Ṣ and T1: “a split.” See al-Tibyān, 7/135.
notes.ar: في ص، ت 1: "شق". وينظر التبيان 7/ 135.

notes.en: Al-Muʿjam al-kabīr reads: “soundness.”
notes.ar: في المعجم الكبير: "صحة".

notes.en: In the original and T1: “the earth.”
notes.ar: في الأصل، ت 1: "الأرض".

notes.en: Ibn Kathīr reproduced it with its chain and wording in his Tafsīr, 5/261. Al-Ṭabarānī transmitted the portion traced from Ibn ʿAbbās to the Prophet in al-Muʿjam al-kabīr, 12/254 (13024), through ʿAbd Allāh. Al-Suyūṭī mentioned the portion stopped at Ibn ʿAbbās in al-Durr al-manthūr, 4/286, attributing it to the author, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abī Ḥātim.
notes.ar: نقله ابن كثير في تفسيره 5/ 261 بإسناده ولفظه، وأخرج الطبراني في المعجم الكبير 12/ 254 (13024) من طريق عبد الله به الجزء المرفوع من ابن عباس للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم، وذكر السيوطي في الدر المنثور 4/ 286 الجزء الموقوف على ابن عباسٍ وعزاه إلى المصنف وابن المنذر وابن أبي حاتم.

notes.en: Al-Suyūṭī mentioned it in al-Durr al-manthūr, 4/287, attributing it to Ibn al-Mundhir.
notes.ar: ذكره السيوطي في الدر المنثور 4/ 287 وعزاه إلى ابن المنذر.

notes.en: Omitted in Ṣ, M, T1, T2, and F.
notes.ar: سقط من: ص، م، ت 1، ت 2، ف.

notes.en: Ibn Kathīr mentioned it in his Tafsīr, 5/262, from Kaʿb.
notes.ar: ذكره ابن كثير في تفسيره 5/ 262 عن كعب.

notes.en: In Ṣ, T1, and T2: “so it splits apart.”
notes.ar: في ص، ت 1، ت 2: "فتتصدع".

notes.en: Ibn Abī Ḥātim transmitted it—as cited in Taghlīq al-taʿlīq, 4/251—through Abū Ṣāliḥ ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ṣāliḥ. Ibn Kathīr mentioned it in his Tafsīr, 5/261. Al-Suyūṭī attributed it in al-Durr al-manthūr, 4/286, to the author, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abī Ḥātim.
notes.ar: أخرجه ابن أبي حاتم - كما في تغليق التعليق 4/ 251 - من طريق أبي صالح عبد الله بن صالح به، وذكره ابن كثير في تفسيره 5/ 261، وعزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 4/ 286 إلى المصنف وابن المنذر وابن أبي حاتم.

notes.en: In Ṣ: “and they made them both.”
notes.ar: في ص: "وجعلوهما".

notes.en: In Ṣ, M, T1, T2, and F: “with him.”
notes.ar: في ص، م، ت 1، ت 2، ف: "معه".

notes.en: Ibn Kathīr mentioned it briefly in his Tafsīr, 5/261, with the wording “out of anger for God.”
notes.ar: ذكره ابن كثير في تفسيره 5/ 261 مختصرا بلفظ "غضبا لله".

notes.en: See Maʿānī al-Qurʾān, 2/173.
notes.ar: ينظر معاني القرآن 2/ 173.

notes.en: Cited earlier, 7/726.
notes.ar: تقدم في 7/ 726.

notes.en: The verse appears in Majāz al-Qurʾān, 2/12; al-Tibyān, 7/136; al-Baḥr al-muḥīṭ, 6/219; and Lisān al-ʿArab (root d-ʿ-w), unattributed in all of them. Al-Baḥr al-muḥīṭ gives it as: “How many a person is called a sincere friend, yet when absent … you find, in his absence, no sincerity from him.”
notes.ar:
البيت في مجاز القرآن 2/ 12، والتبيان 7/ 136، والبحر المحيط 6/ 219، واللسان (د ع و)، غير منسوب عندهم جميعًا. وجاء في البحر المحيط هكذا: ألا رب من يُدعى نصيحا وإن يغب 
…. تجده بغيب منك غير نصيح

notes.en: In the original: “he is absent.”
notes.ar: في الأصل: "يغب".

notes.en: The verse appears in Majāz al-Qurʾān, 2/13; Muḥammad ibn Dāwūd al-Jarrāḥ’s Min ismuhu ʿAmr min al-shuʿarāʾ, p. 131—the poet is named ʿAmr ibn Aḥmar there, p. 130—al-Tibyān, 7/136; and Lisān al-ʿArab (roots d-ʿ-w and h-w-y).
notes.ar: البيت في مجاز القرآن 2/ 13، و "من اسمه عمرو من الشعراء" لمحمد بن داود الجراح ص 131 - والشاعر اسمه عمرو بن أحمر، على ما في هذا المصدر ص 130 - والتبيان 7/ 136، واللسان (د ع و)، (هـ و ى).

notes.en: In M and the sources documenting the report: “ahwā.” In this context, hawā and ahwā mean “he hastened.” See Sharḥ Dīwān Zuhayr, p. 242, and Lisān al-ʿArab (root h-w-y).
notes.ar: في م، ومصادر التخريج: "أهوى". وهوى وأهوى، في هذا السياق: أسرع. ينظر شرح ديوان زهير ص 242، واللسان (هـ و ى).

notes.en: Mishqaṣ is a long, narrow arrowhead. Saḥm ḥashr is an arrow whose feathers are evenly shaped; feather shaping means trimming their tips and cutting them into matching, rounded forms. Shabraqahā means “he tore it apart.” See Lisān al-ʿArab (roots sh-q-ṣ, ḥ-sh-r, q-dh-d, and “shabraq”).
notes.ar: المشقص: نصل السهم إذا كان طويلًا غير عريض. وسهمٌ حشرٌ: مستوى قُذَذ الرِّيش - وقدُّ الريش: قطع أطرافه وحَذفُه على نحو الحذو والتدوير والتسوية -. وشَبرقَها: مزَّقها. ينظر اللسان (ش ق ص)، (ح ش ر)، (ق ذ ذ)، "شبرق".

notes.en: Qird means something clumped together, one part piled atop another. The sense is that his enemy aimed an arrow at his eye and tore it apart, though the poet had intended that eye for kohl. See Lisān al-ʿArab (root q-r-d).
notes.ar: القرد: المتجمع الذي يركب بعضُه بعضًا. والمعنى أن عدوه صوب لعينه سهما فمزَّقها، وقد كان الشاعر يعُدُّها للكحل. ينظر اللسان (ق ر د).

notes.en: Its source documentation was given earlier, p. 538. Lisān al-ʿArab (root ʿ-n-q) says it describes a mountain: “There should be no plain or mountain above it more beautiful than it.” Khalqāʾ, as explained in Lisān al-ʿArab (root kh-l-q), means “the sky.”
notes.ar: تقدم تخريجه في ص 538. قال في اللسان (ع ن ق): يصف جبلًا، يقول: لا ينبغى أن يكون فوقها سهل ولا جبل أحسن منها. والخلقاء - كما في اللسان (خ ل ق) - هي السماء.

notes.en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq transmitted it in his Tafsīr, 2/14, through Mujāhid, with the wording “love.” Ibn Kathīr mentioned it in his Tafsīr (cited here as 5/26, apparently 5/264). Al-Suyūṭī attributed it in al-Durr al-manthūr, 4/287, to al-Firyābī and ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd.
notes.ar: أخرجه عبد الرزاق في تفسيره 2/ 14 من طريق مجاهد به، بلفظ محبة، وذكره ابن كثير في تفسيره 5/ 26، وعزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 4/ 287 للفريابي وعبد بن حميد.

notes.en: Ibn Kathīr mentioned it in his Tafsīr, 5/264, from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭalḥah, from Ibn ʿAbbās.
notes.ar: ذكره ابن كثير في تفسيره 5/ 264 عن علي بن أبي طلحة عن ابن عباس.

notes.en: Ibn Kathīr mentioned it in his Tafsīr, 5/264, from al-ʿAwfī, from Ibn ʿAbbās.
notes.ar: ذكره ابن كثير في تفسيره 5/ 264 عن العوفي عن ابن عباس.

notes.en: Al-Ṭūsī mentioned it in al-Tibyān, 7/137, with the wording “in this world.”
notes.ar: ذكره الطوسى في التبيان 7/ 137 بلفظ في الدنيا.

notes.en: Tafsīr Mujāhid, p. 459, through Warqāʾ. Al-Baghawī mentioned it in his Tafsīr, 5/257.
notes.ar: تفسير مجاهد ص 459 من طريق ورقاء به، وذكره البغوي في تفسيره 5/ 257.

notes.en: Ibn Kathīr mentioned it in his Tafsīr, 5/264, from Saʿīd, from Ibn ʿAbbās. Al-Suyūṭī attributed it in al-Durr al-manthūr, 4/287, to Ibn Abī Shaybah, Hannād, ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abī Ḥātim.
notes.ar: ذكره ابن كثير في تفسيره 5/ 264 عن سعيد عن ابن عباسٍ، وعزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 4/ 287 إلى ابن أبي شيبة وهناد وعبد بن حميد وابن المنذر وابن أبي حاتم.

notes.en: In Ṣ, T1, and F: “he added.”
notes.ar: في ص، ت 1، ف: "زاد".

notes.en: In Ṣ and F: “Ḥassān.” He is Hirm ibn Ḥayyān al-ʿAbdī, one of the younger Companions. See his entry in Usd al-ghābah, 5/391.
notes.ar: في ص، ف: "حسان". وهو هرم بن حيان العبدى، من صغار الصحابة، ترجمته في أسد الغابة 5/ 391.

notes.en: Al-Qurṭubī mentioned it in his Tafsīr, 11/161; Ibn Kathīr mentioned it in his Tafsīr, 5/294, from Qatādah.
notes.ar: ذكره القرطبي في تفسيره 11/ 161، وذكره ابن كثير في تفسيره 5/ 294 عن قتادة به.

notes.en: Ibn Kathīr mentioned it in his Tafsīr, 5/264, from Qatādah.
notes.ar: ذكره ابن كثير في تفسيره 5/ 264 عن قتادة به.

notes.en: Omitted from the manuscripts and Tafsīr al-Thawrī. The adopted wording is from Tafsīr ʿAbd al-Razzāq; it correctly appears in Tafsīr al-Thawrī, p. 135. He is ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muslim ibn Hurmuz al-Makkī; see Tahdhīb al-kamāl, 16/130.
notes.ar: سقط من: النسخ، وتفسير الثورى. والمثبت من تفسير عبد الرزاق، وقد جاء على الصواب في تفسير الثورى ص 135 وهو عبد الله بن مسلم بن هرمز المكي، مترجم في تهذيب الكمال 16/ 130.

notes.en: Omitted in T2.
notes.ar: سقط من: ت 2.

notes.en: Tafsīr al-Thawrī, p. 190, which reads “from Muslim”; this was explained in the preceding note. Tafsīr ʿAbd al-Razzāq, 2/14, cites al-Thawrī from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muslim.
notes.ar: تفسير الثورى ص 190 ووقع عنده "عن مسلم" وبينا ذلك في الحاشية السابقة، وتفسير عبد الرزاق 2/ 14 عن الثورى عن عبد الله بن مسلم به.

notes.en: Al-Qurṭubī mentioned a similar statement from Ibn ʿAbbās in his Tafsīr, 11/161. Abū Ḥayyān gave its sense in his Tafsīr, 6/221, but with the wording: “It is said that this verse was revealed about ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf …,” followed by the rest of his account. Al-Suyūṭī attributed it in al-Durr al-manthūr, 4/287, to the author, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Mardawayh, but named him “ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAwf.”
notes.ar: ذكره القرطبي في تفسيره 11/ 161 من قول ابن عباسٍ بنحوه، وذكره أبو حيان في تفسيره 6/ 221 بمعناه، لكن بلفظ: قيل نزلت هذه الآية في عبد الرحمن بن عوف .... إلى آخر ما ذكره. وعزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 4/ 287 إلى المصنف وابن المنذر وابن مردويه لكن سماه "عبد الله بن عوف".

notes.en: Tafsīr Mujāhid, p. 459, through Warqāʾ. Ibn Kathīr mentioned it in his Tafsīr, 5/265, from Ibn Abī Najīḥ. Al-Suyūṭī attributed it in al-Durr al-manthūr, 4/288, to ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abī Ḥātim.
notes.ar: تفسير مجاهد ص 459 من طريق ورقاء به، وذكره ابن كثير في تفسيره 5/ 265 عن ابن أبي نجيحٍ به، وعزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 4/ 288 إلى عبد بن حميد وابن المنذر وابن أبي حاتم.

notes.en: In T1 and F: “laddan.” Ibn Kathīr mentioned the report in his Tafsīr, 5/265, from al-ʿAwfī, from Ibn ʿAbbās. Al-Suyūṭī attributed it in al-Durr al-manthūr, 4/288, to the author. Ibn Kathīr and al-Suyūṭī read “wicked” instead.
notes.ar: في ت 1، ف: "لدا". والأثر ذكره ابن كثير في تفسيره 5/ 265 عن العوفي عن ابن عباسٍ، وعزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 4/ 288 إلى المصنف. وعند ابن كثير والسيوطي بلفظ: "فجارًا".

notes.en: In Ṣ, M, T1, and F: “argumentation.”
notes.ar: في ص، م، ت 1، ف: "جدالا".

notes.en: See the source documentation for the following report.
notes.ar: ينظر تخريج الأثر بعد التالى.

notes.en: Ibn Kathīr mentioned it in his Tafsīr, 5/265, from Layth—meaning Ibn Abī Sulaym.
notes.ar: ذكره ابن كثير في تفسيره 5/ 265 عن ليث - وهو ابن أبي سليم - به.

notes.en: In Ṣ, M, and F: “argumentation.”
notes.ar: في ص، م، ف: "جدالا".

notes.en: Tafsīr ʿAbd al-Razzāq, 2/14. ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd transmitted it, as cited in Fatḥ al-bārī, 13/181, through Maʿmar.
notes.ar: تفسير عبد الرزاق 2/ 14. وأخرجه عبد بن حميد كما في فتح الباري 13/ 181 من طريق معمر به.

notes.en: Omitted in T1.
notes.ar: سقط من: ت 1.

notes.en: Ṣ reads: “vehemently disputatious, very unjust”; T1: “vehemently disputatious, intense in argument”; T2: “vehemently disputatious, unjust”; F: “vehemently disputatious,” followed by an unclear word.
notes.ar: في ص: "اللدد الظلوم"، وفى ت 1: "اللدد شديد الخصومة"، وفى ت:2: "اللد الظلوم"، وفي ف: "اللدد" ثم كلمة غير واضحة.

notes.en: Ibn Kathīr mentioned it in his Tafsīr, 5/265.
notes.ar: ذكره ابن كثير في تفسيره 5/ 265.

notes.en: Al-Baghawī mentioned it in his Tafsīr, 5/258; Ibn Kathīr in his Tafsīr, 5/265; and al-Suyūṭī in al-Durr al-manthūr, 4/288, attributing it to Saʿīd ibn Manṣūr, ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abī Ḥātim. The last two cite it briefly as “deaf.”
notes.ar: ذكره البغوي في تفسيره 5/ 258، وابن كثير في تفسيره 5/ 265، والسيوطي في الدر المنثور 4/ 288، وعزاه إلى سعيد بن منصور وعبد بن حميد وابن المنذر وابن أبي حاتم. وجاء ذكره عند الأخيرين مختصرا بلفظ "صما".

notes.en: Ṣ, T1, and F read “Bashshār”; M reads “Sinān”; T2 reads “Sinān al-Qarrān.” He is Muḥammad ibn Sinān al-Qazzāz. Ibn Bashshār is Muḥammad ibn Bashshār, known as Bundār. The author narrates from both. See al-Ansāb, 4/491, and the entry for Abū ʿĀṣim al-Nabīl in Tahdhīb al-kamāl, 13/281.
notes.ar: في ص، ت 1، ف: "بشار"، وفى م: "سنان"، وفى ت 2: "سنان القران". وهو محمد بن سنان القزاز. أما ابن بشار فهو محمد بن بشار المعروف ببندار. وكلاهما يروى عنه المصنف. وينظر الأنساب 4/ 491، وترجمة أبي عاصم النبيل في تهذيب الكمال 13/ 281.

notes.en: Cited earlier, 3/578.
notes.ar: تقدم في 3/ 578.

notes.en: In Ṣ, M, T1, T2, and F: “they hasten.”
notes.ar: في ص، م، ت 1، ت 2، ف: "يعاجلوا".

notes.en: Ibn Kathīr mentioned it in his Tafsīr, 5/265. Al-Suyūṭī attributed it in al-Durr al-manthūr, 4/288, to Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abī Ḥātim.
notes.ar: ذكره ابن كثير في تفسيره 5/ 265، وعزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 4/ 288 إلى ابن المنذر وابن أبي حاتم.

notes.en: Tafsīr ʿAbd al-Razzāq, 2/14, from Maʿmar. Ibn Kathīr mentioned it in his Tafsīr, 5/265. Al-Suyūṭī attributed it in al-Durr al-manthūr, 4/288, to ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd.
notes.ar: تفسير عبد الرزاق 2/ 14 عن معمر به، وذكره ابن كثير في تفسيره 5/ 265، وعزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 4/ 288 إلى عبد بن حميد.

notes.en: Al-Ṭūsī mentioned it in al-Tibyān, 7/137, with the wording “al-rakz is a sound”; Ibn Kathīr gave the same wording in his Tafsīr, 5/265.
notes.ar: ذكره الطوسى في التبيان 7/ 137 بلفظ "الركز الصوت"، وابن كثير في تفسيره 5/ 265 بلفظه.

notes.en: Al-Ṭūsī mentioned it in al-Tibyān, 7/137, and Ibn Kathīr in his Tafsīr, 5/265.
notes.ar: ذكره الطوسى في التبيان 7/ 137، وابن كثير في تفسيره 5/ 265.

notes.en: Al-Ṭūsī mentioned it in al-Tibyān, 7/137, with the wording “it is sensation”; al-Qurṭubī in his Tafsīr, 11/162, has “a sensation”; and Ibn Kathīr in his Tafsīr, 5/265, has “a sound.”
notes.ar: ذكره الطوسى في التبيان 7/ 137 بلفظ "هو الحس"، والقرطبي في تفسيره 11/ 162 بلفظ "حسا"، وابن كثير في تفسيره 5/ 265 بلفظ صوتا.

notes.en: He is Labīd ibn Rabīʿah. His Dīwān, p. 311. The verse also appears in al-Tibyān, 7/138, and Tafsīr al-Qurṭubī, 11/162.
notes.ar: هو لبيد بن ربيعة، ديوانه ص 311. وجاء البيت في التبيان 7/ 138، وتفسير القرطبي 11/ 162.

notes.en: Ṣ, M, T1, T2, and F read “dhakara”; the Dīwān reads “rizz.” Rizz and rakz have the same meaning. See al-Wasīṭ (root r-z-z). The Dīwān’s editor notes that the verse is also transmitted with “rakz.” “Its familiar one is sick” means that it sensed people approaching to hunt it, hence the word “sick.”
notes.ar: في ص، م، ت 1، ت 2، ف: "ذكر"، وفى الديوان: "رِزّ". ورزّ وركز بمعنىً. ينظر الوسيط (رزز). وأشار محقق الديوان في تعقيباته على الأبيات أنه يروى أيضا "ركز". والمقصود بـ "الأنيس سقامها" أنها أحست باقتراب الناس يريدون صيدها، ولذا قال: "سقامها".
